M_5(\mathbb C)\oplus M_5(\mathbb C)
\oplus M_3(\mathbb C)\oplus \boxed{M_2(\mathbb C)}.
\]

It is the linking completion of the one-dimensional \(C\xrightarrow{e^c}E\) edge. Its Hermitian part is \(H_2(\mathbb C)\), and entrywise conjugation fixes exactly \(H_2(\mathbb R)\). The projection

\[
\mathbb E(A)=\frac12(A+\bar A)
\]

is positive and onto the complete \(H_2(\mathbb R)\) cone. For

\[
X=\begin{pmatrix}a&b\\b&d\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
t=\frac{a+d}{2},\quad x=\frac{a-d}{2},\quad y=b,
\]

one has

\[
\det X=t^2-x^2-y^2.
\]

Consequently the programme now has an exact internal algebraic chain

\[
\boxed{
M_{\rm SM}
\Longrightarrow
!\,M_2(\mathbb C)
\xrightarrow{\rm real\ form}
H_2(\mathbb R)
\Longrightarrow
Sp(4,\mathbb R)\cong Spin_0(2,3).
}
\]

The exclamation mark denotes uniqueness by simple-factor size, not a claim of physical inevitability.

The obstruction is equally exact. Hypercharge rotates the off-diagonal entry \(z\mapsto e^{i\theta}z\), so the fixed real slice survives only for \(\theta=0,\pi\). Selecting it before electroweak breaking would incorrectly reduce the continuous \(U(1)\) to \(\mathbb Z_2\).

The central frontier has therefore shifted. The question is no longer whether an \(H_2(\mathbb R)\) occurs inside the Furey-derived matter structure—it does, in a unique simple ideal. The remaining question is whether a neutral composite, covariant bundle or external lock transfers that Jordan structure into a gauge-invariant response carrier.

### 20.31 The charged real slice remains obstructed after Higgs breaking

The post-Higgs escape fails for a simple representation-theoretic reason. A charge-\(q\) complex line is a real rotation plane. For any real line direction \(v_\phi\),

\[
v_\phi\wedge R(q\theta)v_\phi=\sin(q\theta).
\]

If \(q\ne0\), no line is invariant under the full continuous \(U(1)\); its stabilizer is only \(q\theta\in\pi\mathbb Z\).

The off-diagonal relation in the unique \(M_2(\mathbb C)\) factor has \(Y=+1\) before electroweak breaking. Because it is weak-singlet \(e^c\)-like data, it has \(Q=+1\) afterward. The Higgs vacuum is electromagnetically neutral, so the surviving photon continues to rotate the line.

Therefore a literal fixed-real restriction

\[
M_2(\mathbb C)_{\rm sa}\supset H_2(\mathbb R)
\]

cannot be the gauge-invariant physical carrier of the charged edge, either before or after breaking. What survives is the algebraic selector: it identifies the unique rank-two complex linking ideal and the real Jordan form available inside it.

The physical bridge must now use one of three sharper mechanisms:

1. a neutral gauge-invariant composite or bilinear built from the charged edge and its Yukawa/Higgs partners;
2. a rotating real subbundle whose connection and holonomy are retained;
3. a distinct gauge-neutral external \(M_2\) factor locked to the unique internal ideal.

This is a narrowing, not a return to the original ambiguity.

### 20.32 The selected Yukawa triangle supplies a neutral \(H_2(\mathbb R)\) response

The gauge-neutral dressing route is unusually constrained. Among renormalizable one-scalar/two-Weyl monomials containing \(e^c\), the only Standard-Model singlet is

\[
Le^cH^\dagger,
\]

which is precisely the charged-lepton block cycle that selected the surviving matter topology.

Define two dressed chiral faces

\[
\chi_L=H^\dagger L,
\qquad
\chi_R=e^{c\dagger}.
\]

Both are weak singlets with \(Y=-1\). Therefore their response matrix

\[
G_{ij}=\langle\chi_i^\dagger\chi_j\rangle
\]

is gauge invariant entry by entry. For a positive Gram or Euclidean two-point functional,

\[
G=
\begin{pmatrix}
A&Z\\
\bar Z&D
\end{pmatrix}
\ge0.
\]

Its real response

\[
G_{\mathbb R}=
\begin{pmatrix}
A&\operatorname{Re}Z\\
\operatorname{Re}Z&D
\end{pmatrix}
\]

remains positive and obeys

\[
\det G_{\mathbb R}=t^2-x^2-y^2.
\]

For one generation the charged-lepton Yukawa phase can be removed by field rephasing, so taking the CP-even off-diagonal coordinate discards no physical one-generation phase.

This resolves the direct gauge obstruction at the level of neutral observables: the real operation is no longer imposed on a charged field but on its gauge-invariant two-face response. The remaining burden is genuinely field-theoretic—construct the Lorentz-covariant reflection-positive or spectral kernel and keep complex flavor CP data in a separate multiplicity factor.

### 20.33 The dressed response passes the reduced spectral-positivity gate

Let the CP-even spin-projected spectral residues be

\[
\rho_n=r_nr_n^T\ge0.
\]

Then

\[
C_E(q^2)=\sum_n\frac{\rho_n}{q^2+m_n^2}
\]

is an \(H_2(\mathbb R)_+\)-valued matrix Stieltjes function. Each one-particle residue has determinant zero and lies on a cone extreme ray; linearly independent residues produce an interior positive response.

The Lorentzian continuation

\[
R(z)=\sum_n\frac{\rho_n}{m_n^2-z}
\]

obeys

\[
\operatorname{Im}R(z)\ge0
\qquad(\operatorname{Im}z>0),
\]

so it is matrix Herglotz-positive. The positive-time kernel

\[
K_{ia,jb}=C_{E,ab}(t_i+t_j)
\]

factorizes into residue/exponential vectors and is a Gram matrix. This supplies reduced reflection positivity and connects directly with the previously derived positive rank-one boundary pole residues.

The word “reduced” matters: the full fermionic proof must restore spinor reflection matrices, Grassmann signs and contact terms.

### 20.34 Carrier reality need not erase flavor CP

The CP obstruction is avoided if the real operation is confined to the two-face carrier:

\[
\mathcal A_{\rm response}
=
H_2(\mathbb R)
\otimes_{\mathbb R}
\operatorname{Herm}_3(\mathbb C).
\]

Carrier transformations \(S\otimes I_3\) commute with flavor observables \(I_2\otimes H_f\). An explicit checkpoint with positive Hermitian \(H_u,H_d\) gives

\[
\det[H_u,H_d]=12i,
\qquad
\operatorname{tr}[H_u,H_d]^3=36i,
\]

while the carrier basis remains real.

Thus a real \(Spin(2,3)\)-linked response carrier is mathematically compatible with nonzero flavor CP. The earlier no-go continues to exclude a single antiunitary reality condition imposed on the flavor matrices themselves.

The physical requirement is now a commutant condition: the carrier action must remain in the commutant of the interacting flavor algebra under radiative closure. Exact tensor factorization is sufficient but not yet derived.

### 20.35 In the free Dirac checkpoint, mass is the Jordan relation

In a real fixed-helicity chiral basis, the free Dirac Hamiltonian is

\[
h(k)=k\sigma_z+m\sigma_x,
\qquad
h(k)^2=(k^2+m^2)I.
\]

Its positive-energy projector is

\[
P_+(k)=\frac12\left(I+\frac{h(k)}{\omega}\right),
\qquad
\omega=\sqrt{k^2+m^2}.
\]

This is a rank-one element of \(H_2(\mathbb R)_+\):

\[
P_+
=
\begin{pmatrix}
t+x&y\\
y&t-x
\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
t=\frac12,\quad
x=\frac{k}{2\omega},\quad
y=\frac{m}{2\omega},
\]

with

\[
t^2-x^2-y^2=0.
\]

The carrier interpretation is exact in this checkpoint: momentum/helicity sets the face imbalance, while the Dirac mass is the off-diagonal relation joining left and right chirality.

For positive Euclidean times, the reflected kernel

\[
K_{ia,jb}=e^{-\omega(t_i+t_j)}P_+(k)_{ab}
\]

factorizes as one outer product and is positive. This closes the free fixed-helicity fermionic Osterwalder–Schrader gate rather than relying only on scalar Gram analogy.

The remaining step is global and interacting: arbitrary momentum directions introduce spin-frame phases, and gauge transport may turn the real helicity basis into a nontrivial bundle with Berry/holonomy data.

### 20.36 The helicity state is Hopf-twisted—but its Jordan response descends

Over the momentum-direction sphere, positive helicity is not one globally trivial complex line. North and south eigenvectors satisfy

\[
u_N=e^{i\phi}u_S,
\]

so the clutching function winds once. With

\[
A_N=\frac{1-\cos\theta}{2}\,d\phi,
\qquad
A_S=-\frac{1+\cos\theta}{2}\,d\phi,
\]

the curvature is

\[
F=\frac12\sin\theta\,d\theta\wedge d\phi,
\qquad
\frac1{2\pi}\int_{S^2}F=1.
\]

Thus the helicity eigenvector in the preceding section cannot be promoted to one globally smooth basis. It was initially tempting to conclude that the external carrier must be refined from a single vector space to a bundle

\[
\mathcal J\longrightarrow S^2_{\hat{\mathbf p}}
\]

of local \(H_2(\mathbb R)\) response fibers with Berry transition data. The explicit descent calculation shows that this is too strong for the free response.

Indeed, with

\[
\Psi_\alpha=v\otimes u_\alpha,
\qquad
u_N=e^{i\phi}u_S,
\]

the phase cancels in

\[
\rho_\alpha=\Psi_\alpha\Psi_\alpha^\dagger,
\qquad
\rho_N=\rho_S.
\]

Tracing the spin factor yields

\[
\rho_{\rm chiral}
=\operatorname{Tr}_{\rm spin}\rho
=vv^T\in H_2(\mathbb R)_+,
\]

which is globally real. The nontrivial line bundle belongs to the helicity state, while the common-phase-neutral Jordan response descends to the base sphere.

On the equator,

\[
\oint A_N=\pi,
\qquad
\operatorname{Hol}=-1.
\]

This is a mathematically exact version of the programme’s “one twist” intuition at the **state-vector** level. It does not derive a three-strand braid or any Monster/Moonshine completion. Moreover, the sign is invisible in a density matrix, just as a central metaplectic sign is invisible in its projective action. Merely matching the two minus signs would therefore have no physical content.

Mass remains the local off-diagonal Jordan relation and does not change the helicity Chern class. The next global question is precise: can an interaction, unequal face transition or interference observable make Berry transport act nontrivially on the Jordan face relation while preserving the cone? Only then is a Hopf-to-symplectic/metaplectic lift physically testable.

See [Helicity, the Hopf bundle, and the global real-carrier obstruction](../0100-0199/122_helicity_hopf_bundle_real_carrier_obstruction.md).
The correction and descent calculation are in [Hopf phase descent and the carrier correction](../0100-0199/123_hopf_phase_descent_and_carrier_correction.md).

### 20.37 Continuous relative phase either trivializes or complexifies the carrier

The descent result can be classified completely for diagonal two-face patch actions. Let

\[
H=\begin{pmatrix}a&b\\b&c\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
D=\operatorname{diag}(e^{i\alpha},e^{i\beta}).
\]

Then

\[
DHD^\dagger
=
\begin{pmatrix}
a&be^{i(\alpha-\beta)}\\
be^{-i(\alpha-\beta)}&c
\end{pmatrix}.
\]

This remains in \(H_2(\mathbb R)\) exactly when

\[
\alpha-\beta=0\ \text{or}\ \pi\pmod{2\pi}.
\]

For a continuous \(U(1)\) with charges \(q_1,q_2\), preservation for every group parameter requires \(q_1=q_2\). The action is then a common phase and disappears from the response. If \(q_1\ne q_2\), positivity and determinant remain valid in \(H_2(\mathbb C)\), but the imaginary off-diagonal component becomes a new fourth real coordinate. The programme has then changed carrier and no longer has the same three-dimensional Lorentz cone.

Within the real carrier, the sole nontrivial diagonal relative action is the discrete reflection

\[
b\longmapsto-b.
\]

This creates a precise fork:

1. retain \(H_2(\mathbb R)\) and derive a dynamical relative \(\mathbb Z_2\) holonomy;
2. enlarge to \(H_2(\mathbb C)\) and rederive the symmetry target;
3. leave Berry phase on state/interference data and keep the Jordan density phase-neutral.

The current dressed faces have equal gauge quantum numbers, and their helicity phase is common, so the known free construction follows the third path. A future Hopf–metaplectic synthesis must not confuse the common central sign, which bilinears cannot see, with the relative face sign, which reverses the Jordan relation coordinate.

See [Two-face patch actions and the real-slice gate](../0100-0199/124_two_face_patch_actions_and_real_slice_gate.md).

### 20.38 The braid-center sign is not the relative Jordan sign

The two surviving signs have different \(Sp(4,\mathbb R)\) matrices. Under

\[
\iota(A)=
\begin{pmatrix}
A&0\\0&A^{-T}
\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
X\mapsto AXA^T,
\]

the braid center uses \(A=-I_2\):

\[
\iota(-I_2)=-I_4,
\qquad
(-I_2)X(-I_2)^T=X.
\]

It is common inversion and fixes the entire Jordan carrier.

The visible face reflection instead uses

\[
A_r=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1),
\qquad
\iota(A_r)=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1,1,-1),
\]

and sends

\[
\begin{pmatrix}a&b\\b&c\end{pmatrix}
\longmapsto
\begin{pmatrix}a&-b\\-b&c\end{pmatrix}.
\]

The latter endpoint is reached by a \(\pi\)-rotation of one canonical phase plane. Its metaplectic lift is single-mode parity times a path phase; the former lifts as total parity. They are not alternate descriptions of one operation.

This closes the most direct Hopf/braid shortcut. The central full twist can remain hidden from Jordan observables, but it cannot itself orient or reverse the off-diagonal relation. A successful synthesis must derive an additional selector that singles out one phase plane, or use an interference observable that detects the common central lift without pretending it acts on \(H_2(\mathbb R)\).

See [Common central sign versus relative face reflection](../0100-0199/125_common_central_sign_vs_relative_face_reflection.md).

### 20.39 Face–flavor entanglement is compatible with real marginal geometry and CP

Strict product factorization between face and flavor is not necessary. Take amplitude matrices

\[
V_u=
\begin{pmatrix}1&0&0\\0&2&0\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
V_d=
\begin{pmatrix}1&1&i\\1&i&1+i\end{pmatrix},
\]

and positive rank-one residues

\[
R_f=|\operatorname{vec}V_f\rangle
\langle\operatorname{vec}V_f|.
\]

Both state vectors have face–flavor Schmidt rank two. Nevertheless their face marginals are

\[
F_u=V_uV_u^\dagger=
\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&4\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
F_d=V_dV_d^\dagger=
\begin{pmatrix}3&2\\2&4\end{pmatrix},
\]

which lie strictly inside \(H_2(\mathbb R)_+\).

The flavor marginals \(H_f=V_f^\dagger V_f\) remain complex and give

\[
\det[H_u,H_d]=24i,
\qquad
\operatorname{tr}[H_u,H_d]^3=72i.
\]

Thus positivity, microscopic face–flavor entanglement, a real Jordan face marginal and nonzero flavor CP can coexist in one spectral model. The correct interacting gate is not exact factorization of every state. It is stability of the real partial-response subspace: gauge and radiative transport must not generate the missing imaginary \(\sigma_y\) face coordinate, while complex flavor orientation remains free.

See [Face–flavor entangled spectral CP checkpoint](../0100-0199/126_face_flavor_entangled_spectral_cp_checkpoint.md).

### 20.40 Real marginal closure is one condition, but positivity does not protect it

A general Hermitian perturbation on face times flavor has block form

\[
\delta R=
\begin{pmatrix}
A&C\\C^\dagger&B
\end{pmatrix},
\]

with \(A,B\in\operatorname{Herm}_3(\mathbb C)\) and \(C\in M_3(\mathbb C)\). Its face marginal is real exactly when

\[
\operatorname{Im}\operatorname{tr}C=0.
\]

Thus the safe perturbation space has real dimension \(35\) inside \(\operatorname{Herm}_6(\mathbb C)\), which has dimension \(36\). The forbidden marginal is only the flavor-singlet \(\sigma_y\otimes I_3\) coefficient; complex traceless flavor correlations can survive without appearing in the face partial trace.

This is encouragingly small but not automatic. Because the dressed faces carry equal gauge quantum numbers, common gauge transformations act trivially on every face bilinear and do not forbid \(\sigma_y\otimes I_3\).

Nor does spectral positivity suffice. For

\[
F(q^2)=\sum_n\frac{R_n}{q^2+m_n^2},
\qquad
(R_n)_{12}=c_n,
\]

one fixed face rephasing makes \(F_{12}(q^2)\) real for every momentum if and only if all distinct-pole coefficients \(c_n\) share a phase modulo \(\pi\). Positive residues can have unaligned phases and yield a positive response whose off-diagonal phase varies with momentum.

The external real-carrier claim has therefore reached its sharp dynamical gate:

\[
\boxed{
\text{derive common singlet spectral phase alignment}
\quad\text{or}\quad
\text{enlarge to }H_2(\mathbb C).
}
\]

The alignment may follow from a reflection identity, Ward identity, common real spurion or pole-by-pole spectral pairing. It cannot be inferred from gauge neutrality, positivity or a real choice at one momentum.

See [Real face-marginal perturbation classification](../0100-0199/127_real_face_marginal_perturbation_classification.md) and [Spectral phase alignment as the real-carrier gate](../0100-0199/128_spectral_phase_alignment_real_carrier_gate.md).

### 20.41 Failure of phase alignment restores the \(Spin(2,4)\) parent

The complex fallback has an exact geometric meaning. The real carrier

\[
\begin{pmatrix}t+z&x\\x&t-z\end{pmatrix}
\]

has determinant \(t^2-x^2-z^2\). Allowing the forbidden imaginary singlet response gives

\[
\begin{pmatrix}t+z&x-iy\\x+iy&t-z\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
\det=t^2-x^2-y^2-z^2.
\]

Thus \(y\) is an additional spacelike Jordan coordinate and

\[
H_2(\mathbb R)\subset H_2(\mathbb C)
\]

is exactly the slice \(y=0\).

The corresponding conformal groups are

\[
\operatorname{Conf}(H_2(\mathbb R))
\simeq Sp(4,\mathbb R)
\simeq Spin_0(2,3),
\]

\[
\operatorname{Conf}(H_2(\mathbb C))
\simeq SU(2,2)
\simeq Spin_0(2,4).
\]

At Lie-algebra level this is the already identified decomposition

\[
\mathfrak{so}(2,4)
=
\mathfrak{so}(2,3)\oplus\mathbf5.
\]

The single extra carrier coordinate restores five conformal orbit generators, not five carrier coordinates. This resolves a conceptual gap between the early selector branch and the later spectral response branch:

\[
\boxed{
\text{common spectral phase alignment}
\Longleftrightarrow
\text{preservation of the }Spin(2,3)\text{ real slice};
}
\]

\[
\boxed{
\text{irreducible phase misalignment}
\Longrightarrow
H_2(\mathbb C)\text{ and restoration of }Spin(2,4).
}
\]

This does not derive alignment. It identifies exactly what is at stake when alignment succeeds or fails.

See [The \(H_2(\mathbb C)\) fallback restores the \(Spin(2,4)\) parent](../0100-0199/129_h2c_fallback_restores_spin24_parent.md).

### 20.42 Two exact mechanisms can preserve the real slice

Let

\[
c_E=\langle\Omega|O_1P_EO_2|\Omega\rangle
\]

be a cross-face spectral residue. If an antiunitary \(\Theta\) fixes the vacuum, commutes with \(P_E\) and gives \(O_i\) parities \(\eta_i\), then

\[
c_E^*=\eta_1\eta_2c_E.
\]

All residues are therefore real for equal parity or purely imaginary for opposite parity. This aligns every pole and degenerate spectral subspace.

A weaker sufficient mechanism is one common connector:

\[
b_E=e^{-i\delta}\lambda_Ea_E,
\qquad
\lambda_E\in\mathbb R.
\]

Then

\[
c_E=e^{-i\delta}\lambda_E\|a_E\|^2,
\]

so all residues share one phase. The free Dirac checkpoint has this structure because one real mass spurion supplies the left/right relation.

Neither mechanism is yet established in the interacting three-generation theory. A full antiunitary flavor symmetry would kill the nonzero CP invariant, while loops may produce multiple independent cross-face spurions. The promising narrow possibility is a sector-limited reflection or unique flavor-singlet connector that aligns only the partial response and leaves traceless complex flavor data untouched.

See [Antiunitary and common-spurion criteria for spectral alignment](../0100-0199/130_antiunitary_and_common_spurion_alignment_criteria.md).

### 20.43 Flavor CP can source the missing carrier coordinate

The common-spurion hope faces a precise multigeneration counterterm. Define

\[
\mathcal J_{\rm CP}
=
\operatorname{Im}\operatorname{tr}[H_u,H_d]^3.
\]

It is a flavor-basis invariant and changes sign under complex conjugation. The missing carrier generator \(\sigma_y\) also changes sign. Hence

\[
\delta R
=
\kappa\mathcal J_{\rm CP}\,
\sigma_y\otimes I_3
\]

is invariant under their combined spurionic transformation.

It is Hermitian, gauge neutral and flavor singlet, while

\[
\operatorname{Tr}_{\rm flavor}\delta R
=
3\kappa\mathcal J_{\rm CP}\sigma_y
\]

is exactly the imaginary marginal that moves the response from \(H_2(\mathbb R)\) into \(H_2(\mathbb C)\).

This does not show that \(\kappa\) is generated. It shows that gauge symmetry, flavor covariance and ordinary CP-spurion bookkeeping do not forbid a pseudoscalar connector. The invariant is twelfth order in Yukawa spurions, so it may be extremely suppressed, but suppression is not exact selection.

The central programme has therefore reached a genuine stop-everything calculation:

\[
\boxed{
\text{Does }\kappa\text{ generate a spectral phase inequivalent to the scalar connector?}
}
\]

One constant scalar–pseudoscalar phase can be removed by a relative chiral rotation and merely rotates the selected real slice. The \(Spin(2,4)\) parent is restored only when no single anomaly-allowed rephasing realifies all poles or momentum-dependent form factors.

See [The Jarlskog-sourced \(\sigma_y\) counterterm gate](../0100-0199/131_jarlskog_sourced_sigma_y_counterterm_gate.md).

### 20.44 The dressed carrier is broken-phase normalized, and only phase misalignment is fatal

The original dressed faces have equal gauge charges but unequal engineering dimensions:

\[
[H^\dagger L]=\frac52,
\qquad
[e_R]=\frac32.
\]

A dimensionally homogeneous broken-phase pair is

\[
\widetilde\chi_L=\frac{\sqrt2}{v}H^\dagger L,
\qquad
\widetilde\chi_R=e_R.
\]

This correction makes explicit that the present carrier is a \(v\)-normalized, symmetry-broken construction. It does not extend smoothly to \(v=0\) without a different scale or operator definition.

The faces are also opposite Weyl chiralities. Their scalar \(2\times2\) response is meaningful only after a fixed-helicity/test-spinor projection or in the scalar/pseudoscalar part of a Dirac self-energy. In that language,

\[
m_s\sigma_x+m_p\sigma_y
\]

corresponds to

\[
m_s\bar\psi\psi+i m_p\bar\psi\gamma_5\psi.
\]

Lorentz covariance therefore permits \(\sigma_y\). But a relative chiral rephasing rotates \(m_s-im_p\) by one phase. A single constant Jarlskog-sourced pseudoscalar term can be absorbed into a rotated \(H_2(\mathbb R)\) slice, subject to anomaly constraints.

The actual parent-restoration criterion is unchanged and sharper:

\[
\boxed{
\frac{m_p(p^2)}{m_s(p^2)}
\text{ is not constant across the required spectral support}.
}
\]

Only then is no global real slice available.

See [Lorentz, dimension, and chiral-phase audit](../0100-0199/132_lorentz_dimension_and_chiral_phase_audit.md).

### 20.45 No canonical local polynomial symmetric-phase dressed pair

The \(v\)-normalized construction raises the question whether an equally canonical carrier exists before electroweak breaking.

Three direct options fail to supply one:

1. \((H^\dagger L)/\mu\) has the correct dimension and charge, but the external scale \(\mu\) is arbitrary. It rescales one face by a positive congruence, preserving the cone while changing physical response normalization.
2. \((H^\dagger L)/\sqrt{H^\dagger H}\) is dimensionally correct but nonpolynomial and singular at \(H=0\).
3. \(i\!\not\!D e_R\) has the correct dimension and Weyl index, but the charged-lepton equation of motion makes it proportional to the Yukawa-dressed left face rather than an independent relation.

There is no polynomial gauge-singlet scalar of dimension one in the minimal Standard Model. The first Higgs singlet \(H^\dagger H\) has dimension two.

The present conclusion is therefore structural:

\[
\boxed{
\text{the audited }H_2(\mathbb R)\text{ carrier is a broken-phase/emergent response}.
}
\]

A symmetric-phase version needs a scale selected by stress-energy, boundary conditions, a condensate, a nonlocal dressing, or new field content. This turns the earlier boundary/stress branches into possible normalization mechanisms rather than merely geometric analogies.

See [Symmetric-phase options for the dressed carrier](../0100-0199/133_symmetric_phase_dressed_carrier_options.md).

### 20.46 Boundary response can normalize the carrier—conditionally

Simple covariant stress roots do not supply a universal scale. Both

\[
|T^\mu{}_\mu|^{1/4}
\quad\text{and}\quad
|T_{\mu\nu}T^{\mu\nu}|^{1/8}
\]

vanish for null radiation, while

\[
(T_{\mu\nu}u^\mu u^\nu)^{1/4}
\]

requires an observer or a nondegenerate Landau frame.

The exact scalar boundary response performs better. Its even and odd eigenvalues obey

\[
\lambda_+=m\tanh\frac{mL}{2},
\qquad
\lambda_-=m\coth\frac{mL}{2},
\]

and therefore

\[
\boxed{
\sqrt{\det X_{m,L}}
=
\sqrt{\lambda_+\lambda_-}
=m.
}
\]

This is intrinsic to the independently derived positive response and independent of the interval length. It can normalize the dressed faces without choosing one face or parity channel.

The qualification is essential. At \(m=0\), \(\det X=0\), while the remaining odd eigenvalue \(2/L\) requires a length and sector choice. And if \(X\) is itself built from the already normalized dressed faces, the definition is circular.

The boundary branch now has a concrete conditional role: its normal selects \(H_2(\mathbb R)\), and a nondegenerate response determinant may select the dimension-one normalization.

See [Boundary and stress candidates for the carrier normalization scale](../0100-0199/134_boundary_and_stress_normalization_scale_audit.md).

### 20.47 The hidden metaplectic sign has a minimal interferometer

Consider the constant loop \(\gamma_0\) at \(I_4\) and a loop \(\gamma_1\) rotating one canonical plane through \(2\pi\). Both have the same endpoint and hence the same final Jordan relation. Their metaplectic lifts satisfy

\[
\widetilde\gamma_0(1)=+I,
\qquad
\widetilde\gamma_1(1)=-I.
\]

Prepare a coherent path state

\[
\frac{|0\rangle+|1\rangle}{\sqrt2}\otimes|\psi\rangle.
\]

After the two transports it becomes

\[
\frac{|0\rangle-|1\rangle}{\sqrt2}\otimes|\psi\rangle.
\]

Recombination therefore moves all probability from the \(+\) output to the \(-\) output. The sign is observable even though density matrices at either classical endpoint cannot see it.

For the braid branch, the squared center has identity endpoint and is the appropriate candidate loop. But the homomorphism supplies only that endpoint. A physical braid motion must still be shown to represent the odd element of \(\pi_1(Sp(4,\mathbb R))\) modulo two.

See [A minimal metaplectic loop interferometer](../0100-0199/135_minimal_metaplectic_loop_interferometer.md).

### 20.48 A rephasing-invariant form-factor wedge decides the real slice

After an admissible helicity or Euclidean spinor projection, the most general Hermitian face kernel is

\[
K(p)=tI+z\sigma_z+x\sigma_x+y\sigma_y.
\]

Its positivity condition is the \(H_2(\mathbb C)\) cone:

\[
t\ge0,
\qquad
t^2-x^2-y^2-z^2\ge0.
\]

The scalar and pseudoscalar connectors are \(x\) and \(y\). A common chiral rephasing rotates their plane, so neither \(y(p)\) nor the phase at one momentum is invariant.

For two spectral points define

\[
\boxed{
\mathcal W(p,q)
=
x(p)y(q)-y(p)x(q).
}
\]

This wedge is invariant under the common rotation. It vanishes for every pair exactly when all off-diagonal form-factor vectors are collinear, in which case one fixed chiral rotation selects an \(H_2(\mathbb R)\) hyperplane.

In Dirac notation,

\[
\mathcal W(p,q)
=
m_s(p^2)m_p(q^2)
-m_p(p^2)m_s(q^2).
\]

The decisive Standard-Model calculation is therefore no longer “is there a pseudoscalar term?” It is:

\[
\boxed{
\text{Does any physical pair satisfy }\mathcal W(p,q)\ne0?
}
\]

One nonzero value is immune to face redefinition and forces the complex carrier. Vanishing over complete spectral support is the exact phase-alignment statement needed by the \(Spin(2,3)\) branch.

See [Dirac form factors and the phase-wedge obstruction](../0100-0199/136_dirac_form_factor_wedge_obstruction.md).

### 20.49 Spectral discontinuities carry the decisive phase data

Write the complex cross form factor as

\[
M(q^2)=\int_0^\infty\frac{\rho(s)}{q^2+s}\,ds
\]

up to the required subtractions. The spectral real-slice condition is

\[
\mathcal W_\rho(s,t)
=
\operatorname{Im}
\bigl[\rho(s)\overline{\rho(t)}\bigr]
=0
\]

for every pair in the physical support.

A local momentum diagnostic is

\[
\Omega(q^2)
=
\operatorname{Im}
\left[
\overline{M(q^2)}
\frac{dM(q^2)}{dq^2}
\right].
\]

If \(M=|M|e^{i\theta}\), then

\[
\Omega=|M|^2\theta'.
\]

Hence a nonzero \(\Omega\) is a basis-independent signal that no constant chiral rotation maintains the real slice locally in momentum.

For the minimal ansatz

\[
m_s(r)=m(1+ar),
\qquad
m_p(r)=\mathcal J(b+cr),
\]

the obstruction is

\[
\mathcal W(p,q)
=
m\mathcal J(c-ab)(q-p).
\]

The unknown Standard-Model calculation has therefore been reduced to a precise question about absorptive discontinuities or the independent slope \(c-ab\). Spurion allowance alone cannot answer it.

See [Spectral wedge and phase curvature](../0100-0199/137_spectral_wedge_and_phase_curvature.md).

### 20.50 Arithmetic symmetry and connected symmetry must occupy different levels

For a full lattice \(\Lambda\subset V\), the exact automorphism group

\[
\operatorname{Aut}(\Lambda)\subset GL(V)
\]

is discrete. The continuous image of a connected group is connected. Therefore every continuous homomorphism

\[
Spin_0(2,3)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Aut}(\Lambda)
\]

is trivial.

The same argument applies immediately to the finite Monster:

\[
Spin_0(2,3)\longrightarrow\mathbb M
\]

has trivial image whenever the map is continuous.

This does not eliminate arithmetic or Moonshine from the programme. It fixes their possible roles:

\[
\text{integral admissibility}
\longrightarrow
\text{selected flag}
\longrightarrow
\text{real scalar extension and connected stabilizer},
\]

or else

\[
\text{local connected response symmetry}
\quad\text{and}\quad
\text{separate modular/VOA symmetry on global states}.
\]

It rules out the simpler claim that \(Spin(2,3)\) is directly a continuous subgroup or image inside the Monster or exact Leech automorphism group.

A valid Moonshine bridge must now exhibit a partition function, graded module, commutant or genus-two sewing law. A shared minus sign, dimension coincidence or octonionic ambient space is not enough.

See [Connected continuous symmetry versus arithmetic and Monster symmetry](../0100-0199/138_connected_continuous_vs_arithmetic_symmetry_separation.md).

### 20.51 The boundary normalization is exactly invariant under homogeneous gluing

For two homogeneous scalar segments,

\[
X_{m,L_1}\star X_{m,L_2}
=
X_{m,L_1+L_2},
\]

where \(\star\) denotes Schur-complement elimination of the shared boundary value.

Iteration gives

\[
X_{m,L_1}\star\cdots\star X_{m,L_n}
=
X_{m,\sum_iL_i}.
\]

Consequently,

\[
\boxed{
\sqrt{\det X}=m
}
\]

at every intermediate and final stage, regardless of the subdivision lengths.

This removes a major ambiguity from the boundary-scale proposal: refining the interface description does not change the normalization. The result depends on one homogeneous bulk fluctuation operator. If adjacent masses differ, the sewn determinant is generally neither input mass squared, so heterogeneous or interacting systems need a generalized transfer invariant.

The remaining physical question is not internal consistency but origin: can an independently selected boundary sector couple this scale to the dressed Standard-Model carrier without circularity?

See [Dirichlet-to-Neumann determinant scale under arbitrary gluing](../0100-0199/139_dtn_determinant_scale_under_gluing.md).

### 20.52 The braid image has exact finite congruence shadows

Reducing the established \(SL(2,\mathbb Z)\) braid matrices modulo \(p\) gives full images

\[
\rho_p(B_3)=SL(2,\mathbb F_p)
\]

for the explicitly enumerated primes \(p=2,3,5\), with orders

\[
6,\quad24,\quad120.
\]

The central full twist maps to \(-I\). In characteristic two the sign disappears because \(-I=I\); at odd primes it survives as the nontrivial central element.

Projectivization yields

\[
PSL(2,2)\cong S_3,
\qquad
PSL(2,3)\cong A_4,
\qquad
PSL(2,5)\cong A_5.
\]

These are genuine finite arithmetic shadows of the braid branch. They do not select three generations, a flavor group or a Monster module. Physical content requires an independently selected modulus and an action on actual states.

See [Congruence reductions of the braid image](../0100-0199/140_braid_congruence_reductions_and_finite_shadows.md).

### 20.53 Heterogeneous boundaries make normalization nonunique

For a piecewise free interface, let

\[
T_{\rm tot}
=
\begin{pmatrix}a&b\\c&d\end{pmatrix}
\in SL(2,\mathbb R).
\]

The boundary response has

\[
\det X=\frac cb,
\]

giving

\[
\mu_{\det}=\sqrt{\frac cb}.
\]

The same transfer matrix has an effective decay exponent

\[
\mu_{\rm F}
=
\frac1{L_{\rm tot}}
\operatorname{arcosh}
\left(\frac{\operatorname{tr}T_{\rm tot}}2\right).
\]

Both are invariant under subdivision of the same physical profile. For a homogeneous bulk they coincide with \(m\). For heterogeneous masses they generally differ.

Thus the exact homogeneous normalization survives refinement but not uniqueness under heterogeneous generalization. Direct boundary-Hessian coupling favors \(\mu_{\det}\); asymptotic decay favors \(\mu_{\rm F}\). The physical definition of the dressed carrier must state which operation it measures.

See [Heterogeneous boundary transfer scales](../0100-0199/141_heterogeneous_boundary_transfer_scales.md).

### 20.54 Arithmetic selection can coexist with continuous symmetry after scalar extension

The connected/discrete no-go does not forbid one integral object from having different groups of points over different scalars.

In the exact toy model,

\[
J_{\mathbb Z}=\operatorname{Sym}_2(\mathbb Z)
\]

contains the primitive rank-one flag generated by \(E_{11}\). The congruence transformations

\[
g_b=
\begin{pmatrix}1&b\\0&1\end{pmatrix}
\]

fix that flag.

For

\[
b\in\mathbb Z,
\]

they preserve the integral order and form a discrete arithmetic subgroup. After scalar extension to

\[
J_{\mathbb R}=\operatorname{Sym}_2(\mathbb R),
\]

the same formula with

\[
b\in\mathbb R
\]

gives a connected real stabilizer.

The viable exceptional architecture is therefore:

\[
(J_{\mathbb Z},F_{\mathbb Z})
\longrightarrow
(J_{\mathbb R},F_{\mathbb R}),
\]

with arithmetic orbits selecting admissible flags and the real identity component supplying the continuous local symmetry.

The unresolved calculation is specific: construct primitive integral versions of the nested \(H_2(\mathbb C)\subset H_3(\mathbb C)\subset H_3(\mathbb O)\) flag inside a chosen exceptional order, then compare its integral stabilizer and real identity component with Leech data and the faithful Standard-Model group.

See [Integral flag selection and continuous stabilizer after scalar extension](../0100-0199/142_integral_flag_and_real_stabilizer_architecture.md).

### 20.55 A Planck-scale pixel can justify continuum approximation—but not exact symmetry

For the central-difference Laplacian,

\[
\widehat k_a^2
=
\frac4{a^2}\sum_i\sin^2\frac{ak_i}{2},
\]

and

\[
0
\le
|k|^2-\widehat k_a^2
\le
\frac{a^2}{12}|k|^4
\]

in the low-momentum regime. The relative free dispersion error is bounded by

\[
\frac{(a|k|)^2}{12}.
\]

If \(a\) is assumed to be the Planck length, ordinary sub-Planckian free propagation can therefore be extraordinarily close to the continuum.

But the correction contains \(\sum_i k_i^4\), exposing lattice-axis anisotropy. Small error does not prove exact Lorentz symmetry, and scalar convergence does not solve lattice chirality, gauge invariance or anomaly matching.

See [A quantified discrete-to-continuum error budget](../0100-0199/143_discrete_continuum_error_budget.md).

### 20.56 Null cell links are exact in \(1+1\), not a derivation of Game of Life

With

\[
\Delta t=\frac ac,
\qquad
\Delta x=\pm a,
\]

nearest-neighbor links satisfy

\[
ds^2=-c^2\Delta t^2+\Delta x^2=0.
\]

The Courant-one update

\[
\phi_{t+1,n}
=
\phi_{t,n-1}
+\phi_{t,n+1}
-\phi_{t-1,n}
\]

propagates arbitrary left- and right-moving profiles exactly:

\[
\phi_{t,n}=f(n-t)+g(n+t).
\]

This makes the “cell-to-cell communication along \(ds^2=0\)” intuition mathematically exact in \(1+1\) dimensions.

For the standard Cartesian stencil in \(d>1\), stability requires \(c\Delta t/a\le1/\sqrt d\), so axis links cannot simultaneously be null. A different causal graph or quantum walk is required.

Bounded local dependence explains why cellular automata have causal cones. It does not single out Conway’s birth/death rule or provide quantum, gauge and fermionic structure.

See [Null links, cell-to-cell communication, and cellular causality](../0100-0199/144_null_links_and_cellular_causality.md).

### 20.57 Higher-dimensional null directions expose a speed–isotropy tradeoff

The failure of null *axis* links in the standard Cartesian stencil does not imply that higher-dimensional null cellular geometry is impossible. Take all body-diagonal directions

\[
n_\epsilon=\frac1{\sqrt d}(\epsilon_1,\ldots,\epsilon_d),
\qquad \epsilon_i=\pm1,
\]

and stream a distance \(c\Delta t\,n_\epsilon\). Every link is exactly null. The complete symmetric set also obeys

\[
\langle n_i n_j\rangle=\frac{\delta_{ij}}d,
\]

so it is isotropic at second order. But the most direct scalar average produces a continuum spatial coefficient \(1/d\), hence

\[
c_{\rm eff}=\frac c{\sqrt d}.
\]

Multiplying the stencil by \(d\) restores the infrared speed while destabilizing high lattice momenta for \(d>1\), and fourth moments remain direction dependent. The constructive path is therefore a multicomponent null-streaming system with a local unitary coin or collision operator. That operator must earn the scalar, spinorial, chiral and gauge sectors rather than assume them.

See [Higher-dimensional null directions and the isotropy tradeoff](../0100-0199/145_higher_dimensional_null_direction_tradeoff.md).

### 20.58 A discrete Standard Model must pass the fermion-doubling gate

The symmetric lattice derivative has momentum symbol

\[
\widehat D_i(k)=\frac{\sin(ak_i)}a.
\]

It vanishes at every corner with \(ak_i\in\{0,\pi\}\), giving \(2^d\) zeros and sixteen in four Euclidean dimensions. A Wilson term

\[
M_W(k)=\frac ra\sum_i(1-\cos ak_i)
\]

lifts every corner except the origin in the free calculation, at the price of breaking naive chiral symmetry at finite spacing.

This creates a strict interface between the discrete and Furey branches. The anomaly-free ternary matter sectors identify admissible representation content, but they do not construct a local chiral regulator. Any cellular completion must specify its Wilson, staggered, domain-wall, overlap/Ginsparg–Wilson or genuinely new mechanism; count its poles and index; reproduce anomaly cancellation; and show that mirror matter does not return. \(Spin_0(2,3)\) organizes the proposed response carrier but, by itself, does not change the topology of the lattice Dirac symbol.

See [The lattice-fermion doubling gate](../0100-0199/146_lattice_fermion_doubling_gate.md).

### 20.59 A unitary null-streaming coin produces Dirac kinematics but retains a Floquet partner

The minimal two-face construction is explicit in (1+1) dimensions. Let the two components stream in opposite directions on exact null links and mix locally through a symmetric coin:

\[
U(k)=e^{-im\sigma_x/2}e^{-ik\sigma_z}e^{-im\sigma_x/2}.
\]

The update is exactly unitary, obeys \(\sigma_yU\sigma_y=U^\dagger\), and has spectrum

\[
\cos\omega=\cos k\cos m.
\]

Near (k=m=0), its generator is (k\sigma_z+m\sigma_x), giving the Dirac dispersion \(\omega^2=k^2+m^2+cdots\). Its group velocity never exceeds the microscopic null-link speed. Thus the internal coin is enough to convert two causal directional carriers into a relativistic spinor prototype.

The global spectrum supplies the caution. At (m=0) there is a cone at ((k,\omega)=(0,0)) and another at ((\pi,\pi)). Discrete time does not present the partner as a second zero of the same static operator; it moves it to the edge of the periodic quasienergy zone. Gauge interactions and anomalies must nevertheless account for it. The exact construction therefore advances the causal branch while sharpening, rather than bypassing, the mirror-sector question.

See [A minimal null-streaming Dirac quantum walk](../0100-0199/147_null_streaming_dirac_quantum_walk.md).

### 20.60 Gauge covariance forces a Higgs-dressed relation between unequal faces

Place an oriented phase (L_n=e^{iA_n}) on each null link. With

\[
L_n\mapsto g_{n+1}L_ng_n^{-1},
\]

the right- and left-moving conditional shifts are exactly locally (U(1))-covariant and unitary. If the two faces carry the same charge, their local mixing coin is also covariant. This gives a complete vectorlike charged walk.

The chiral case is more informative. For

\[
G_n=\operatorname{diag}(e^{iq_R\alpha_n},e^{iq_L\alpha_n}),
\]

the separate massless shifts remain covariant, but a fixed off-diagonal coin fails whenever (q_R\ne q_L). Covariance is restored by

\[
C(m,\theta)=
\begin{pmatrix}
\cos m&-i\sin m\,e^{i\theta}\\
-i\sin m\,e^{-i\theta}&\cos m
\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
\theta\mapsto\theta+(q_R-q_L)\alpha.
\]

The local relation mixing the faces must itself carry their charge difference. This is precisely the representation-theoretic job of a Higgs/Yukawa insertion. Consequently the earlier nonuniqueness of Furey Higgs-like block maps is no longer merely a static inventory problem: it becomes a nonuniqueness among admissible microscopic coins. A successful common selector must choose the coin, its normalization and its action on the quasienergy-\(\pi\) sector.

See [Gauge covariance of the null walk and the Higgs-coin necessity](../0100-0199/148_gauge_covariant_null_walk_higgs_coin.md).

### 20.61 The mixing relation is a compact-group intertwiner

For arbitrary compact (G), a fixed face-mixing block (M:V_R\to V_L) is gauge invariant exactly when

\[
M\in\operatorname{Hom}_G(V_R,V_L).
\]

Schur's lemma therefore kills a bare coin between inequivalent irreducible chiral modules. A field-valued block instead transforms as

\[
\Phi\mapsto\rho_L(g)\Phi\rho_R(g)^{-1},
\]

so the Hermitian off-diagonal generator built from \(\Phi\) and \(\Phi^\dagger\) exponentiates to a unitary covariant coin.

Applying this to one Standard-Model generation reproduces the exact Higgs pattern: charged leptons and down quarks require (H), while up quarks and an optional Dirac neutrino require \(\widetilde H\). The result makes contact with the Furey cyclic topology, where distinct oriented Higgs block components close the up/lepton and down chains. It does not yet lock those components, fix Yukawa matrices or derive the cyclic rule. The physical synthesis requires the Jordan/Furey selector to reduce the entire covariant intertwiner space to a distinguished normalized coin orbit.

See [The compact-group coin intertwiner theorem](../0100-0199/149_compact_group_coin_intertwiner_theorem.md).

### 20.62 One surviving Furey topology becomes a rank-seven Higgs coin

Choose the cyclically surviving internal arrows

\[
Q:H\to O_2,quad u^c:O_2\to C,quad d^c:O_2\to O_1,quad L:R\to H,quad e^c:C\to R.
\]

Their three charged cycles close through (h_C), (h_D^\dagger) and (h_C^\dagger). After making the conventional—but not yet internally derived—conversion from left-handed conjugate sectors to (u_R,d_R,e_R), the walk faces are

\[
V_L=Q\oplus L,qquad \dim V_L=8,
\]

\[
V_R=u_R\oplus d_R\oplus e_R,qquad \dim V_R=7.
\]

The broken-phase field-valued coin is an (8\times7) block with (y_uI_3), (y_dI_3), (y_e), and one zero row. At generic nonzero charged Yukawas its rank is seven, so the unmatched state is exactly the minimal left-handed neutrino. The Hermitian coin generator on (V_L\oplus V_R) has paired eigenvalues \(\pm|y_u|\), \(\pm|y_d|\), \(\pm|y_e|\) with color multiplicities and one zero.

This is a genuine three-branch interface: Furey fixes directed incidence, the Standard Model identifies chiral modules, and the walk turns the allowed incidence into unitary dynamics. The missing bridge is equally explicit: neither the TRO nor the external Jordan carrier has yet derived the antilinear particle-conjugation map used to form (V_R), distinguished the (O_1/R) pair, or fixed the Yukawa singular values.

See [Translating a surviving Furey TRO into walk-coin support](../0100-0199/150_furey_tro_to_walk_coin_translation.md).

### 20.63 Dagger closure does not by itself restore physical mirror fermions

The walk translation exposes a necessary correction to the earlier block-language interpretation. Algebraically,

\[
X_{ab}\mapsto X_{ab}^\dagger
\]

reverses every off-diagonal Furey arrow, and no inner block-sign grading separates the two orientations. Those exact results remain valid. Physically, however, the dagger of a left-handed Weyl field is its right-handed adjoint operator in the Hermitian action. It is not automatically a second independent left-handed field in the conjugate representation.

This distinction is visible in anomalies. One independent (U(1)) Weyl field of charge (q) contributes (q^3); its adjoint in the kinetic term supplies no separate \((-q)^3\). A genuinely independent left-handed mirror does supply that term and makes the pair vectorlike. Likewise the fifteen independent left-handed fields of one Standard-Model generation cancel their anomalies without being doubled to thirty by Hermitian conjugation.

The correct unresolved question is therefore not whether the full algebra contains reverse blocks—it must—but how they are quantized. They may be adjoint operators, independent mirrors or constrained Nambu partners. Settling that requires the antiunitary real structure, independent Grassmann generators, Fock assignment and anomaly functional of both zero- and \(\pi\)-quasienergy sectors.

See [Dagger closure: antiparticles are not automatically mirror fermions](../0100-0199/151_dagger_antiparticle_vs_mirror_distinction.md).

### 20.64 The minimal walk's π cone is an independent Fock sector

For the symmetric null walk,

\[
U(k+\pi)=-U(k),
\qquad JUJ=-U,
\]

where (J=(-1)^n) is lattice staggering. This produces exact spectral pairing between zero- and π-quasienergy neighborhoods. It does not identify them. On an even periodic lattice the Fourier modes (k) and (k+\pi) are orthogonal, so second quantization assigns them distinct canonical anticommutation generators.

The Fock lift satisfies

\[
\Gamma(-U)|_{\mathcal F_p}=(-1)^p\Gamma(U)|_{\mathcal F_p}.
\]

Thus paired evolutions differ only by fermion parity within a fixed particle-number sector, but the underlying modes remain independent. Keeping one staggering eigenspace fails because one time step exchanges the two sublattices; passing to two steps merely folds π back to zero. Identifying the two cones by charge conjugation would impose a Majorana/Nambu constraint and cannot be applied to generic charged quarks or leptons.

This settles the minimal model negatively: its π cone is a duplicate species, not merely the adjoint of the zero cone. The broader branch remains open because a different split-step, higher-dimensional or anomalous Floquet walk may gap or reorganize that sector while preserving gauge covariance.

See [Second quantization of the null walk: Floquet-π sector independence](../0100-0199/152_floquet_pi_sector_fock_independence.md).

### 20.65 Split stepping gaps the π copy but weakens the all-null ontology

The π duplicate is forced by the minimal walk's bipartite relation, not by every finite-range unitary. For

\[
U_{\rm ss}(k)=S_+(k)C(θ_2)S_-(k)C(θ_1),
\]

the exact dispersion is

\[
\cos ω=\cos k\cos θ_1\cos θ_2-\sin θ_1\sin θ_2.
\]

Consequently the zero gap is controlled by (θ_1+θ_2), while the π gap is controlled by (θ_1-θ_2). Choosing (θ_1=-θ_2=θ\) leaves one massless infrared cone with velocity \(|\cos θ|\) but opens a π gap (2|θ|\). A small nonzero angle sum gives the infrared cone a mass without closing the π gap.

This is a real advance over the single-shift model: local discrete-time unitarity can avoid its exact duplicate. It also exposes a foundational tradeoff. During each partial shift one component moves while the other remains stationary. Finite propagation speed and gaugeable locality survive, but not the stronger literal claim that every elementary dependency is a null link. Moreover the relative angle is an unexplained regulator parameter unless another branch derives it.

The programme must now decide whether (ds^2=0) describes the outer causal bound or every microscopic relation. Requiring the latter may reinstate doubling; accepting timelike local mixing permits independent Floquet-gap control.

See [Split-step walk: independent zero/π gap control and the null-link tradeoff](../0100-0199/153_split_step_walk_zero_pi_gap_tradeoff.md).

### 20.66 Gauge covariance survives split stepping only when both coin events are dressed

The split-step deformation admits exact spatial gauge coupling:

\[
U_{\rm ss}=S_+[A]C_2[\Phi_2]S_-[A]C_1[\Phi_1].
\]

Each partial shift carries the oriented link transporter appropriate to its moving face. For unequal left/right charges, each local coin must independently transform as a field-valued intertwiner. Dressing (C_1) while leaving (C_2) fixed fails gauge covariance; dressing both restores it exactly and preserves norm.

This yields a tempting but unproved comparison with Furey: the walk has two ordered Higgs-coin events, while the cyclic matter topology requires two oriented Higgs block components. Their common cardinality is not a bridge. The former are separated in update order; the latter are distinguished by internal endpoints. A genuine synthesis must supply an equivariant map between those structures and fix the relative coin angle that controls the π gap.

There is also a temporal qualification. The exact certificate allows one site-dependent gauge transformation common to all factors inside a clock tick. If partial shifts occupy separate physical sub-times, temporal link variables are required between them. Treating the factorization as instantaneous is consistent but further weakens the literal microscopic-spacetime reading.

See [Gauge-covariant split stepping requires two dressed coin events](../0100-0199/154_gauge_covariant_split_step_two_higgs_coins.md).

### 20.67 Full substep gauge covariance makes timelike transport unavoidable

Allow the gauge frame to vary independently across the four operator factors of a split step. Spatial links alone cannot compare states at successive sub-times. Introduce temporal phases with

\[
B_{s,n}\mapsto B_{s,n}+α_{s+1,n}-α_{s,n}.
\]

Together with the spatial link and Higgs-intertwiner laws, these temporal transporters give exact covariance from the initial to the final slice. Omitting them fails explicitly.

The geometric consequence is unambiguous. A temporal link has \(Δx=0\) and positive \(Δt\), hence it is timelike. For this route, three desirable properties cannot presently be held simultaneously:

\[
\text{independent π-gap control}
+\text{substep-resolved local gauge covariance}
+\text{every elementary edge null}.
\]

The first two are explicitly realized; the third is not. The strict all-null ontology is therefore pinned for this model. A more defensible surviving claim is that the microscopic graph is causal and non-spacelike: propagation may occupy null edges, while local mixing and gauge-frame transport occupy timelike edges inside the cone.

Alternatively, the split factors may be treated as an instantaneous decomposition of one integer-time event. That avoids physical intermediate slices but also makes the full product, rather than its apparent shifts, ontologically elementary.

See [Full substep gauge covariance forces temporal links](../0100-0199/155_spacetime_gauge_split_step_temporal_links.md).

### 20.68 Eliminating a finite walk interior produces a positive (H_2(\mathbb R)) response

For a finite real orthogonal walk (U), choose (0<r<1) and form

\[
H=(I-rU)^T(I-rU)>0.
\]

Retain the two inward boundary ports and eliminate every internal amplitude. The Schur complement

\[
X=H_{bb}-H_{bi}H_{ii}^{-1}H_{ib}
\]

is a positive real symmetric (2\times2) matrix, hence

\[
X\in H_2(\mathbb R)_+.
\]

Successive elimination in any order gives exactly the same (X), providing a finite sewing law. This is the first discrete construction in the programme where the proposed Jordan carrier emerges directly from a walk interior rather than being assigned in advance.

The result is not yet a derivation of (Spin(2,3)). Any positive real quadratic system compressed to two ports has the same cone. The physical boundary transformations have not been shown to generate the full (Sp(4,\mathbb R)) conformal group, and the Euclideanization, reflection rule and port normalization remain selected by hand.

See [A finite walk produces a positive two-port (H_2(\mathbb R)) response](../0100-0199/156_walk_two_port_h2r_boundary_response.md).

### 20.69 The boundary determinant invariant fails under heterogeneous coins

Uniform-coin data initially produced the exact-looking relation

\[
\det X=(1-r^2)^2
\]

for every tested length and angle. Heterogeneous site coins break it. Alternative port orientations break it, and a common boundary-coordinate rescaling (b\mapsto sb) changes the determinant by (s^{-4}).

The correct conclusion is therefore narrower. The homogeneous reflecting walk appears to carry a transfer invariant worthy of analytic proof, but the generic discrete response has no universal determinant scale. This exactly parallels the heterogeneous scalar boundary branch: sewing is exact, while operational normalization remains nonunique.

The result is valuable because it blocks an attractive overclaim. The walk genuinely produces the Jordan cone, but it has not selected a canonical point, scale or full conformal symmetry on that cone.

See [The walk-response determinant is homogeneous, not universal](../0100-0199/157_walk_response_determinant_homogeneity_obstruction.md).

### 20.70 A passive positive response gives a semigroup, not automatically \(Sp(4,\mathbb R)\)

The conformal action on a symmetric response is

\[
X\mapsto(AX+B)(CX+D)^{-1},
\qquad
\begin{pmatrix}A&B\\C&D\end{pmatrix}
\in Sp(4,\mathbb R).
\]

Its ten infinitesimal directions split as

\[
4\;\text{congruences}
+3\;\text{upper translations}
+3\;\text{lower directions}.
\]

The walk presently realizes the positive cone, boundary-basis congruences and passive additions \(X\mapsto X+B\) with \(B\ge0\). These operations preserve positivity, but the additions form a semigroup because their inverses need not. The Fourier/Legendre element acts as \(X\mapsto-X^{-1}\) and also leaves the real positive cone.

Thus the full \(Sp(4,\mathbb R)\) is naturally the conformal completion of \(H_2(\mathbb R)\), not yet the verified physical symmetry of the passive walk. To make it dynamical, the programme must derive signed boundary translations, a canonical response/impedance duality and the lower-shear operations on a domain where composition remains meaningful—most plausibly the compactified Jordan algebra or a causal Siegel domain.

This sharpens the central claim: the walk has produced the carrier on which \(Spin_0(2,3)\) can act, but not yet the physical availability of every such action.

See [Boundary response operations and the gap to full \(Sp(4,\mathbb R)\)](../0100-0199/158_boundary_response_operations_and_sp4_gap.md).

### 20.71 A walk resolvent reaches the Siegel domain preserved by the full symplectic group

The real-cone obstruction is resolved at the level of causal analytic response. From a real orthogonal walk define

\[
K=\frac{U+U^T}{2}
\]

and compress its resolvent to the two boundary ports:

\[
Z(ζ)=P^T(K-ζI)^{-1}P,
\qquad \operatorname{Im}ζ>0.
\]

Then \(Z=Z^T\) and

\[
\operatorname{Im}Z
=(\operatorname{Im}ζ)
P^T\left((K-\operatorname{Re}ζ)^2+(\operatorname{Im}ζ)^2I\right)^{-1}P
>0.
\]

Thus \(Z\) lies in the genus-two Siegel upper half-space, and the full fractional \(Sp(4,\mathbb R)\) action preserves the domain. This gives the \(Spin_0(2,3)\) pole a concrete interpretation as the conformal geometry of a two-channel causal response, rather than merely the abstract conformal group of a real Jordan cone.

The construction is not yet unique or dynamically complete. \(K=(U+U^T)/2\) records \(\cos ω\) and identifies opposite quasienergy orientations. It may erase precisely the band orientation needed for chirality and Floquet anomaly accounting. Moreover domain covariance does not prove that the microscopic walk realizes every symplectic generator as a physical operation.

See [A walk resolvent reaches the Siegel \(Sp(4)\) domain](../0100-0199/159_walk_siegel_resolvent_and_sp4_domain.md).

### 20.72 Orientation-complete response restores the \(Spin(2,4)\) parent

The symmetric walk variable uses the even map \(ω\mapsto\cos ω\). To retain quasienergy orientation, use the Cayley chart

\[
H_C=i(I+U)(I-U)^{-1},
\qquad
e^{-iω}\mapsto\cot(ω/2).
\]

Its compressed retarded resolvent has positive Hermitian imaginary part. For generic oriented link or substep phases it is not transpose-symmetric. The natural causal carrier is then \(H_2(\mathbb C)\), whose conformal tube-domain group is

\[
SU(2,2)\simeq Spin_0(2,4).
\]

Imposing the compatible reciprocity/real condition restricts the response to complex symmetric matrices over \(H_2(\mathbb R)\), with

\[
Sp(4,\mathbb R)\simeq Spin_0(2,3).
\]

This gives the \(15=10+5\) descent a concrete response interpretation. The missing parent coordinate is not merely an abstract imaginary matrix entry; it carries oriented causal phase information. The selector could therefore be reciprocity or an antiunitary real structure.

The danger is equally concrete. If the selector simply replaces (U) by its cosine, it obtains the real slice by forgetting \(ω\leftrightarrow-ω\), potentially erasing chirality or Floquet anomaly data. A viable synthesis must keep the external two-port response reciprocal while storing orientation in the Furey, flavor or Fock factor. The Cayley chart also requires a quasienergy-origin choice at eigenvalue one, while the logarithmic chart trades that pole for a branch cut at π.

See [Orientation-complete walk response restores the \(Spin(2,4)\) parent](../0100-0199/160_orientation_complete_response_restores_spin24_parent.md).

### 20.73 Antiunitary reciprocity identifies the five broken conformal directions

On the Hermitian parent carrier,

\[
X=tI+xσ_x+yσ_y+zσ_z,
\]

entrywise antiunitary conjugation gives

\[
κ(X)=tI+xσ_x-yσ_y+zσ_z.
\]

Its fixed algebra is exactly (H_2(\mathbb R)\). On the causal tube, the equivalent response condition is transpose reciprocity. Every parent response decomposes as

\[
Z=\frac{Z+Z^T}{2}+\frac{Z-Z^T}{2}.
\]

The first term lies in the symmetric Siegel domain and retains positive imaginary part; the second is one complex orientation coordinate. Discarding it is lossy, while retaining it in an auxiliary factor permits exact reconstruction.

The (15=10+5) conformal descent also becomes explicit in the Jordan three-grading. The removed directions are

\[
1\ \text{translation}
+3\ \text{structure/Lorentz mixings}
+1\ \text{special conformal direction}.
\]

This makes reciprocity a mathematically complete selector candidate. The remaining physics is factorization: it must fix the external two-port response without imposing reality on the complex flavor and Fock data that carry CP violation and chirality. The correct target is therefore a tensor antiunitary

\[
Θ=κ_{\rm external}\otimes Θ_{\rm internal},
\]

not a global complex-conjugation constraint on the entire Standard Model.

See [Antiunitary reciprocity selects \(Spin(2,3)\) and the five broken directions](../0100-0199/161_antiunitary_reciprocity_selector_and_five_directions.md).

### 20.74 The two surviving Furey topologies form an antiunitary exchange pair

The anomaly- and cycle-surviving matter TROs are exchanged exactly by

\[
O_1\leftrightarrow R.
\]

Their common \(Q,u^c\) arrows remain fixed, while the \(d^c,L,e^c\) endpoints and all three Yukawa cycles are exchanged. Dagger is not this operation: it reverses arrows and maps neither survivor to the other.

On the direct sum of the two supports, define

\[
Θ_{\rm ex}(v_A,v_B)
=(\overline{v_B},\overline{v_A}).
\]

The fixed space has real dimension thirty—the same as one complex fifteen-dimensional generation. Thus the exchange presentation need not double independent matter. It also relates a complex coefficient to its conjugate rather than requiring the coefficient to be real.

This supplies a concrete candidate for the internal factor of

\[
Θ=κ_{\rm external}\otimes Θ_{\rm ex,internal}.
\]

The caveat is fundamental: \(O_1\leftrightarrow R\) is presently established only as a symmetry of the surviving support diagrams. Unless it extends to the nested algebra, gauge generators and cyclic action, the antiunitary is a reconstruction rather than a source-derived selector.

See [The two surviving Furey TROs form an antiunitary exchange pair](../0100-0199/162_furey_survivor_exchange_antiunitary_candidate.md).

### 20.75 The native real form forbids the neutral swap; the completed carrier restores it noncanonically

Furey's source construction now decides one of the programme's longest-lived ambiguities. The native algebra is

\[
\mathcal A=\mathbb O\oplus\mathbb H\oplus\mathbb C\oplus\mathbb R
\]

with componentwise multiplication. Its summands are two-sided ideals of distinct real dimensions \(8,4,2,1\). Hence every real-algebra automorphism preserves each summand setwise. The block \(O_1\) is a complex line selected inside the octonionic summand, while \(R\) is the terminal one-real-dimensional ideal. No real-algebra automorphism or anti-automorphism can exchange them.

The reduced centralizer records the same mismatch:

\[
\Delta_{\rm SM}
=\mathbb C_{\mathbb O}\oplus M_3(\mathbb C)_{\mathbb O}
\oplus M_2(\mathbb C)_{\mathbb H}\oplus\mathbb C_{\mathbb C}
\oplus\mathbb R_{\mathbb R}.
\]

The two proposed neutral factors have different real dimensions and different anti-Hermitian parts. This falsifies the strong claim that the incidence exchange was already hidden as a symmetry of the native nested algebra.

The weaker construction survives. The fifteen-real-dimensional source space embeds into a sixteen-real-dimensional carrier \(\mathbb V\), and a global complex structure turns the terminal real coordinate together with the complementary direction into a complex line. On that completed carrier, \(O_1\) and \(R\) are isomorphic gauge-trivial complex modules and their permutation is exact. Because the source embedding is only linear, not multiplicative, this is an emergent carrier symmetry rather than a source-algebra symmetry.

This creates a clean fork: preserve native provenance and select one TRO, promote the completed carrier and explain why provenance is redundant, or retain the exchange and break it by a vacuum/boundary orientation.

See [The Furey neutral exchange fails at the native real algebra but survives on the completed complex carrier](../0100-0199/163_furey_real_form_obstruction_and_complex_carrier_escape.md).

### 20.76 Exchange-paired flavor data makes CP violation an orientation variable

For three families let

\[
H_u=Y_uY_u^\dagger,
\qquad
H_d=Y_dY_d^\dagger,
\qquad
\mathcal J_{\det}=\operatorname{Im}\det[H_u,H_d].
\]

The exchange antiunitary sends \((Y_u,Y_d)\) to \((\overline Y_u,\overline Y_d)\), and therefore

\[
\mathcal J_{\det}\longmapsto-\mathcal J_{\det}.
\]

This does not force \(\mathcal J_{\det}\) to vanish within either oriented sector. An exact positive-matrix example gives

\[
\mathcal J_A=1080,
\qquad
\mathcal J_B=-1080.
\]

What vanishes is the unoriented equal-sector sum. Thus the antiunitary can coexist with observed flavor CP only if the second TRO is the adjoint/antiparticle presentation rather than an independent mirror, or if a vacuum/boundary condition selects an orientation.

The external response supplies a strikingly parallel odd variable: entrywise conjugation reverses the \(\sigma_y\) component discarded by the reciprocal \(H_2(\mathbb R)\) slice. Hence a symmetry-allowed bridge has the schematic parity

\[
\chi_{\rm orient}\,\mathcal J_{\det},
\qquad
\chi_{\rm orient}\mapsto-\chi_{\rm orient}.
\]

Both factors are odd and their product is even. This is not yet a derived interaction, but it turns the vague idea that complex flavor may source an oriented external carrier into a precise operator-class target.

See [Exchange-paired Yukawas preserve local CP phase but cancel unoriented CP-odd observables](../0100-0199/164_exchange_paired_yukawas_and_cp_orientation_gate.md).

### 20.77 Real dimension matching does not make the survivor pair a CAR adjoint pair

The exchange-fixed space has the real dimension of one complex generation, but gauge equivariance blocks the simplest Fock interpretation. For a hypercharge-\(y\) state and anti-linear \(J\),

\[
J e^{iy\theta}=e^{-iy\theta}J.
\]

If the target support carries the same charge \(y\), commuting with the ordinary gauge action would require \(e^{-iy\theta}=e^{iy\theta}\) for every \(\theta\), hence \(y=0\). All five matter sectors in each survivor have nonzero hypercharge, and the neutral-label exchange preserves rather than reverses those charges.

A self-dual CAR construction instead needs

\[
K\oplus\overline K,
\qquad
U(g)=\rho(g)\oplus\overline{\rho(g)},
\]

so the second Nambu half carries the conjugate gauge representation. The two Furey survivors carry \(R_{\rm SM}\oplus R_{\rm SM}\) at the block level, not \(R_{\rm SM}\oplus\overline{R_{\rm SM}}\). Declaring one support conjugate repairs the CAR algebra but adds a polarization not supplied by the neutral incidence.

There is a second repair. The same-charge antiunitary can cover the outer charge-conjugation automorphism

\[
(g_3,g_2,e^{i\theta})
\mapsto
(\overline g_3,\overline g_2,e^{-i\theta}).
\]

Then it is a CP-like twisted symmetry. It does not commute with each local gauge transformation and is not the adjoint operation itself. This sharpens the programme's decision: derive a conjugate Nambu action and Lorentz chirality map from the full endomorphic model, treat the pair as a CP-related doublet requiring orientation selection, or preserve the native real form and retain only one TRO.

See [The survivor exchange is not by itself a gauge-equivariant CAR adjoint](../0100-0199/165_exchange_fixed_car_gauge_equivariance_obstruction.md).

### 20.78 Furey's older complex conjugation supplies the missing Nambu operation

The CAR obstruction does not end the route. In Furey's complex-quaternionic basis, the source conjugation \(i\mapsto-i\) maps a left-handed Weyl ideal to its right-handed conjugate; the basis itself absorbs the usual \(-i\sigma_y\) matrix. In the complex-octonionic ladder system the same conjugation exchanges the two minimal ideals and reverses color representation and electric charge.

Thus the older construction contains

\[
C_F:
(\tfrac12,0;R_y)
\longmapsto
(0,\tfrac12;\overline R_{-y}),
\qquad C_F^2=1.
\]

This is the missing self-dual CAR transformation type. It is independent of the neutral permutation \(s:O_1\leftrightarrow R\). On a common completed carrier one may conditionally form

\[
\Gamma=sC_F.
\]

The remaining problem is no longer “find an antiunitary.” It is to construct an equivariant isometry between the 2016 tensor-product ideals and the 2026 five-block endomorphism carrier. Without that intertwiner, \(sC_F\) combines correct operations from different algebraic models rather than deriving them from one object.

See [Furey complex conjugation supplies the Nambu map—but not the neutral exchange](../0100-0199/166_furey_complex_conjugation_repairs_nambu_but_not_neutral_exchange.md).

### 20.79 Ternary closure uniquely completes the matter TRO with a neutrino arrow

After electroweak breaking, the 2016 ideal pair and the 2026 matter TRO have identical charged representation content. The older module has exactly one additional neutral singlet. Testing every canonical neutral block-singlet direction against ternary closure produces the decisive table

\[
\begin{array}{c|ccccccc}
x&p_{O_1}&p_{O_2}&p_H&p_C&p_R&D\to E&E\to D\\ \hline
\dim\operatorname{TRO}(M+\mathbb Cx)
&17&28&22&20&18&16&23.
\end{array}
\]

Only

\[
\nu^c:D\to E
\]

is a genuine one-state extension. It also closes

\[
H\xrightarrow{h_D}D
\xrightarrow{\nu^c}E
\xrightarrow{L}H,
\]

the missing cyclic neutrino Yukawa interaction. The previously rectangular \(8\times7\) Higgs coin becomes an \(8\times8\) potentially full-rank coin after the standard conversion to \(\nu_R\).

The result comes with a structural price. The fifteen-state linking algebra

\[
M_5\oplus M_5\oplus M_3\oplus M_2
\]

becomes

\[
M_5\oplus M_5\oplus M_3\oplus M_3.
\]

The unique \(M_2(\mathbb C)\) factor—and therefore the simplest internally selected \(H_2(\mathbb R)\) carrier—disappears. The programme now has a concrete neutrino/geometry fork: a fifteen-state branch with a unique capacity-two factor and non-Dirac neutrino mechanism, or a sixteen-state branch with a square Dirac coin requiring a new selector for an \(H_2\) corner inside \(M_3\).

See [A unique right-handed-neutrino TRO completion—and its Spin(2,3) tradeoff](../0100-0199/167_unique_right_handed_neutrino_tro_completion_and_spin23_tradeoff.md).

### 20.80 The neutrino completion restores \(H_2(\mathbb R)\) as a gauge-neutral Peirce corner

The disappearance of the unique \(M_2\) simple factor does not eliminate capacity two. The new \(M_3\) linking component has basis

\[
(E;C,D),
\]

where \(C\to E\) is the charged-lepton arrow and \(D\to E\) is the new neutral-neutrino arrow. It contains two canonical principal corners:

\[
p_eM_3p_e\cong M_2(\mathbb C),
\qquad p_e=p_E+p_C,
\]

and

\[
p_\nu M_3p_\nu\cong M_2(\mathbb C),
\qquad p_\nu=p_E+p_D.
\]

Hypercharge acts on \((E,C,D)\) with weights \((0,1,0)\). Hence the neutrino corner is the unique endpoint-selected corner with equal, trivial gauge weights on both faces. Its entrywise-real Hermitian subspace is a gauge-invariant

\[
H_2(\mathbb R),
\]

with determinant \(t^2-x^2-y^2\) and conformal group \(Sp(4,\mathbb R)\cong Spin_0(2,3)\). This removes the hypercharge obstruction that afflicted the old charged-lepton real slice.

The revised bridge is therefore

\[
\mathcal M_{15}
\to
\mathcal M_{16}
\to
M_3(E;C,D)
\to
p_\nu M_3p_\nu
\to
H_2(\mathbb R)
\to
Spin_0(2,3).
\]

The price is no longer arbitrariness of the corner: incidence and gauge neutrality select it. The price is dynamical isolation. Generic \(M_3\) operations mix the common face \(E\) with the charged direction \(C\), so a boundary response, superselection rule or Schur elimination must justify the compression \(X\mapsto p_\nu Xp_\nu\).

See [The neutrino Peirce corner restores a gauge-neutral \(H_2(\mathbb R)\) carrier](../0100-0199/168_neutrino_peirce_corner_restores_gauge_neutral_h2r.md).

### 20.81 Charged-channel elimination gives the same positive response functor as the walk

On the decomposition \((E,D)\oplus C\), let a positive quadratic kernel be

\[
K=\begin{pmatrix}A&b\\b^\dagger&c\end{pmatrix},
\qquad c>0.
\]

Eliminating the charged channel gives

\[
R_\nu=A-bc^{-1}b^\dagger\ge0.
\]

This response is exactly gauge invariant: hypercharge changes \(b\) only by a common phase. It also obeys

\[
\det K=c\det R_\nu
\]

and the associative Schur-composition law. If the microscopic kernel is reciprocal, \(R_\nu\in H_2(\mathbb R)\); otherwise its entrywise-real projection remains positive.

The scalar-network, finite-walk and internal-neutrino branches have therefore converged on one exact operation:

\[
\text{positive larger kernel}
\xrightarrow{\text{eliminate internal channels}}
\text{positive two-face response}.
\]

This is a genuine structural synthesis. What remains conditional is the physical input that the Furey action supplies a positive causal kernel and makes \(C\) internal while \(D,E\) are accessible boundary variables.

See [Charged-channel Schur elimination produces the neutral \(H_2\) response](../0100-0199/169_charged_channel_schur_elimination_to_neutrino_h2_response.md).

### 20.82 The exchanged neutrino arrows close the only quadratic neutral cycle

The two survivor completions contain

\[
n_A:O_1\to R,
\qquad
n_B:R\to O_1.
\]

Individually \(n_A^2=n_B^2=0\), but together their two cyclic products have nonzero trace. The exchange-fixed Hermitian combination

\[
N(m)=mn_A+\bar m n_B
\]

satisfies

\[
N(m)^2=|m|^2(p_{O_1}+p_R)
\]

and has spectrum \(\pm|m|\). This provides the exact block support for a neutral quadratic mass. If the reverse arrow is the CAR conjugate of the first, it is a Majorana channel; if both are independent, it is a Dirac mixing of two sterile Weyl fields.

The gauge-singlet addition changes no anomaly. Together with the cyclic \(L\nu^ch_D\) interaction, it makes a type-I seesaw representation-theoretically possible. The mass scale and the CAR identification remain undetermined.

The same two-face operator lies in the neutral \(H_2\) carrier: \(\operatorname{Re}m\) occupies its reciprocal off-diagonal coordinate and \(\operatorname{Im}m\) the orientation-odd \(\sigma_y\) direction. This makes a sterile-neutrino phase a concrete candidate source for response orientation.

See [The exchange-paired neutrino arrows form a quadratic cycle](../0100-0199/170_exchange_paired_neutrino_two_cycle_and_majorana_gate.md).

### 20.83 The fermion action and the positive Jordan response are different layers

The neutral support admits the standard one-family Weyl mass action

\[
\mathcal L_m=-\frac12(\nu,N)
\begin{pmatrix}0&m_D\\m_D&M_R\end{pmatrix}
\binom{\nu}{N}+\text{h.c.}
\]

The signed mass matrix has determinant \(-m_D^2\) and is indefinite. This is not a ghost: Grassmann integration is controlled by a determinant or Pfaffian, and physical Majorana masses are Takagi singular values. They satisfy

\[
m_lm_h=m_D^2,
\qquad m_h-m_l=M_R.
\]

Consequently the mass matrix itself must not be identified with \(H_2(\mathbb R)_+\). Positivity belongs to \(D^\dagger D\), Euclidean covariances, spectral densities or current responses. The safe chain is

\[
\text{Fock action}
\to
\text{positive spectral/observable kernel}
\to
H_2(\mathbb R).
\]

This distinction preserves chirality and phase information that would be lost by replacing the fermion operator with its square too early.

See [Neutral Fock action: seesaw support is real, but positive response is a different kernel](../0100-0199/171_neutral_fock_action_and_positive_response_separation.md).

### 20.84 Seesaw mixing turns boundary rays into an interior Lorentz-cone response

Each fixed-helicity mass eigenmode has positive-energy residue

\[
P_i(k)=\frac12\left(I+\frac{k\sigma_z+m_i\sigma_x}{\sqrt{k^2+m_i^2}}\right)
\in H_2(\mathbb R)_+,
\]

with determinant zero. The active-neutrino residue is a convex mixture

\[
R_{\rm act}=wP_l+(1-w)P_h.
\]

Its determinant is

\[
\det R_{\rm act}
=\frac{w(1-w)}2
\left(1-\mathbf n_l\cdot\mathbf n_h\right).
\]

For distinct masses, nonzero momentum and nontrivial mixing this is strictly positive. Unresolved mixing therefore carries a boundary ray into the interior of the Lorentz cone. The determinant measures spectral multiplicity/coarse-graining rather than a fundamental loss of unitarity.

The corresponding Euclidean time kernel is a positive sum of pole Gram kernels. This gives the neutral Jordan carrier a legitimate free Fock/spectral origin while keeping the raw Majorana matrix outside the positive cone.

See [Seesaw spectral mixing moves the neutral response into the interior of \(H_2(\mathbb R)_+\)](../0100-0199/172_seesaw_spectral_mixture_enters_h2r_interior.md).

### 20.85 Electromagnetic superselection makes the neutral corner a physical direct summand

In the ordered linking basis \((E,C,D)\), electromagnetic charge is \((0,1,0)\). A vacuum two-point kernel satisfying

\[
U(\theta)KU(\theta)^\dagger=K
\]

for all \(\theta\) must have the form

\[
K=
\begin{pmatrix}
a&0&z\\
0&c&0\\
\bar z&0&d
\end{pmatrix}.
\]

Hence

\[
\operatorname{Comm}_{M_3}(U(1)_Q)
\cong M_2(\mathbb C)_{E,D}\oplus\mathbb C_C.
\]

The neutrino projection is central in the gauge-invariant response algebra. Charged loops can renormalize the neutral block but cannot generate linear neutral--charged mixing while electromagnetism is unbroken. The earlier non-ideal leakage concern applies to generic linking operators, not physical invariant vacuum kernels.

Gauge symmetry therefore performs the first selection,

\[
M_3\longrightarrow M_2(\mathbb C)_{E,D}\oplus\mathbb C_C,
\]

while reciprocity performs the second,

\[
H_2(\mathbb C)_{E,D}\longrightarrow H_2(\mathbb R)_{E,D}.
\]

See [Electromagnetic superselection protects the neutrino \(H_2\) corner](../0100-0199/173_electromagnetic_superselection_protects_neutrino_h2_corner.md).

### 20.86 Three-flavor PMNS complexity coexists with an exactly real face carrier

For neutrino mass eigenstate \(i\), let \(P_i\in H_2(\mathbb R)_+\) be its fixed-helicity face residue and \(u_i\) the corresponding complex PMNS column. The full spectral carrier is

\[
\mathcal R=\sum_i P_i\otimes u_i u_i^\dagger\ge0.
\]

Every term is a rank-one Gram operator. Complex Dirac CP phases reside in the flavor projectors, while the face matrices remain real symmetric. Hence external reciprocity can act only on the face factor without projecting the PMNS algebra to a real form.

The carrier is not generally a simple tensor product. Distinct masses give different coefficients of \(I,\sigma_x,\sigma_z\), and the operator-Schmidt rank is generically three. Face and flavor are correlated rather than either independent or fused.

Majorana column phases cancel from \(u_i u_i^\dagger\), so they do not populate a free face \(\sigma_y\) coordinate. They survive in the anomalous tensor

\[
\mathcal M_{\alpha\beta}=\sum_i m_iU_{\alpha i}U_{\beta i}.
\]

Therefore the proposed Majorana-phase/orientation bridge, if real, must pass through a lepton-number-violating anomalous correlator or interaction. Ordinary oscillation spectral density cannot provide it.

See [Three-flavor spectral carrier: real faces, complex PMNS data, no naive factorization](../0100-0199/174_three_flavor_real_face_complex_pmns_spectral_carrier.md).

### 20.87 Majorana Nambu data do not canonically orient the external face

Writing the complex symmetric Majorana tensor as \(\mathcal M=A+iB\), with \(A\) and \(B\) Hermitian, gives the Nambu block

\[
H_N=\sigma_z\otimes\xi I+\sigma_x\otimes A-\sigma_y\otimes B.
\]

This makes a nonzero face \(\sigma_y\) coefficient visible in a chosen flavor basis, but it does not make it invariant. Takagi factorization gives a unitary \(U\) with

\[
U^T\mathcal M U=D,\qquad D\geq0,
\]

and the corresponding raw \(\sigma_y\) coefficient is zero in the mass basis. The coefficient therefore cannot be the missing canonical orientation of the external \(H_2(\mathbb R)\) carrier.

The surviving information is relational. In the charged-lepton mass frame, quantities such as

\[
I_{\alpha\beta}=\operatorname{Im}\!\left[
M_{\alpha\alpha}M_{\beta\beta}(M_{\alpha\beta}^{*})^2
\right]
\]

are invariant under the residual flavor rephasings and can detect Majorana-type CP structure. A possible portal has the schematic form \(\chi_{\rm ext}I_{\alpha\beta}\), where \(\chi_{\rm ext}\) is odd under external face exchange. This is a symmetry-compatible target, not a derivation: its fully weak-basis-invariant form, operator dimension, coefficient and radiative closure remain open.

See [Majorana Nambu \(\sigma_y\) is not a basis-invariant orientation](../0100-0199/175_majorana_nambu_sigma_y_is_not_a_basis_invariant_orientation.md).

### 20.88 The first explicit \(3+1\)-dimensional all-body-diagonal Weyl test

The ordered conditional-shift walk

\[
U(\mathbf k)=e^{-ik_z\sigma_z}e^{-ik_y\sigma_y}e^{-ik_x\sigma_x}
\]
