is exactly unitary and has eight one-tick body-diagonal dependencies. At small momentum it yields the Weyl generator \(\boldsymbol\sigma\cdot\mathbf p\). It therefore realizes the programme's carrier/relation intuition in three spatial dimensions without scalar averaging.

The same construction exposes two non-negotiable costs. First, if the body-diagonal edges of length \(\sqrt3a\) are null, then \(\Delta t=\sqrt3a/c\) and the emergent Weyl speed is \(c/\sqrt3\). Choosing the timestep that gives Weyl speed \(c\) makes those dependencies spacelike. Second, the eight Brillouin corners split into four zero- and four \(\pi\)-quasienergy species. The construction is a Weyl prototype, not yet a chiral Standard-Model regulator.

This produces a clean fork: either a larger all-null unitary must gap the duplicates while preserving gauge anomaly flow, or the ontology must admit timelike substeps/boundaries, or the observed metric must be universally emergent with \(c_{\rm observed}=c_{\rm micro}/\sqrt3\). Species-dependent cones would falsify the latter path.

See [Eight-body-diagonal Weyl walk and the null-speed gate](../0100-0199/176_eight_body_diagonal_weyl_walk_and_null_speed_gate.md).

### 20.89 Odd support parity forces zero/\(\pi\) pairing

The eight-cone duplication is not peculiar to the ordered Pauli walk. Any translation-invariant kernel supported on the body diagonals has

\[
U(\mathbf k)=\sum_{\epsilon\in\{\pm1\}^3}A_\epsilon e^{-i\mathbf k\cdot\epsilon}
\]

and hence

\[
U(\mathbf k+\pi e_j)=-U(\mathbf k).
\]

This identity is independent of the dimension and values of the matrices \(A_\epsilon\). Every zero-gap closing is therefore replicated at four zero and four \(\pi\) momenta. For the explicit Weyl walk, the global \(SU(2)\) Bloch-map degrees are \(+1\) at the zero corners and \(-1\) at the \(\pi\) corners, so the total degree vanishes.

The result pins the simplest all-null repair: a larger coin on the same eight edges cannot independently gap the duplicate sector. At least one structural premise must change. A concrete surviving option is the cubically symmetric, mixed-parity null shell formed from permutations and signs of \((1,2,2)\). Its 24 vectors all have length three but do not share a common sign under coordinate \(\pi\)-shifts. Whether they admit a unitary single-Weyl walk is now a sharply posed algebraic problem.

See [Body-diagonal parity theorem and Floquet chirality balance](../0100-0199/177_body_diagonal_parity_theorem_and_floquet_chirality_balance.md).

### 20.90 A parity-mixed all-null shell cancels anisotropy through fourth order

The first parity-mixed escape, the 24 signed permutations of \((1,2,2)\), has common length three but cannot propagate along a coordinate axis faster than \(2c/3\) under null timing. The same integer sphere also contains the six axis vectors \((\pm3,0,0)\) and permutations. Their union is a 30-link, equal-length, cubically symmetric null shell with both axis-speed support and mixed displacement parity.

Each of the two cubic orbits is isotropic at second order. Requiring the spherical fourth moments fixes their total weights uniquely:

\[
w_{\rm axis}=\frac{13}{40},
\qquad
w_{(1,2,2)}=\frac{27}{40}.
\]

With these weights,

\[
\langle n_i n_j n_k n_l\rangle
=\frac{
\delta_{ij}\delta_{kl}+\delta_{ik}\delta_{jl}+\delta_{il}\delta_{jk}
}{15}.
\]

The finite shell therefore cancels directional errors through fourth moment order while retaining exact null links. It is not continuously isotropic: the sixth moment is \(4/27\) rather than the spherical \(1/7\). More importantly, positive quadrature weights are not unitary quantum amplitudes. The next hard gate is solving the matrix autocorrelation equations for a Weyl carrier on this support.

This is also the first discrete branch result that gives the arithmetic programme a non-metaphorical target. An independent integral/Jordan/code construction would have to select the radius-three shell and its \(13:27\) orbit ratio. Until such a derivation exists, the numbers come only from moment matching.

See [Weighted 30-link null shell with fourth-order isotropy](../0100-0199/178_weighted_30_link_null_shell_fourth_order_isotropy.md).

### 20.91 The natural two-component amplitudes fail

Exact unitarity for a finite shell is equivalent to matrix autocorrelation equations at every displacement difference. On the 30-link shell, the only differences represented by a single ordered pair are the antipodal ones. They force

\[
A_e^\dagger A_{-e}=0,
\qquad
A_eA_{-e}^\dagger=0.
\]

If both amplitudes are nonzero and two-dimensional, each is rank one and their input and output lines are complementary. This makes the direction-aligned helicity assignment \(A_e\propto P_{\hat e}\) the obvious first ansatz.

It fails exactly. With arbitrary complex orbit coefficients \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\), cubic cancellation gives

\[
U(0)=(3\alpha+12\beta)I,
\qquad
U(\pi,0,0)=(\alpha+4\beta)I,
\]

so \(U(0)=3U(\pi,0,0)\). Both matrices cannot be unitary. The fourth-order isotropic scalar weights therefore cannot simply be promoted to square roots of helicity-projector amplitudes.

This does not close the 30-link branch. The mixed cubic orbit has enough freedom to support spin lines not parallel to displacement, and input and output textures need not coincide. Those skew textures are now the remaining two-component problem. If they fail, the programme must identify a principled carrier enlargement rather than adding components only to gain parameters.

See [Thirty-link unitarity reduction and helicity-ansatz no-go](../0100-0199/179_30_link_unitarity_reduction_and_helicity_ansatz_no_go.md).

### 20.92 The complete ordinary-cubic skew family is numerically obstructed

After antipodal rank-one reduction and proper-cubic covariance, the all-nonzero two-component family has only four real variables: a normalized orbit-magnitude angle, a relative phase, and independent mixed-orbit input and output Bloch angles. This is the complete ordinary-cubic class under the stated assumptions, not another aligned sub-ansatz.

A deterministic search evaluated both exact autocorrelation families over all 327 displacement differences. Twelve restarts finished with squared residuals between \(1.0875577212854972\) and \(1.3333333333333341\); none approached zero. The leading unsatisfied equations form the cubic orbit of \((\pm3,\pm3,0)\) and permutations.

This changes the execution order but not yet the theorem list. The ordinary-cubic all-nonzero two-component walk is now numerically pinned. Closing it requires an exact inconsistency or positive lower bound for the obstructing displacement orbit. Meanwhile, projective phases, sparse support and a principled higher-dimensional carrier remain live. The programme should not spend the next cycle repeatedly optimizing the same four variables; it should either algebraize the obstruction or move to another branch.

See [Ordinary-cubic skew textures: complete reduction and numerical obstruction](../0100-0199/180_ordinary_cubic_skew_texture_numerical_obstruction.md).

### 20.93 Majorana orientation data admit an exact weak-basis invariant

For nondegenerate charged-lepton masses, let \(P_\alpha(H_e)\) be the spectral projector labeled by \(\alpha=e,\mu,\tau\). The closed trace

\[
Q_{\alpha\beta}
=\operatorname{Tr}\left(
P_\alpha^*MP_\alpha M^\dagger
P_\beta^*MP_\beta M^\dagger
\right)
\]

is invariant under arbitrary weak-basis transformations \(M\mapsto W^TMW\) and \(H_e\mapsto W^\dagger H_eW\). In the charged-lepton mass frame,

\[
\operatorname{Im}Q_{\alpha\beta}
=\operatorname{Im}\left[
M_{\alpha\alpha}M_{\beta\beta}(M_{\alpha\beta}^*)^2
\right].
\]

This resolves the concern that the previously identified Majorana quantity was merely a chosen-frame artifact. The datum is relational: neither \(M\) nor a raw Nambu \(\sigma_y\) component is enough; the charged-lepton spectral structure supplies the second tensor needed to close the invariant cycle.

The possible external coupling \(\chi_{\rm ext}\operatorname{Im}Q_{\alpha\beta}\) is now weak-basis covariant. It is not yet a satisfactory local interaction. Spectral projectors contain inverse charged-lepton eigenvalue differences, and clearing their denominators produces a high-degree spurion polynomial. A selected mediator, scale and coefficient remain necessary.

See [Weak-basis Majorana invariant from charged-lepton spectral projectors](../0100-0199/181_weak_basis_majorana_invariant_from_charged_lepton_projectors.md).

### 20.94 A lower-degree polynomial replaces the spectral denominators

Pair-resolved Majorana information can be made polynomial by clearing projector denominators, but the resulting numerator contains eight powers of \(H_e\). A lower-degree alternative is obtained by summing over flavor implicitly:

\[
J_M
=\operatorname{ImTr}
\left(H_e^*MH_eM^\dagger MM^\dagger\right).
\]

This is an exact weak-basis invariant with no eigenvalue labels or inverse discriminants. Within the closed trace family containing two \(M\)'s and two \(M^\dagger\)'s, degree zero and one in \(H_e\) are necessarily real; degree two is the first nonzero CP-odd level.

An explicit real two-flavor rotation with one Majorana phase gives \(J_M\ne0\), while the zero-phase matrix gives \(J_M=0\). Thus the invariant probes Majorana-type phase information without relying on a Dirac mixing phase.

The price is loss of pairwise flavor resolution. The possible combined-even source \(\chi_{\rm ext}J_M\) is now polynomial and weak-basis covariant, but its coefficient remains free. If the Yukawa and Majorana matrices are nondynamical couplings, it is simply an orientation-selecting tadpole. A predictive bridge still requires a selected mediator or boundary action.

See [Low-degree polynomial Majorana-CP invariant](../0100-0199/182_low_degree_polynomial_majorana_cp_invariant.md).

### 20.95 A common orientation field does not imply a common CP law

If \(\chi\) is an SM-singlet external pseudoscalar, both

\[
\chi J_q,
\qquad
\chi J_M
\]

are allowed by gauge symmetry and by a combined operation that reverses external orientation and internal CP. The general tadpole is

\[
\chi(c_qJ_q+c_MJ_M+\cdots).
\]

The coefficients are independent in ordinary effective field theory. Explicit flavor sectors realize \((J_q\ne0,J_M=0)\) and \((J_q=0,J_M\ne0)\), while changing \(c_q,c_M\) can reverse or cancel the selected external orientation without altering the measured flavor matrices.

This is a decisive selection test. A common odd field supplies a place for CP data to couple, but it does not unify their normalization or sign. Any exceptional, integral or Jordan completion must provide one source-derived invariant tensor that fixes the relative coefficients and remains closed under radiative corrections. Merely embedding the sectors into one algebra does not defeat the independent-counterterm obstruction.

See [One orientation field, independent quark and Majorana CP portals](../0100-0199/183_common_orientation_field_independent_cp_portal_obstruction.md).

### 20.96 Exceptional arithmetic supplies a parity clue, not yet a selector

The primary exceptional results do not derive the radius-three shell measure. Wilson's minimal vectors occur in families counted by \(3\cdot240(1+16+16^2)\); Elkies–Gross obtain 819 Jordan roots and a rank-26 lattice linked to the Leech lattice. Although \(13=26/2\) and \(27=\dim H_3(\mathbb O)\), no known map turns those dimensions into the walk's \(13{:}27\) orbit weights. Those weights still come uniquely from fourth-moment isotropy.

The Baez–Schwahn flag does contribute a structurally relevant fact: the full stabilizer has a disconnected component acting antiunitarily on \(H_3(\mathbb C)\), while the identity component gives the Standard-Model gauge group. This supplies a credible home for internal conjugation parity.

However, the Jordan spectral invariants do not orient that parity. On \(H_3(\mathbb C)\), trace, quadratic trace and determinant are real and invariant under entrywise conjugation. The exceptional cubic norm is therefore an even consistency invariant, not the missing odd scalar that could relate \(J_q\) and \(J_M\).

The live exceptional question is narrower: does an oriented integral flag canonically provide an additional odd tensor whose invariant space is one-dimensional? Without that calculation, the Leech relation remains an arithmetic-selection candidate, while Monster/moonshine remains quarantined.

See [Exceptional cubic norm, CP evenness and the \(13{:}27\) audit](../0100-0199/184_exceptional_cubic_norm_cp_even_and_13_27_selection_audit.md).

### 20.97 Orienting the exceptional flag exposes a unique cubic odd scalar

The evenness of the real cubic norm does not end the exceptional orientation branch. Once the complex flag is oriented, the Baez–Schwahn decomposition

\[
H_3(\mathbb O)
\cong H_3(\mathbb C)\oplus M_3(\mathbb C)
\]

provides a complement field \(Z\) transforming as \(Z\mapsto hZg^\dagger\) under the connected \(SU(3)\times SU(3)\) stabilizer. Hence

\[
D_-(Z)=\operatorname{Im}\det Z
\]

is connected-invariant and reverses sign under the disconnected antiunitary component.

For one \(Z\), the holomorphic cubic invariant is unique up to scale because the only singlet contraction uses the two three-index volume forms. The nested qubit/qutrit flag retains this determinant as a two-selected-columns-plus-complement contraction. This is the first canonical antiunitary-odd scalar supplied by the exceptional flag itself.

It does not yet solve the physical portal. The complement matrix is not automatically a Yukawa, Majorana or Furey matter matrix. Canonical covariant maps from physical flavor data into one \(Z\) are still missing, and multiple complement fields produce multiple polarized determinant invariants. The positive result moves the problem from “find an odd tensor” to “derive the physical embedding and prove multiplicity one.”

See [The oriented exceptional flag supplies a unique bare cubic odd invariant](../0100-0199/185_oriented_exceptional_flag_unique_cubic_odd_invariant.md).

### 20.98 The exceptional complement is a mixed-chirality quark module

Under the nested Standard-Model stabilizer, the exceptional complement decomposes exactly as

\[
M_3(\mathbb C)
\downarrow G_{\rm SM}
=
(\mathbf3,\mathbf2)_{1/6}
\oplus
(\mathbf3,\mathbf1)_{-1/3}.
\]

It therefore packages \(Q_L\) with \(d_R\). Furey's all-left TRO packages \(Q_L\) with \(d_L^c\). Conjugating the whole complement fixes the singlet convention but also conjugates the doublet, so no global real-structure choice identifies both sectors simultaneously.

The cubic determinant is a genuine gauge singlet:

\[
\det Z=\epsilon_{abc}Q_1^aQ_2^bd^c,
\qquad
\frac16+\frac16-\frac13=0.
\]

But it is a \(QQd\)-type contraction, not a Yukawa with a colorless Higgs. If the entries are ordinary Weyl fermions, three spinors contain no Lorentz scalar. The determinant must instead be interpreted through a bosonic flavon, composite, supersymmetric superfield or state-space orientation variable.

Moreover, cubic uniqueness is fragile: \(n\) complement fields admit \(\binom{n+2}{3}\) polarized determinant coefficients. The exceptional branch has therefore advanced from a missing odd invariant to a sharply defined representation, statistics and multiplicity problem.

See [Exceptional complement: quark partial match and the statistics gate](../0100-0199/186_exceptional_complement_quark_partial_match_and_statistics_gate.md).

### 20.99 The unique neutrino completion unlocks a composite exceptional carrier

The direct fermion interpretation fails, but the exceptional complement can be built from Lorentz-scalar fermion bilinears. Exhausting one-generation products gives a striking dependency:

\[
(\mathbf3,\mathbf2)_{1/6}
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
Q\nu^c
\]

uniquely. Without the previously derived \(\nu^c\) TRO extension, no minimal-matter bilinear has the exceptional doublet quantum numbers.

The singlet slot has two candidates,

\[
(QL)_{\mathbf1},
\qquad
(u^cd^c)_{\mathbf3}.
\]

Using \(QL\) makes the determinant violate baryon number by one unit. Using \(u^cd^c\) gives

\[
\det Z_B
\sim
\epsilon\epsilon
(Q\nu^c)(Q\nu^c)(u^cd^c),
\]

with \(\Delta B=0\), \(\Delta L=-2\). It is a dimension-nine, six-fermion, gauge- and Lorentz-scalar candidate whose imaginary part has the required orientation parity.

This is a genuine cross-branch convergence among the unique neutrino completion, Majorana orientation and exceptional determinant. It remains conditional because gauge representations do not construct the map: Furey's native closure is ternary \(XY^\dagger Z\), while these entries are binary CAR bilinears. The next gate is a functorial linking/CAR construction and an explicit seesaw matching calculation.

See [The neutrino completion unlocks a composite exceptional complement](../0100-0199/187_neutrino_completion_unlocks_composite_exceptional_complement.md).

### 20.100 Seesaw matching makes the convergence precise—and exposes its price

Write the baryon-safe exceptional interaction together with the minimal sterile sector as

\[
\mathcal L\supset
-\frac12M_RNN-y_\nu(LH)N
+\frac{C}{\Lambda^5}(QN)(QN)(u^cd^c)+\text{h.c.}
\]

At leading order the heavy-field equation gives \(N=-y_\nu(LH)/M_R+\cdots\), and therefore

\[
\mathcal L_{\rm eff}
\supset
\frac{C y_\nu^2}{\Lambda^5M_R^2}
[Q(LH)][Q(LH)]\bigl(u^cd^c\bigr)+\text{h.c.}
\]

This is a dimension-eleven, baryon-conserving, \(\Delta L=2\) operator. The combination \(C y_\nu^2/M_R^2\) is invariant under rephasing of the sterile field, so its phase cannot be dismissed as a convention. After electroweak breaking,

\[
\frac{C y_\nu^2v^2}{\Lambda^5M_R^2}
=-\frac{C m_\nu}{\Lambda^5M_R}.
\]

The convergence is therefore real but conditional: the exceptional determinant, neutrino TRO completion and seesaw communicate through a legal EFT operator, yet they do not automatically reduce the parameter count. For one generation the phase is physical only relative to the new coefficient \(C\); it is not the multi-flavor invariant \(J_M\). A decisive advance now requires the algebra to select \(C\), its flavor tensor and its relation to the external orientation response.

See [Seesaw matching of the composite exceptional determinant](../0100-0199/188_seesaw_matching_of_composite_exceptional_determinant.md).

### 20.101 A portal-independent orientation observable

The response branch supplies a dimensionless discriminator that does not assume the exceptional or neutrino construction. For a positive two-face cross-spectral density, define

\[
c(\omega)
=\frac{\rho_{12}(\omega)}
{\sqrt{\rho_{11}(\omega)\rho_{22}(\omega)}},
\qquad |c(\omega)|\le1,
\]

and the ordered two-frequency area

\[
\mathcal A(\omega_1,\omega_2)
=\operatorname{Im}
\left[c(\omega_1)\overline{c(\omega_2)}\right].
\]

This quantity is bounded by one, invariant under a constant relative phase convention and independent positive channel gains, yet odd under exchanging the two faces. It is therefore a calibrated pseudoscalar of the response family rather than an arbitrary imaginary matrix entry.

One nonzero value proves that no constant face rotation makes both responses real. It thus rules out one global \(H_2(\mathbb R)\) carrier for that family and activates the orientation-complete \(H_2(\mathbb C)\), locally \(Spin_0(2,4)\), parent. Pairwise vanishing over the complete connected spectral support is the converse real-slice criterion. At nearby frequencies, \(\mathcal A\) reduces to the normalized phase curvature already isolated in the form-factor branch.

This is not yet a prediction: a concrete Standard-Model two-port response and its absorptive phases must be calculated. It is, however, the programme's cleanest current dimensionless observable gate because it is independent of every exceptional Wilson coefficient.

See [A dimensionless two-frequency orientation observable](../0100-0199/189_dimensionless_two_frequency_orientation_observable.md).

### 20.102 The simplest Standard-Model realization lives in flavor space

For two neutrino flavor tags \(a,b\), the residue at mass pole \(i\) has the positive minor

\[
R_i^{(ab)}=
\begin{pmatrix}
|U_{ai}|^2&U_{ai}\overline{U_{bi}}\\
\overline{U_{ai}}U_{bi}&|U_{bi}|^2
\end{pmatrix}.
\]

Its normalized coherence has unit magnitude. The oriented area between poles \(i,j\) becomes

\[
\mathcal A_{ij}^{(ab)}
=
\frac{\operatorname{Im}
\left(U_{ai}U_{bj}\overline{U_{aj}}\overline{U_{bi}}\right)}
{|U_{ai}U_{bi}U_{aj}U_{bj}|},
\]

which is precisely a normalized Jarlskog quartet. This is a satisfying identification: the response observable rediscovers established weak-basis CP geometry rather than manufacturing a new invariant.

It also exposes a crucial category boundary. In

\[
\mathcal R(s)=\sum_iF_i^{\rm face}(s)\otimes R_i^{\rm flavor},
\qquad F_i^{\rm face}\in H_2(\mathbb R),
\]

the flavor area may be nonzero while the external face marginal remains real. Flavor CP therefore does not by itself restore the \(Spin(2,4)\) parent of the external carrier. That conclusion would require a source-derived nonseparable face--flavor intertwiner. An arbitrary portal is insufficient because it merely adds another free coefficient.

See [Neutrino flavor orientation and the factor-locality gate](../0100-0199/190_neutrino_flavor_orientation_observable_and_factor_locality_gate.md).

### 20.103 Multi-flavor matching isolates an exact alignment target

Let \(M=M^T\) be the sterile Majorana matrix, \(Y\) the active--sterile Yukawa matrix and \(C=C^T\) the sterile-pair slice of the exceptional coefficient. Integrating out the heavy fields gives

\[
K=YM^{-1}CM^{-1}Y^T,
\]

whereas the ordinary seesaw gives

\[
m_\nu=-v^2YM^{-1}Y^T.
\]

The matched tensor is exactly invariant under arbitrary sterile basis changes because \(M\) and \(C\) transform by the same congruence. This makes the relative position of \(C\) and \(M\) physical rather than conventional.

The decisive ray is

\[
C=\kappa M
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
K=-\frac{\kappa}{v^2}m_\nu.
\]

On this ray, the exceptional operator inherits the light-neutrino flavor matrix and adds no new mixing texture. Away from it, a generic symmetric \(C\) adds independent flavor and CP data; for three sterile fields even a fixed spectator slice begins with six complex coefficients. A complex free \(\kappa\) also retains one relative phase.

The synthesis has therefore gained a precise algebraic burden: derive \(C\propto M\), fix the phase of \(\kappa\), and prove that radiative corrections preserve the ray. Merely assigning \(C\) the same transformation law as \(M\) does not select it.

See [Multi-flavor exceptional seesaw and the alignment gate](../0100-0199/191_multiflavor_exceptional_seesaw_alignment_gate.md).

### 20.104 The present Furey two-cycle cannot select the flavor ray

Replicating the one-generation Furey carrier gives \(\mathcal H_{\rm int}\otimes F\) with source action \(a\otimes1_F\). The multiplicity commutant therefore contains the full \(M_n(\mathbb C)\). Both \(M\) and \(C\) lie in

\[
\operatorname{Sym}^2(F^*),
\qquad
\dim_\mathbb C=\frac{n(n+1)}2.
\]

No nonzero canonical tensor is selected by the generation-blind algebra: the central \(U(1)_F\) sends every symmetric tensor to \(e^{2i\theta}S\). The neutral two-cycle therefore selects where a sterile interaction can live but not which flavor matrix occupies it.

Alignment follows from a unique shared spurion, \(M=aS\) and \(C=bS\), but this is additional structure. With two independent symmetric spurions, proportionality requires a non-generic coefficient relation. The programme must either derive families intrinsically or prove a one-spurion theorem.

See [Generation-commutant no-go for automatic alignment](../0100-0199/192_generation_commutant_no_go_for_automatic_seesaw_alignment.md).

### 20.105 Radiative closure has an exact transverse test

At \(C=\kappa M\), the aligned manifold is preserved precisely when

\[
P_M^\perp(\beta_C-\kappa\beta_M)=0.
\]

If both tensors experience the same matrix-valued congruence flow, alignment survives and different scalar anomalous dimensions only run \(\kappa\). If the exceptional operator experiences a different flavor matrix or mixes additively with an independent symmetric tensor, a transverse component is generated immediately.

This matters because the exceptional dimension-nine operator contains quark and composite fields absent from the Majorana mass term. A shared representation is not enough; a symmetry must enforce a one-dimensional operator ray throughout renormalization and threshold matching.

See [Radiative stability of exceptional-seesaw alignment](../0100-0199/193_radiative_stability_criterion_for_exceptional_seesaw_alignment.md).

### 20.106 An anomalous pole comparison isolates Majorana orientation

For a charged-current flavor tag \(\alpha\), the particle--hole residue at mass pole \(i\) has the positive rank-one form

\[
\mathcal N_i^{(\alpha)}
\propto
\begin{pmatrix}
|U_{\alpha i}|^2&U_{\alpha i}^2\\
\overline{U_{\alpha i}}^2&|U_{\alpha i}|^2
\end{pmatrix}.
\]

Its normalized coherence is \(c_i=U_{\alpha i}^2/|U_{\alpha i}|^2\). Comparing two mass poles removes the common charged-flavor phase. In the electron row,

\[
\mathcal A_{12}^{N,e}
=\operatorname{Im}(c_1\overline c_2)
=\sin(\eta_1-\eta_2).
\]

This is a genuine Majorana-sensitive orientation invariant in the anomalous spectral sector. It does not contradict the earlier warning that a raw Nambu \(\sigma_y\) coefficient is basis dependent: the new quantity is relational between two labeled poles and a charged-lepton spectral channel.

The result brings the Furey neutral two-cycle closer to an observable role but does not finish the bridge. The reverse arrow must first be proved to be the CAR conjugate of the original rather than an independent sterile field. Then a source-derived response map must connect that internal Nambu pair to the external Jordan faces.

See [Majorana Nambu pole area and the CAR-identification gate](../0100-0199/194_majorana_nambu_pole_area_and_car_identification_gate.md).

### 20.107 The neutral arrows realize CAR, but only in the correct category

On the completed neutral two-plane, the arrows are exact adjoints:

\[
a=|R\rangle\langle O_1|,
\qquad
a^\dagger=|O_1\rangle\langle R|,
\qquad
\{a,a^\dagger\}=1.
\]

They generate the one-mode algebra \(M_2(\mathbb C)\). This removes the local finite-carrier obstruction to a Nambu/Majorana reading.

The matter category gives a crucial distinction. One selected arrow extends the matter TRO from 15 to 16 dimensions. Using the reverse arrow as an independent matter direction instead closes to dimension 23; adjoining both independent orientations closes to dimension 24. By contrast, retaining one matter arrow while placing its adjoint in the surrounding observable star algebra preserves sixteen independent matter amplitudes.

Thus “the reverse arrow exists” does not imply a second sterile field. It becomes a second field only if its coefficient is independently integrated. The unresolved work is now Lorentz and Fock theoretic: prove that the block adjoint implements charge conjugation in a local Majorana field and that the Nambu pole-area response descends externally.

See [Local CAR realization and the matter-TRO enlargement gate](../0100-0199/195_local_car_realization_and_matter_tro_enlargement_gate.md).

### 20.108 Internal nilpotence does not erase the Majorana bilinear

The selected neutral arrow obeys \(n_A^2=0\) as a matrix unit. A left-handed Weyl field nevertheless obeys

\[
\epsilon^{\alpha\beta}N_\alpha N_\beta
=N_1N_2-N_2N_1
=2N_1N_2\ne0.
\]

These are products in different algebras. The physical action combines the Lorentz/Grassmann exterior product with an internal module pairing, for example

\[
B(n_A,n_A)=\operatorname{Tr}(n_A^\dagger n_A)=1,
\]

rather than multiplying the internal arrow by itself. The adjoint basis vector is part of the fixed dual structure and need not carry another independently integrated field coefficient.

This corrects the interpretation of the quadratic-cycle gate. The reverse-arrow cycle is useful for the Hermitian Nambu operator, but a physical Majorana term does not require two independent matter arrows. Conversely, a rule based only on ordinary cyclic matrix multiplication is too narrow to reproduce standard chiral fermion masses; it must include Lorentz exterior products and representation pairings.

See [Lorentz exterior pairing resolves the nilpotent-arrow mass gate](../0100-0199/196_lorentz_exterior_pairing_resolves_nilpotent_arrow_mass_gate.md).

### 20.109 Gauge symmetry makes the neutral self-pair unique

On the completed all-left generation

\[
Q\oplus u^c\oplus d^c\oplus L\oplus e^c\oplus N,
\]

exhausting all 21 unordered fermion pairs gives exactly one bare holomorphic gauge singlet:

\[
NN.
\]

All charged alternatives fail color, weak or hypercharge neutrality. With one Higgs doublet inserted, the exhaustive list becomes precisely

\[
Qu^cH,
\quad
Qd^cH^\dagger,
\quad
Le^cH^\dagger,
\quad
LNH.
\]

This gives the internal pairing a real uniqueness property: gauge equivariance singles out the sterile support and prevents bare charged overpairing. It still does not determine whether the coefficient is nonzero, its scale, or its three-family matrix. For three sterile generations, the allowed symmetric coefficient space remains six complex dimensional.

See [The unique gauge-invariant holomorphic pairing on completed matter](../0100-0199/197_unique_gauge_invariant_holomorphic_pairing_on_completed_matter.md).

### 20.110 The linking algebra normalizes—but does not phase-fix—the pairing

Every irreducible rectangular TRO carries the linking-unitary-invariant Hermitian form

\[
h(x,y)=\operatorname{Tr}(x^\dagger y),
\]

unique up to scale. This canonically normalizes the selected neutral arrow. A holomorphic Majorana term, however, needs a complex bilinear form. On the neutral line it is obtained only after choosing

\[
J_\phi(z)=e^{i\phi}\bar z,
\qquad
B_\phi(z,w)=h(J_\phi z,w)=e^{-i\phi}zw.
\]

Every \(J_\phi\) is an involutive antiunitary. The linking algebra alone does not choose \(\phi\), the mass magnitude or a family tensor. Nor can this neutral real structure extend internally over the undoubled charged chiral module, whose representations are complex.

The current conclusion is therefore precise: the linking algebra supplies the adjoint, dual and normalization needed to **permit** the unique neutral pairing, but it does not yet **require** or parameter-fix the Majorana action.

See [Linking-algebra pairing uniqueness and the real-structure gap](../0100-0199/198_linking_algebra_pairing_uniqueness_and_real_structure_gap.md).

### 20.111 Intrinsic orientation first appears as transport or loop holonomy

The two-frequency area on one edge is not invariant under the full calibration freedom. Even a reciprocal scalar link with

\[
c(\omega)=e^{i\omega\tau}
\]

has a nonzero area \(\sin[(\omega_1-\omega_2)\tau]\), which a relative clock shift removes. A fixed connection can make the area meaningful, but the connection is extra structure.

With three ports, the closure product

\[
\mathcal B_{123}=c_{12}c_{23}c_{31}
\]

is invariant under arbitrary local port phases. Its imaginary part flips under loop reversal. It equals one for a rank-one spectral carrier, while an explicit positive rank-two Gram response gives \((1+i)/4\).

The intrinsic response question therefore moves from an isolated two-face matrix to a network of pairwise carriers and their composition law. This is a natural place for Jordan-triple recursion to matter: not as a slogan for one edge, but as a candidate rule for sewing edges and determining loop holonomy.

See [Two-port transport-gauge obstruction and the three-port loop escape](../0100-0199/199_two_port_transport_gauge_obstruction_and_three_port_loop_escape.md).

### 20.112 The cubic norm is the three-relationship sewing condition

A reciprocal three-port response is

\[
R=
\begin{pmatrix}
a&x&y\\x&b&z\\y&z&c
\end{pmatrix}
\in H_3(\mathbb R),
\]

with cubic norm

\[
\det R=abc+2xyz-az^2-by^2-cx^2.
\]

The three principal \(H_2\) faces can each be positive while the full determinant fails; the cubic is the missing global compatibility condition. Eliminating the third face gives

\[
R_{12|3}=A-uu^T/c\in H_2(\mathbb R),
\qquad
\det R=c\det R_{12|3}.
\]

This is the first exact realization in the programme of the intuition that a cubic norm keeps three pairwise relationships locally consistent. It also positions \(Spin(2,3)\) accurately: the full real three-face cone has conformal group \(Sp(6,\mathbb R)\), while each effective two-face reduction has \(Sp(4,\mathbb R)\simeq_{\rm loc}Spin_0(2,3)\).

For a complex Hermitian three-port response, the determinant sees \(2\operatorname{Re}(uvw)\) but not \(\operatorname{Im}(uvw)\). The latter is the loop-orientation pseudoscalar. The exceptional \(H_3(\mathbb O)\) remains a higher candidate, not a consequence of this associative three-port calculation.

See [Three-port H3(R), cubic consistency and the Spin(2,3) edge reduction](../0200-0299/200_three_port_h3r_cubic_consistency_and_spin23_edge_reduction.md).

### 20.113 Jordan recursion is congruence normalization plus Peirce restriction

For

\[
R_n=
\begin{pmatrix}A&u\\u^T&c\end{pmatrix}>0,
\]

the recursive carrier is

\[
R_{n-1}=A-uu^T/c>0,
\qquad
\det R_n=c\det R_{n-1}.
\]

The triangular matrix

\[
G=
\begin{pmatrix}1&-u/c\\0&1\end{pmatrix}
\]

has determinant one and gives \(GR_nG^T=R_{n-1}\oplus c\). Each step is therefore a symmetric-cone structure-group congruence followed by projection onto a Peirce corner. Eliminating several interior ports is associative and commutes with congruences on the retained boundary.

This supplies the programme's rigorous version of Jordan-triple recursion. The triple system provides congruence, inversion and Peirce data, but raw iteration of \(\{A,X,B\}\) is not itself the response recursion. The conformal groups descend

\[
Sp(2n,\mathbb R)
\rightsquigarrow\cdots\rightsquigarrow
Sp(4,\mathbb R)
\simeq_{\rm loc}Spin_0(2,3).
\]

Thus \(Spin(2,3)\) is the universal nontrivial two-port terminus of this real symmetric hierarchy, conditional on a physical rule choosing which ports become interior.

See [Recursive Schur--Jordan descent and functorial sewing](../0200-0299/201_recursive_schur_jordan_descent_and_functorial_sewing.md).

### 20.114 The remembered Jordan-triple implication is now exact—with hypotheses

For a positive real symmetric response decomposed into retained, relational and interior Peirce components,

\[
R=A+X+C,
\]

the exact effective carrier is

\[
\boxed{
R_{\rm eff}
=A-\{X,C^{-1},X\}.
}
\]

In the special Jordan algebra, \(\{X,Y,X\}=XYX\), so this is precisely the Schur correction. The relationship \(X\) occupies both outer slots; the interior Green function \(C^{-1}\) occupies the middle. Recursion through positive Peirce corners is associative and, when two ports remain, lands in \(H_2(\mathbb R)_+\).

Therefore the programme can finally state

\[
\text{positive Peirce--Schur Jordan-triple recursion}
\Longrightarrow
H_2(\mathbb R)
\Longrightarrow
Sp(4,\mathbb R)
\cong Spin_0(2,3).
\]

The hypotheses are essential. An arbitrary Jordan triple, arbitrary tensoring process or arbitrary endpoint does not imply \(Spin(2,3)\). The outstanding physics is to derive the real positive response and canonical two-boundary filtration from stress, causal or cellular dynamics.

See [Peirce--Schur triple recursion to Spin(2,3)](../0200-0299/202_peirce_schur_triple_recursion_to_spin23.md).

### 20.115 A scalar boundary system realizes the entire mechanism

For three boundary values \(\phi_i\) coupled to one interior scalar \(\chi\),

\[
S=\frac12\sum_i g_i(\phi_i-\chi)^2+\frac12m\chi^2,
\]

the interior response is \(C=m+\sum_i g_i\), and exact elimination gives

\[
R_3
=\operatorname{diag}(g_i)
-\frac{gg^T}{C}
=A-\{X,C^{-1},X\}.
\]

Its cubic determinant is

\[
\det R_3
=\frac{m g_1g_2g_3}{m+g_1+g_2+g_3}.
\]

For \(m>0\), this is a positive \(H_3(\mathbb R)\) response and reduces to a positive \(H_2(\mathbb R)\) carrier. For \(m=0\), the interior inverse still exists but the boundary response has the common-shift zero mode \((1,1,1)\). The latter is a gauge/Goldstone-style degeneracy, not a failure of Peirce--Schur recursion.

This is a rigorous physical prototype of the desired mechanism. It remains scalar and Gaussian; extending it to conserved Standard-Model stress or current response is the next burden.

See [A three-boundary scalar star realizes Peirce--Schur recursion](../0200-0299/203_three_boundary_scalar_star_realizes_peirce_schur_recursion.md).

### 20.116 Gauge zero modes impose a range condition, not an arbitrary inverse

For a semidefinite block response

\[
R=\begin{pmatrix}A&B\\B^T&C\end{pmatrix},
\qquad C\ge0,
\]

the generalized recursion exists on the physical quotient only when

\[
\operatorname{ran}(B^T)\subseteq\operatorname{ran}(C),
\qquad\text{equivalently}\qquad
B\ker C=0.
\]

Then

\[
R_{\rm eff}=A-BC^+B^T=A-\{X,C^+,X\}\ge0,
\]

and the result is independent of a regulator placed on the decoupled null subspace. If a boundary source couples to an exact interior zero mode, the full quadratic form is indefinite and the regulated correction diverges as \(1/\varepsilon\).

This turns Ward identities into a concrete admissibility test: gauge null modes must decouple from gauge-invariant boundary sources before the Jordan response is defined.

See [Singular-interior Peirce--Schur quotient and the range gate](../0200-0299/204_singular_interior_peirce_schur_quotient_and_range_gate.md).

### 20.117 Ward identities implement the singular quotient

A conserved Euclidean vector-current spectral tensor has

\[
C_{\mu\nu}=\rho\left(\delta_{\mu\nu}-\frac{q_\mu q_\nu}{q^2}\right),
\qquad Cq=0.
\]

For two conserved probes, \(Bq=0\), exactly matching the singular-Schur range condition. The physical response is

\[
R_2=A-BC^+B^T\in H_2(\mathbb R)_+.
\]

A longitudinal probe instead makes the enlarged kernel indefinite and regulator dependent. Conservation is therefore not merely compatible with the Jordan quotient; it enforces its admissible domain.

See [Conserved-current Ward quotient to an H2 response](../0200-0299/205_conserved_current_ward_quotient_to_h2_response.md).

### 20.118 Stress spectral data reach the same carrier

On the ten-dimensional space of symmetric Euclidean sources, conserved stress spectral data decompose as

\[
C_T=\rho_2P_2+\rho_0P_0,
\]

where \(P_2\) has rank five, \(P_0\) has rank one and four longitudinal directions are Ward nulls. Two conserved stress smearings satisfy the range condition and give

\[
R_2=A-BC_T^+B^T\in H_2(\mathbb R)_+.
\]

This is the first direct stress-spectral realization of the terminal Jordan carrier. It remains kinematic because the Standard-Model values of \(\rho_2,\rho_0\), the conserved contact matrix and the physical choice of two probes have not been derived.

See [Conserved-stress spectral quotient to an H2 response](../0200-0299/206_conserved_stress_spectral_quotient_to_h2_response.md).

### 20.119 Stress contact terms force a spectral formulation

For two fixed conserved probes, both the physical correlator and local diffeomorphism-compatible counterterms project onto the same matrices:

\[
R(q)=
[F_2(q^2)+p_2(q^2)]G_2
+[F_0(q^2)+p_0(q^2)]G_0.
\]

No fixed-momentum linear combination can remove every contact shift while retaining the physical stress signal. Across a Lorentzian cut, however, \(\operatorname{Disc}p_s=0\), leaving the positive, scheme-independent spectral carrier

\[
\rho(s)=\rho_2(s)G_2+\rho_0(s)G_0.
\]

The stress/Jordan programme must therefore formulate observables through pole residues, discontinuities or sum rules rather than absolute Euclidean kernel entries.

See [Stress contact-counterterm obstruction and the spectral escape](../0200-0299/207_stress_contact_counterterm_obstruction_and_spectral_escape.md).

### 20.120 The stress spectrum occupies only a slice of the Jordan cone

For fixed probes in a parity-even Lorentz-invariant vacuum,

\[
\dim\operatorname{span}\{\rho(s)\}\le2
<\dim H_2(\mathbb R)=3.
\]

In the conformal limit, \(\rho_0=0\), the family collapses to the single ray \(\rho_2(s)G_2\). A generic \(Sp(4,\mathbb R)\) cone transformation moves the response outside this physical slice.

Thus the full group is presently an ambient cone symmetry, not a demonstrated dynamical symmetry of the stress spectral family. A third independent direction must come from additional boundary, medium, parity-sensitive, detector or mixed-operator structure and must be derived rather than inserted.

See [Stress spectral-family dimension and the ambient Sp(4) obstruction](../0200-0299/208_stress_spectral_family_dimension_and_ambient_sp4_obstruction.md).

### 20.121 Free conformal matter realizes only one Jordan ray

The first concrete free-field check makes the preceding obstruction exact. For a four-dimensional free conformal field, conservation and tracelessness leave only the spin-two discontinuity,

\[
\rho_{ab}(s)=\kappa_Ts^2(G_2)_{ab},\qquad \kappa_T>0.
\]

All nonzero matrices are collinear in \(H_2(\mathbb R)_+\). Adding conformal species adds their positive stress central charges and merely rescales the same ray; it does not generate a new matrix direction. Scale-dependent normalized shape therefore diagnoses a departure from the exact conformal vacuum assumptions.

Mass thresholds, Higgs-scale breaking, nonconformal improvement and running can activate the transverse scalar Gram matrix \(G_0\). That expands the family to the already identified two-dimensional plane, not to the third Jordan direction. The physical Standard Model should therefore exhibit ray-to-plane deformation, while any third direction must be sourced by genuinely additional structure such as a boundary normal, medium velocity, mixed operator or varying probe family.

This result does not weaken the exact ambient identity \(\operatorname{Conf}(H_2(\mathbb R))=Sp(4,\mathbb R)\cong Spin_0(2,3)\). It specifies the missing burden: a theory must explain why physical response explores the ambient cone rather than merely living in a ray or plane inside it.

See [A free conformal field's stress spectrum is one Jordan ray](../0200-0299/209_free_conformal_field_stress_spectrum_is_one_jordan_ray.md).

### 20.122 The generic stress plane carries a \(Spin(2,2)\) subgeometry

Whitening \(G_2\) and solving the generalized eigenproblem for \((G_0,G_2)\) sends every generic independent two-form-factor plane to the diagonal Jordan subalgebra

\[
\mathcal D=\{\operatorname{diag}(x,y)\}\cong\mathbb R\oplus\mathbb R.
\]

Its positive cone is a quadrant. Direct calculation shows that its linear congruence stabilizer consists only of diagonal scalings and their composition with channel exchange. More importantly, its connected stabilizer under the full Siegel fractional action is

\[
SL(2,\mathbb R)\times SL(2,\mathbb R)
\cong Spin_0(2,2),
\]

a proper subgroup of the ambient \(Sp(4,\mathbb R)\cong Spin_0(2,3)\).

This produces a nested geometric interpretation of the stress route:

\[
\text{conformal ray}
\subset
\text{two-channel }Spin_0(2,2)\text{ subgeometry}
\subset
\text{ambient }Spin_0(2,3)\text{ cone}.
\]

The third Jordan coordinate is now identifiable: it is off-diagonal coherence between the two generalized stress eigenchannels. No choice of the two scalar functions \(\rho_2(s)\) and \(\rho_0(s)\) can create it while the Gram matrices remain fixed. A successful full-cone mechanism must rotate the physical eigenbasis, transform probes/background data, or introduce a mixed response not simultaneously diagonalizable with \(G_2\) and \(G_0\).

See [The stress-plane stabilizer is a Spin(2,2) subgeometry inside Spin(2,3)](../0200-0299/210_stress_plane_stabilizer_is_spin22_inside_spin23.md).

### 20.123 A medium can supply the missing relational coordinate

The vacuum obstruction is not universal once the state itself contributes a timelike vector. In a thermal or finite-density state, the Ward-quotiented stress response at nonzero momentum decomposes into tensor, shear/vector and sound/scalar sectors. For two conserved probes, each sector supplies a positive \(2\times2\) Gram matrix.

An explicit channel assignment gives

\[
G_T=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad
G_V=\begin{pmatrix}0&0\\0&1\end{pmatrix},\qquad
G_S=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&1\end{pmatrix}.
\]

These matrices are positive semidefinite and linearly independent, so their span is all of \(H_2(\mathbb R)\). The off-diagonal entry is generated by a channel shared coherently between the two probe faces. This gives a concrete stress-response realization of the relational-carrier intuition: the third coordinate is a relation, not merely a third diagonal weight.

The result is deliberately limited. It proves that a physical medium removes the kinematic two-plane obstruction; it does not prove that one Standard-Model plasma supplies three independent nonzero functions, explores an open part of the cone, selects the probes, or realizes \(Spin_0(2,3)\) dynamically. Full linear span and full group symmetry are different claims.

See [Thermal stress channels can kinematically span the full H2 carrier](../0200-0299/211_thermal_stress_channels_can_span_full_h2.md).

### 20.124 Hydrodynamic controls can locally explore all three coordinates

Full linear span does not guarantee a locally open response family. A concrete leading hydrodynamic prototype resolves that next gate. Let the tensor, shear-diffusion and sound-channel weights depend on frequency, momentum and temperature through the usual positive dissipative shapes, with \(w\propto T^4\), \(\eta\propto T^3\) and diffusion/attenuation scales proportional to \(T^{-1}\).

For explicit positive constants, the map

\[
(\omega,k,T)\longmapsto(a,b,c)
\]

has a nonzero Jacobian determinant at a declared sample point. Because the three channel Gram matrices form a basis of \(H_2(\mathbb R)\), the response matrices then occupy a locally open three-dimensional subset of the positive carrier.

The stress branch has therefore crossed three distinct thresholds:

\[
\text{vacuum plane}
\longrightarrow
\text{medium full span}
\longrightarrow
\text{medium local rank three}.
\]

It has not crossed the fourth threshold: a physical composition law or group action closing the family under \(Sp(4,\mathbb R)\). The hydrodynamic pole structure, KMS relations and transport data may break the ambient group strongly even while providing complete tomography of the cone.

See [A hydrodynamic stress map can have local rank three](../0200-0299/212_hydrodynamic_stress_map_can_have_local_rank_three.md).

### 20.125 Causal thermal responses admit exact Schur sewing

The medium carrier can be strengthened from a family of positive matrices to a matrix-valued Herglotz function \(K(z)\), analytic in the upper half-plane with \(\operatorname{Im}K(z)\succeq0\). For reciprocal boundary/interior blocks joined by a real frequency-independent coupling,

\[
K_{\rm eff}=A-BD^{-1}B^T
\]

remains Herglotz because

\[
\operatorname{Im}K_{\rm eff}
=\operatorname{Im}A
+BD^{-\dagger}(\operatorname{Im}D)D^{-1}B^T\succeq0.
\]

At one common temperature, multiplying the boundary spectral density by the scalar bosonic KMS factor produces the sewn fluctuation kernel. This is the first exact composition law in the thermal stress branch that preserves causality, passivity and equilibrium simultaneously.

The temperature hypothesis is rigid. Two independent channels at different temperatures carry different \(\coth(\beta_i\omega/2)\) multipliers and cannot be represented by one effective equilibrium temperature. Nonequilibrium sewing is therefore a separate branch, not a harmless extension of the equilibrium theorem.

See [Fixed-temperature KMS--Herglotz responses are closed under Schur sewing](../0200-0299/213_fixed_temperature_kms_herglotz_schur_sewing.md).

### 20.126 Ultraviolet normalization breaks abstract full-group response symmetry

The entire symplectic Möbius group preserves the abstract Siegel/Herglotz response domain. A physical normalization is more restrictive. For a response with \(K(iy)/(iy)\to M>0\), a generic fractional transformation with lower-left block \(C\ne0\) removes the linear growth; symplectic inversion sends \(iyM\) to \(iM^{-1}/y\).

Preserving the normalized class forces \(C=0\), leaving the Siegel parabolic

\[
K\longmapsto AKA^T+Q,
\qquad
P\cong GL(2,\mathbb R)\ltimes Sym_2(\mathbb R).
\]

The real symmetric \(Q\) is a contact shift and leaves spectral density unchanged. Fixing the leading coefficient \(M\) reduces \(GL(2)\) further to \(O(M)\). Thus full \(Spin_0(2,3)\) is exact on the unconstrained response domain but generally not on one UV-normalized local-QFT response family.

See [Ultraviolet normalization reduces abstract Sp4 response symmetry to a Siegel parabolic](../0200-0299/214_uv_normalization_reduces_sp4_to_siegel_parabolic.md).

### 20.127 Ward-singular causal sewing works exactly on constant-rank patches

The causal Schur theorem survives conservation-law null spaces when the kernel is fixed on the analytic patch. Restricting the interior Herglotz function to its physical support makes its inverse analytic, while the Ward identity \(B\ker D=0\) removes every null-sector coupling. The effective response

\[
K_{\rm eff}=A-BD^+B^T
\]

is then analytic and passive, and is exactly independent of a null-sector regulator.

This supplies the missing compatibility between the Ward quotient and Herglotz/Jordan sewing. It also sharpens the boundary: if support rank changes, \(D^+\) is generally nonanalytic and the corresponding mode must be treated through a pole, a spectral measure, patching data or explicit restoration. A global fixed-face carrier may additionally encounter holonomy in the momentum-dependent physical-support bundle.

See [Constant-kernel Ward Herglotz responses admit analytic pseudoinverse sewing](../0200-0299/215_constant_kernel_ward_herglotz_pseudoinverse_sewing.md).

### 20.128 The null stress face carries a fourth-power Hopf twist

Global Ward-support topology separates the massive and null branches. For Euclidean nonzero momentum, \(q^\perp\cong TS^3\) has a global quaternionic frame, so the conserved rank-five traceless and rank-one trace bundles are trivial. The timelike mass shell is contractible as well. No unavoidable momentum-space twist exists in those sectors.

For null directions, the screen bundle is \(TS^2\). A screen-frame rotation by \(\theta\) acts on transverse traceless spin-two polarization by \(2\theta\), giving single-helicity Chern numbers \(\pm4\). The opposite-helicity pair can be globally trivial even though either oriented face is not.

This makes the Hopf language precise. If \(H\) is the primitive Hopf line with \(c_1(H)=1\), the helicity-two line is topologically \(H^{\pm4}\), subject to convention. The primitive carrier may have “one twist,” but the stress polarization itself has four units. Connecting this twisted helicity pair to the real two-face Jordan carrier now requires an explicit patchwise intertwiner.

See [The massive Ward bundle is trivial, but the null spin-two bundle has Chern number four](../0200-0299/216_massive_ward_bundle_trivial_null_spin2_bundle_chern_four.md).

### 20.129 Opposite helicities give global norms but a Chern-eight relationship

If the two Jordan faces are conditionally identified with the null helicity lines \(L_+\) and \(L_-\), their intensities are global scalars but their coherence is a section of

\[
\operatorname{Hom}(L_-,L_+),
\qquad c_1=4-(-4)=8.
\]

On patch overlaps the off-diagonal coordinate transforms as \(z\mapsto e^{i8\phi}z\). A fixed real axis is therefore not preserved, and the nonzero Euler class rules out a global real-line subbundle. The helicity construction cannot by itself produce one globally componentwise-real \(H_2(\mathbb R)\) carrier.

Nevertheless, \(a\), \(b\), \(|z|^2\), trace, determinant and positivity are global. This makes the “norm as local consistency” intuition exact: Jordan invariant data can glue even when Jordan coordinates do not. A global real carrier now requires a Chern-minus-eight compensator, loss of the phase through invariant-only dynamics, or explicitly patchwise coordinates carrying holonomy.

See [An opposite-helicity carrier has a Chern-eight relationship obstruction](../0200-0299/217_opposite_helicity_carrier_has_chern_eight_relationship_obstruction.md).

### 20.130 Hypercharge weights do not cancel celestial topology by themselves

The Furey/internal \(U(1)\) inventory does not automatically provide the inverse relationship bundle. A normalized hypercharge is a representation weight; it becomes a Chern number only after specifying a principal bundle, flux and map to the celestial sphere. No elementary one-generation multiplet has weight minus eight, and arithmetic composites do not solve the base-space, gauge-singlet or nonvanishing-section requirements.

Therefore any internal cancellation must be an explicit locking construction relating internal and celestial transition functions. A numerical appearance of eight in charge arithmetic is not enough.

See [Furey hypercharge does not automatically cancel the celestial Chern-eight obstruction](../0200-0299/218_furey_hypercharge_does_not_automatically_cancel_celestial_chern_eight.md).

### 20.131 The obstruction naturally lifts the carrier to \(H_2(\mathbb C)\)

Although the off-diagonal relationship cannot be globally real, the full opposite-helicity endomorphism bundle glues as a bundle of \(H_2(\mathbb C)\) Jordan algebras. Patch changes act by unitary conjugation and preserve the Jordan product, triple product, determinant and positive cone.

This supplies a concrete global ladder:

\[
\text{twisted }H_2(\mathbb C)
\;\xrightarrow{\text{real relationship selector}}\;
H_2(\mathbb R),
\]

with the corresponding conformal rungs

\[
Spin_0(2,4)\longrightarrow Spin_0(2,3).
\]

The parent complex rung is what global helicity topology permits automatically; the middle real rung requires compensating or defect data. Since the relationship line has Chern number eight, a generic selector must have total zero index eight. This turns the earlier selector descent into a topologically constrained problem rather than an arbitrary real-form choice.

See [The twisted helicity carrier glues as H2(C): Spin(2,4) before Spin(2,3)](../0200-0299/219_twisted_helicity_carrier_glues_as_h2c_spin24_before_spin23_reduction.md).

### 20.132 An explicit real selector has total defect index eight

Model the relationship line as \(\mathcal O(8)\to\mathbb{CP}^1\). The section

\[
s_N(z)=z^8-1,
\qquad
s_S(w)=1-w^8
\]

is regular at infinity and has eight simple zeros. Away from those zeros, its phase chooses a real relationship axis and therefore a local \(H_2(\mathbb R)\) carrier with local \(Spin_0(2,3)\) conformal geometry. At each zero the phase and real reduction fail, returning to the complex parent carrier.

The symmetric placement of the roots is a model choice, but their total signed index is not:

\[
\sum_k\operatorname{ind}(s;z_k)=8.
\]

Thus any uncompensated global real selector must contain defects of total index eight. Whether they are polarization vortices, physical nodes, boundary data or only momentum-space patch singularities is now a concrete dynamical question.

See [A degree-eight selector produces eight local Spin(2,3) defects](../0200-0299/220_degree_eight_selector_gives_eight_local_spin23_defects.md).

### 20.133 Jordan recursion is globally valid in the twisted parent bundle

Boundary and interior response blocks transform covariantly under their respective unitary patch frames. Consequently,

\[
S=A-BD^{-1}B^\dagger
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
S'=USU^\dagger.
\]

Schur complements computed in different helicity gauges are therefore representatives of one global section. Successive elimination, positivity, trace, determinant and Jordan triple composition survive the Chern twisting without modification.

The topology obstructs only the additional real-form reduction. On a selector domain, a portal \(B\) preserves \(H_2(\mathbb R)\) precisely when it intertwines the boundary and interior real structures. Around a selector defect, the complex recursion remains single-valued as a bundle operation while raw real coordinates acquire transition monodromy.

Thus the programme's central recursion now has a stronger form: global Jordan-triple recursion first yields the twisted \(H_2(\mathbb C)\) parent; \(Sp(4,\mathbb R)\cong Spin_0(2,3)\) follows only on selector-compatible real domains or after topological cancellation.

See [Schur--Jordan recursion is globally covariant in the twisted H2(C) bundle](../0200-0299/221_twisted_bundle_schur_recursion_is_globally_covariant.md).

### 20.134 The Furey portal condition is a fixed real TRO equation

For a Furey rectangle \(M\subset\operatorname{Hom}(F,E)\), antiunitary involutions \(J_E,J_F\) induce

\[
\tau(X)=J_EXJ_F.
\]

The real-portal condition required by twisted Schur sewing is precisely

\[
\tau(B)=B
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
J_EB=BJ_F.
\]

Fixed points of \(\tau\) remain closed under \(XY^\dagger Z\), so the portal can preserve the exact oriented-TRO/Jordan-triple composition. The obstruction is gauge-theoretic rather than ternary: a charged undoubled rectangle rotates its real axis under continuous \(U(1)\), and conjugation sends it to the opposite charge representation.

The viable routes are consequently restricted to neutral dressing, Nambu/conjugate completion, a gauge-covariant rotating real subbundle, or an external lock. The TRO permits these structures but its norm and incidence data do not select the conjugation phases.

See [The TRO real-portal intertwiner theorem and its gauge obstruction](../0200-0299/222_tro_real_portal_intertwiner_theorem_and_gauge_obstruction.md).

### 20.135 The dressed charged-lepton carrier is neutral but topologically different

The Higgs-dressed charged-lepton faces solve the internal gauge problem: both carry the same electromagnetic phase, so their full Gram response is neutral. This remains the strongest explicit Furey-derived matter \(H_2(\mathbb R)\) candidate.

It does not solve the celestial selector problem. In the massless limit the two fermion helicity lines have Chern numbers \(\pm1\), so their relationship winds twice; the opposite stress-helicity relationship winds eight times. After the electron becomes massive, its timelike mass shell is contractible and the spin bundle becomes trivial rather than supplying inverse stress winding.

Four tensor copies of the fermion relationship have the correct arithmetic Chern magnitude eight, but no canonical fourfold Lorentz/gauge bundle morphism follows from the Yukawa triangle. The dressed matter and stress carriers must therefore be treated as distinct until an explicit locking action is derived.

See [The dressed charged-lepton portal solves gauge neutrality, not celestial Chern eight](../0200-0299/223_dressed_charged_lepton_portal_solves_gauge_not_celestial_topology.md).

### 20.136 The stress relationship has an exact fermionic fourth root

Massless helicity bundles obey \(L_h\otimes L_{h'}\simeq L_{h+h'}\). Hence

\[
L_{\pm2}\simeq L_{\pm1/2}^{\otimes4},
\qquad
\mathcal R_2\simeq\mathcal R_{1/2}^{\otimes4}.
\]

At the level of transition functions, the fermion relationship winds as \(e^{i2\phi}\) and its fourth power is exactly the stress relationship transition \(e^{i8\phi}\). The factor four is therefore a canonical helicity-bundle identity, not numerical coincidence.

This provides a precise spinorial root for the stress relationship but not a compositeness theorem. A physical bridge still requires a local, gauge-neutral, statistics-compatible Furey/Lorentz operator map. The stress tensor may realize the relevant little-group weight through derivatives and spinor contractions without being a four-fermion bound state.

See [The stress relationship is the fourth tensor power of the fermion relationship](../0200-0299/224_stress_relationship_is_fourth_tensor_power_of_fermion_relationship.md).

### 20.137 The helicity topology branch requires a genuine null carrier

The Chern-four/eight construction must not be attached automatically to the earlier vacuum stress spectrum. At timelike spectral momentum \(q^2=s>0\), the stress spin-two channel is the five-dimensional \(SO(3)\) representation over a contractible mass shell. It need not contain an isolated massless helicity-
\(\pm2\) particle.

The celestial topology applies only when a genuine null carrier is supplied: a massless pole, gravitational radiation, null-infinity/boundary data, an on-shell helicity amplitude or another controlled screen-bundle construction. The programme therefore has two distinct branches:

\[
\text{timelike Herglotz/Jordan stress response}
\quad\text{and}\quad
\text{null twisted-helicity Jordan bundle}.
\]

Their interface is now an explicit missing theorem rather than an assumed limit. Failure to find it would leave the timelike response results intact while disconnecting the topological \(Spin(2,4)\to Spin(2,3)\) narrative from ordinary Standard-Model stress spectra.

See [Null-helicity topology is not generic stress-spectral topology](../0200-0299/225_null_helicity_topology_is_not_generic_stress_spectral_topology.md).

### 20.138 The Weyl walk supplies local primitive twists with global compensation

The discrete null-walk branch supplies a legitimate null root absent from the generic timelike stress spectrum. Around each Weyl node, one eigenband is a Chern-one line and the opposite-band relationship has Chern number two. Its fourth tensor power has Chern number eight, exactly matching the null stress relationship topology locally.

The same certified walk prevents an isolated global claim: it contains four charge-plus nodes at zero quasienergy and four charge-minus nodes at the Floquet \(\pi\) edge. Their total topological charge vanishes. Thus the primitive “one twist” exists locally while lattice consistency supplies compensating twists globally.

This is a plausible root architecture, not spin-two dynamics. A viable theory must explain whether the \(\pi\) nodes are anomaly-flow/regulator sectors, boundary partners or physical mirrors, and must still derive a gauge-invariant operator with a null spin-two pole.

See [Weyl-walk nodes realize local Hopf roots but cancel globally](../0200-0299/226_weyl_walk_nodes_realize_local_hopf_roots_but_cancel_globally.md).

### 20.139 A domain wall relocates the compensating chirality

A 4+1-dimensional Dirac mass kink supports a normalizable 3+1-dimensional chiral zero mode with profile

\[
f(w)\propto\operatorname{sech}(w/\xi)^{m_0\xi}.
\]

An antikink or remote boundary carries the opposite chirality, with finite-slab mixing suppressed as \(e^{-m_0L}\). Gauge anomaly is balanced by bulk current inflow. The mechanism therefore relocates the compensation required by the Weyl walk rather than deleting it.

This is a viable architecture but not yet a completion of the present walk: an explicit 4+1-dimensional local unitary, bulk gap, boundary spectrum and spectral-flow map are still required. Integrating out such a bulk would naturally produce a boundary Schur response and could connect the construction to the Jordan carrier.

See [A domain wall relocates Weyl compensation into bulk inflow](../0200-0299/227_domain_wall_relocates_weyl_compensation_into_bulk_inflow.md).

### 20.140 A complete Standard-Model generation passes the boundary anomaly test

One all-left Standard-Model generation cancels the color cubic, mixed non-Abelian--hypercharge, cubic hypercharge and gravitational--hypercharge anomalies. Its three colored quark doublets plus one lepton doublet also give an even number of \(SU(2)\) doublets, avoiding the Witten global anomaly.

The anomaly-free Furey matter set is therefore eligible to occupy one domain wall as a whole. This turns the boundary branch from an isolated-Weyl toy into a representation-compatible possibility. It does not solve the hard constructive questions: gauge-invariant mirror gapping, a finite local regulator, boundary Yukawa cycles and the induced positive Jordan response.

See [One Standard-Model generation passes the domain-wall anomaly gate](../0200-0299/228_one_standard_model_generation_passes_domain_wall_anomaly_gate.md).

### 20.141 A finite wall produces an exact Schur--Herglotz carrier

A rectangular discrete kink operator has an exact localized index mode. Embedding it in a finite Hermitian chiral Hamiltonian and projecting the resolvent onto two wall probes gives

\[
G(z)=P(H-zI)^{-1}P^T,
\qquad \operatorname{Im}G(z)\succeq0
\]

for \(\operatorname{Im}z>0\). The zero mode contributes a positive rank-one pole residue, and the massive transverse modes supply additional positive spectral weight.

After separating the two probes from the interior chain, block inversion gives

\[
G(z)=\left[A(z)-BD(z)^{-1}B^T\right]^{-1}.
\]

The boundary carrier therefore arises exactly by Schur elimination of the domain-wall bulk. This unifies index localization, causal passivity and Jordan-response sewing in one executable model. The remaining lift is physical rather than algebraic: tensor the transverse system with 3+1-dimensional Weyl dynamics, load the anomaly-free Furey generation and control the remote mirror wall.

See [A finite domain-wall resolvent is a Schur--Herglotz two-face carrier](../0200-0299/229_finite_domain_wall_resolvent_is_a_schur_herglotz_carrier.md).

### 20.142 The wall carrier supports an exact Weyl cone

Tensoring the transverse kink chain with a two-component spinor gives a finite Hamiltonian whose square separates exactly into transverse mass operators plus \(|\mathbf k|^2\). The index subspace is invariant and carries

\[
H_{\rm wall}(\mathbf k)=\boldsymbol\sigma\cdot\mathbf k,
\qquad E_\pm=\pm|\mathbf k|,
\]

while every nonzero singular value of the transverse operator produces a gapped bulk branch.

The projected wall resolvent remains Herglotz. Its zero-mode contribution factorizes as a real rank-one two-face residue tensored with the complex Weyl spin resolvent. This gives an exact finite model in which the Jordan face carrier, chiral wall localization and null fermion dynamics coexist without identifying their indices incorrectly.

The next burdens are concrete: gauge-covariant wall links, the complete anomaly-free Furey generation, a finite mirror wall and an exactly unitary discrete-time realization.

See [The domain-wall tensor lift has an exact Weyl cone and passive face response](../0200-0299/230_domain_wall_tensor_lift_has_exact_weyl_cone_and_passive_face_response.md).

### 20.143 The complete Furey generation can load without deforming the free carrier

Tensoring the wall system with the fifteen- or sixteen-state one-generation internal module gives

\[
H_0=H_{\rm wall}\otimes I_F,
\qquad
G_0=G_{\rm wall}\otimes I_F.
\]

Carrier operations commute with the internal gauge algebra, Herglotz positivity is unchanged and every species shares the same free light cone and localization profile. This is the exact free reference point required before interactions are introduced. Gauge links, Yukawa cycles, flavor mixing and mirror interactions must now be classified by whether they preserve the carrier commutant or satisfy the selector-compatible TRO portal equation.

See [An anomaly-free Furey generation loads as a commuting wall-carrier factor](../0200-0299/231_anomaly_free_furey_generation_loads_as_wall_carrier_commutant.md).

### 20.144 Spatial gauge links preserve the wall carrier

A finite Wilson-linked wall difference operator transforms by exact local gauge conjugation. Coupling it to the transverse kink through the chiral grading preserves both the index structure and the identity

\[
H_{\rm DW}[U]^2=H_\perp^2\otimes I+I\otimes H_U^2.
\]

The projected wall resolvent remains passive and gauge covariant; same-site two-face Gram data are gauge invariant because both faces carry the same local phase. This establishes compatibility of the domain-wall Jordan response with spatial gauge links in a finite \(U(1)\) prototype.

See [A gauge-linked wall Hamiltonian preserves covariance and passivity](../0200-0299/232_gauge_linked_wall_hamiltonian_preserves_covariance_and_passivity.md).

### 20.145 Finite separation suppresses mirror mixing but does not make the mirror heavy

An open topological dimer slab provides an exact finite kink--antikink analogue. Its two end modes form a pole pair

\[
E_\pm=\pm\delta_N,
\qquad
\delta_N\sim t_2(t_1/t_2)^N,
\]

with exponentially localized residues at the opposite boundaries. The two-end resolvent remains Herglotz and exposes both poles.

The result corrects a common shortcut: a thicker finite slab produces an exponentially smaller physical/mirror mixing mass, not a cutoff-scale mirror mass. Geometry creates a wide approximately chiral energy window but does not remove the partner. A genuine finite regulator still needs symmetric mirror-gapping interactions, an overlap construction or another explicit mechanism.

See [Finite-slab mirror poles split exponentially but persist](../0200-0299/233_finite_slab_mirror_poles_split_exponentially_but_persist.md).

### 20.146 Full Standard-Model Wilson transport remains in the carrier commutant

The full sixteen-state one-generation representation sends each finite gauge link to a block-diagonal matrix with the correct color, weak and hypercharge action. The representation homomorphism gives exact endpoint covariance, while carrier transformations act on a separate factor and commute with every link.

This completes the free spatial gauge-loading theorem beyond the Abelian prototype. It also isolates the actual difficulty: Higgs/Yukawa maps connect inequivalent blocks and are not ordinary Wilson transport.

See [Standard-Model block Wilson links preserve the wall-carrier commutant](../0200-0299/234_standard_model_block_wilson_links_preserve_wall_carrier_commutant.md).

### 20.147 A nonzero one-generation Yukawa portal selects a local real axis

For a complex mass portal \(m=|m|e^{i\varphi}\), antiunitary face structures obey the real-TRO equation precisely when

\[
\alpha-\beta=2\varphi.
\]

The equation is covariant under independent face rephasings, so the selected real line rotates with the gauge/frame bundle. At a Higgs zero the phase becomes undefined and the local real reduction develops a defect.

This gives the one-generation Yukawa interaction an exact selector role without promoting its removable phase to a CP prediction. The construction cannot be imposed entrywise on all flavor Yukawas, because a common full-flavor real structure would erase observed CP-odd invariants.

See [A one-generation Yukawa portal locally selects a real axis, but Higgs zeros are defects](../0200-0299/235_one_generation_yukawa_portal_locally_selects_real_axis_but_zeros_are_defects.md).

### 20.148 Co-localized opposite wall chiralities acquire an exact Dirac pole

Two higher-dimensional species with opposite wall chirality can share a normalized localization profile. Projecting a local Higgs/Yukawa portal onto their wall modes gives

\[
m_{\rm eff}=y\sum_w f_L(w)h(w)f_R(w).
\]

The projected Hamiltonian has diagonal Weyl blocks and off-diagonal (m_{\rm eff}), and its square is exactly

\[
H_D(\mathbf k)^2=(|\mathbf k|^2+|m_{\rm eff}|^2)I_4.
\]

Thus the wall construction, the Yukawa-selected local real axis and the passive Schur-response programme are mutually compatible in this free two-species sector. A zero of the overlap mass removes both the Dirac gap and the phase-selected real axis. This is not yet a derivation of Standard-Model masses: weak-doublet structure, all four Yukawa channels, flavor, finite-slab mirrors and bulk-mode mixing remain separate gates.

See [Co-localized wall chiralities and a Higgs portal give an exact Dirac pole](../0200-0299/236_colocalized_wall_chiralities_and_higgs_portal_give_exact_dirac_pole.md).

### 20.149 The complete one-generation Higgs pattern fits the wall portal

In left-handed Weyl notation, the four one-generation Yukawa contractions are

\[
u^cQ^T\epsilon H,\qquad d^cH^\dagger Q,\qquad
e^cH^\dagger L,\qquad \nu^cL^T\epsilon H.
\]

Their color, weak and hypercharge factors are exactly gauge covariant. In unitary gauge the antisymmetric orientation selects \(u,\nu\), the Hermitian orientation selects \(d,e\), and each nonzero projected wall mass supplies its own local real-axis selector.

The result removes a possible incompatibility between the wall carrier and the full one-generation Standard-Model portal. It simultaneously raises the bar for the Furey connection: cyclic incidence is no longer enough; the division-algebra maps must reproduce these four intertwiners, their conjugations and their shared Higgs doublet at operator level.

See [The full one-generation Higgs/Yukawa portal is gauge covariant](../0200-0299/237_full_one_generation_higgs_yukawa_portal_is_gauge_covariant.md).

### 20.150 Higgs inhomogeneity is measured by a Schur self-energy

The bare overlap mass is exact only when Higgs multiplication preserves the wall-mode subspace. In general the exact boundary response is

\[
P(H-z)^{-1}P=
\left[H_{PP}-z-H_{PQ}(H_{QQ}-z)^{-1}H_{QP}\right]^{-1}.
\]

For a common wall profile, the squared wall/bulk leakage is proportional to

\[
|y|^2\left(\langle h^2\rangle_f-\langle h\rangle_f^2\right).
\]

This gives the nested-doll intuition a precise quantitative role: a flat profile closes on the two faces; a weakly varying profile dresses them; a resonance with the transverse bulk means the boundary carrier must be enlarged. Exact Schur sewing preserves Herglotz passivity throughout, whereas an uncontrolled truncation need not.

See [An inhomogeneous Higgs profile requires Schur self-energy control](../0200-0299/238_inhomogeneous_higgs_requires_schur_self_energy_control.md).

### 20.151 The charged mirror generation has no unbroken-gauge bilinear gap

An exhaustive one-generation census shows that the only same-wall gauge-singlet Weyl mass is

\[
\nu^c\nu^c.
\]

The fifteen charged components admit no quadratic mass while \(SU(3)\times SU(2)\times U(1)\) remains unbroken. Cross-wall overlap is gauge invariant, but its two-face spectrum is \(\pm|\delta|\): it gaps both physical/mirror combinations rather than lifting the remote face selectively.

Anomaly cancellation therefore keeps symmetric mirror gapping logically open but does not construct it. A finite local completion must use genuine multi-fermion dynamics, additional matter, a mirror Higgs phase or a controlled infinite-wall limit. Neither geometric separation nor Furey dagger closure alone solves this regulator problem.

See [A mirror wall has no symmetric bilinear gap for a charged generation](../0200-0299/239_mirror_wall_has_no_symmetric_bilinear_gap_for_charged_generation.md).

### 20.152 Quartic mirror interactions cover the spectrum but do not yet gap it

The first interaction layer beyond bilinears contains eight representation-level gauge-singlet four-Weyl classes. In particular,

\[
QQQL,\qquad u^cu^cd^ce^c
\]

together touch all five charged representation types. They preserve \(B-L\), violate \(B+L\), and show that no charged field is isolated from the mirror interaction hypergraph.

This is a support theorem, not a phase theorem. A connected quartic hypergraph may break symmetry, retain massless composites or develop topological order. The Furey/TRO language offers a precise next construction—pair a ternary output \(xy^\dagger z\) with a fourth fermionic leg—but the resulting local Hermitian operator and its nonperturbative gapped phase must be demonstrated explicitly.

See [The mirror quartic hypergraph covers a generation but does not prove a gap](../0200-0299/240_mirror_quartic_hypergraph_covers_generation_but_does_not_prove_gap.md).

### 20.153 The covering quartics are genuine but symmetry-incomplete

Explicit exterior-algebra calculation confirms nonzero one-generation contractions

\[
\epsilon_{abc}\epsilon_{ij}\epsilon_{kl}(Q^{ai}Q^{bj})(Q^{ck}L^l),
\qquad
\epsilon_{abc}(d^{c\,a}u^{c\,b})(u^{c\,c}e^c).
\]

They provide a concrete local Hermitian interaction target. However, invariance imposes only \(3x_Q+x_L=0\) and \(2x_u+x_d+x_e=0\) on the six species phases. The resulting four-dimensional kernel leaves at least three continuous global symmetries after hypercharge is quotiented.

The mirror problem has therefore advanced from “do interactions touch every field?” to “does a maximal nonvanishing interaction set remove or correctly match every residual global anomaly?” A Furey cubic or ternary construction becomes physically discriminating only if it selects the required invariant tensors and symmetry-completing coupling pattern.

See [The covering mirror quartics are nonzero but leave a large global symmetry](../0200-0299/241_covering_mirror_quartics_are_nonzero_but_leave_large_global_symmetry.md).

### 20.154 Seven quartics plus the sterile Majorana channel are phase-symmetry complete

Exact exterior algebra leaves seven nonzero one-generation quartic classes and kills only the derivative-free \((\nu^c)^4\) class. Their species-phase constraint matrix has rank four, with kernel exactly

\[
\operatorname{span}\{Y,B-L\}.
\]

After gauged hypercharge is removed, global \(B-L\) is the only continuous species phase. Adding the allowed \(\nu^c\nu^c\) Majorana term raises the rank to five and leaves only hypercharge.

This gives the sixteen-state completion a new concrete role: the sterile state can remove the last accidental continuous symmetry in a candidate mirror Hamiltonian. The result remains kinematic; discrete anomalies and the strong-coupling phase must still be established before claiming a symmetric mirror gap.

See [Maximal mirror quartics leave only \(B-L\) before the Majorana channel](../0200-0299/242_maximal_mirror_quartics_leave_only_bminusl_before_majorana.md).

### 20.155 The symmetry-complete mirror lattice leaves only fermion parity

The integer interaction matrix of the seven nonzero quartics plus the sterile Majorana row has Smith normal form

\[
\operatorname{diag}(1,1,1,1,2,0).
\]

Its continuous null direction is hypercharge, and its only disconnected component is simultaneous sign reversal of every fermion. Thus the species-phase group is \(U(1)_Y\times\mathbb Z_2^F\); after quotienting the gauge direction, only mandatory fermion parity remains.

This removes the hidden-Abelian-symmetry objection to the candidate mirror Hamiltonian. It does not solve the nonperturbative phase: other discrete regulator symmetries, global anomalies, massless composites and topological order must still be excluded or characterized.

See [The mirror interaction Smith form leaves only gauge and fermion parity](../0200-0299/243_mirror_interaction_smith_form_leaves_only_gauge_and_fermion_parity.md).

### 20.156 Localization predicts flavor only after the seed matrix is constrained

Equal-width Gaussian wall profiles give

\[
Y^{\rm eff}_{ij}=\Lambda_{ij}
\exp\!\left[-\frac{(a_i-b_j)^2}{4\sigma^2}\right].
\]

Because every overlap is nonzero, arbitrary \(\Lambda_{ij}\) can reproduce any target matrix exactly. Geometry then reparameterizes rather than explains flavor.

If the seed is universal, the logarithmic mixed difference

\[
C_{ij}=\log|Y_{ij}|-\log|Y_{i0}|-\log|Y_{0j}|+\log|Y_{00}|
\]

factorizes as \((a_i-a_0)(b_j-b_0)/(2\sigma^2)\), so \(\operatorname{rank}C\leq1\) in one transverse dimension. This is a genuine falsification test. Real overlaps alone also give zero flavor CP invariant, requiring complex seed data or holonomy.
