See [Gaussian localization is predictive only after seed Yukawas are constrained](../0200-0299/244_gaussian_localization_is_predictive_only_after_seed_yukawas_are_constrained.md).

### 20.157 Logarithmic rank measures transverse dimension only with width control

For equal isotropic widths and separable seed magnitudes,

\[
C_{ij}
=\frac{(a_i-a_0)\cdot(b_j-b_0)}{2\sigma^2},
\qquad
\operatorname{rank}C\leq d_\perp.
\]

The rank theorem is robust under arbitrary row and column seed factors. It is not robust under generation-dependent widths: pair-dependent Gaussian denominators can produce full logarithmic rank even for one transverse coordinate.

Localization can therefore become a genuine geometric discriminator, but only if the wall/Furey dynamics fixes or controls profile widths. Complex nonfactorizable phase data must be supplied separately to generate flavor CP without erasing the magnitude-rank relation.

See [Logarithmic Yukawa rank counts dimensions only when widths are universal](../0200-0299/245_logarithmic_yukawa_rank_counts_dimensions_only_when_widths_are_universal.md).

### 20.158 Width splittings turn exact rank into a controlled singular-value test

For fractional width shifts \(\epsilon_i,\eta_j\), Gaussian overlaps obey

\[
\delta\log O_{ij}
=\frac{\|a_i-b_j\|^2}{4\sigma^2}
(\epsilon_i+\eta_j)+O(\varepsilon^2).
\]

A finite Lipschitz estimate bounds every entry of the logarithmic cross-difference perturbation and hence every singular value beyond the geometric rank. Small representation-dependent width corrections therefore blur the low-rank relation continuously; they do not destroy it discontinuously.

The physically meaningful observable is an approximate-rank hierarchy calibrated against a dynamical width-splitting estimate. It must be satisfied simultaneously with the Schur bound controlling Higgs-induced bulk mixing.

See [Small width splittings only perturb logarithmic rank continuously](../0200-0299/246_small_width_splittings_only_perturb_logarithmic_rank_continuously.md).

### 20.159 Dot-product hierarchy and wedge-product CP can coexist

A simply connected one-dimensional Abelian connection gives only endpoint-factorized phases and cannot generate a Jarlskog invariant. In two transverse dimensions, a flux background can instead give

\[
\theta_{ij}=\kappa a_i\wedge b_j,
\qquad
\Phi_{ik;jl}=\kappa(a_i-a_k)\wedge(b_j-b_l).
\]

Multiplying Gaussian overlaps by \(e^{i\theta_{ij}}\) leaves all magnitudes and their logarithmic rank unchanged while producing a nonzero CP-odd commutator invariant for generic three-family geometry.

This yields a precise geometric division: displacement dot products control hierarchy magnitudes, while oriented wedge products control flavor CP. The real two-face Jordan carrier remains factor-local and need not complexify.

See [Transverse flux generates flavor CP without changing overlap magnitudes](../0200-0299/247_transverse_flux_generates_flavor_cp_without_changing_overlap_magnitudes.md).

### 20.160 Shared left geometry forces a common magnitude/phase complex structure

For two-dimensional quark localization, shared left-doublet displacements give

\[
C_f=\frac1{2\sigma^2}AB_f^T,
\qquad
P_f=\kappa AJB_f^T.
\]

When the matrices are nondegenerate,

\[
P_uC_u^{-1}=P_dC_d^{-1}=M,
\qquad
M^2=-(2\kappa\sigma^2)^2I.
\]

Thus up and down hierarchy cross-ratios and flux plaquettes must encode the same oriented complex structure on the left-family plane. This is an exact model relation, but generic point geometry still contains 17 parameters for ten quark observables and the localization basis must be derived rather than chosen.

See [Shared left geometry links flux phases to magnitude cross-ratios](../0200-0299/248_shared_left_geometry_links_flux_phases_to_magnitude_cross_ratios.md).

### 20.161 Singular sectors can jointly recover the shared orientation

The inverse identity is only a special case of

\[
P_f=MC_f.
\]

Stacking up and down data gives \(\mathcal P=M\mathcal C\). If \(\mathcal C=(C_u\;C_d)\) has row rank two, then

\[
M=\mathcal P\mathcal C^T(\mathcal C\mathcal C^T)^{-1}
\]

is unique even when both \(C_u\) and \(C_d\) are individually rank one. Complementary incomplete relationships can therefore recover the common oriented action, while a rank-one full stack proves the two-plane is not identifiable from those sectors.

See [A stacked pseudoinverse recovers shared orientation from singular sectors](../0200-0299/249_stacked_pseudoinverse_recovers_shared_orientation_from_singular_sectors.md).

### 20.162 The recovered orientation is a complex structure, not yet Spin\((2,3)\)

Every real \(M\) satisfying \(M^2=-g^2I\) is explicitly conjugate to

\[
gJ,\qquad J=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\-1&0\end{pmatrix},
\]

and has centralizer \(\{aI+bM\}\cong\mathbb C\). The canonical \(J\) is not in \(H_2(\mathbb R)\); it generates rotations acting on the Jordan cone by determinant-preserving congruence.

This identifies an exact oriented real-plane structure shared by the localization construction and familiar complex modules. It does not identify the physical planes. A source-derived intertwiner and closure with the other \(Sp(4,\mathbb R)\) generators are mandatory before the result supports the Spin\((2,3)\) pole hypothesis.

See [A negative-square orientation is a complex structure, not yet a Spin\((2,3)\) derivation](../0200-0299/250_negative_square_orientation_is_a_complex_structure_not_yet_a_spin23_derivation.md).

### 20.163 The neutrino Peirce line is the strongest internal orientation candidate

Three source-native complex lines carry \(J^2=-I\): the weak off-diagonal line, the charged \(E\)-\(C\) linking line and the neutral \(E\)-\(D\) Peirce line. Only the last has equal gauge weights on both faces, so only it preserves a fixed real axis under the Standard-Model gauge group.

The neutral survivor exchange instead has square \(+I\) and anticommutes with \(J\); it can model conjugation/selection but not the orientation itself. The strongest current internal bridge is therefore the pair

\[
(J_\nu,\;K_{\rm exchange}),
\qquad
J_\nu^2=-I,\quad K_{\rm exchange}^2=I,\quad
K_{\rm exchange}J_\nu=-J_\nu K_{\rm exchange}.
\]

An explicit intertwiner must still carry the localization orientation, Higgs maps and positive response into this source-native pair without a free conjugating matrix.

See [The neutrino Peirce line is the only gauge-neutral Furey complex-structure candidate](../0200-0299/251_neutrino_peirce_line_is_the_only_gauge_neutral_furey_complex_structure_candidate.md).

### 20.164 Exchange supplies conjugation, but the real carrier also needs diagonal gluing

On the paired neutrino Peirce corners,

\[
\Theta(X_A,X_B)=(\bar X_B,\bar X_A),
\qquad
\Theta^2=1,
\qquad
\Theta J=-J\Theta.
\]

The exchange-fixed space has real dimension four: it retains one full \(H_2(\mathbb C)\), with the second survivor determined by conjugation. Only after imposing the additional diagonal identification \(X_A=X_B\) does the intersection become \(X=\bar X\), hence \(H_2(\mathbb R)\) of dimension three.

The selector problem has therefore narrowed to a physical diagonal gluing or locking mechanism. Exchange antiunitarity supplies conjugation but does not by itself supply the middle rung.

See [Survivor exchange pairs neutrino corners but needs diagonal gluing for \(H_2(\mathbb R)\)](../0200-0299/252_survivor_exchange_pairs_neutrino_corners_but_needs_diagonal_gluing_for_h2r.md).

### 20.165 Positive locking can select exactly the real Jordan carrier

On paired neutral Peirce observables, the potential

\[
V=\frac{\mu}{2}\|X_A-X_B\|^2
+\frac{\lambda}{2}\|X_B-\bar X_A\|^2
\]

is gauge neutral, exchange symmetric and positive for \(\mu,\lambda>0\). Its Hessian gaps the three real anti-diagonal modes and both imaginary combinations. The kernel has dimension three and is exactly

\[
X_A=X_B=\bar X_A\cong H_2(\mathbb R).
\]

This proves that the missing diagonal gluing and real selector can coexist in a healthy quadratic response model. It does not yet derive the locking from Furey's source algebra or establish the chiral Fock/Higgs completion.

See [Positive exchange/diagonal locking leaves exactly \(H_2(\mathbb R)\)](../0200-0299/253_positive_exchange_diagonal_locking_leaves_exactly_h2r.md).

### 20.166 The successful locking cannot be imposed entrywise on matter

Exchange reality on two sixteen-state complex survivors retains 32 real dimensions, exactly one complex generation. Adding diagonal gluing reduces the fixed data to 16 real dimensions and imposes a real condition on charged representations.

The same operation on three-generation flavor matrices makes them simultaneously real and forces

\[
\det[H_u,H_d]=0.
\]

Thus the positive \(H_2(\mathbb R)\) selector is viable only as a neutral response/Peirce compression in the commutant of complex matter and flavor. A universal internal reality condition is decisively excluded.

See [Diagonal Peirce locking cannot be lifted entrywise to full matter](../0200-0299/254_diagonal_peirce_locking_cannot_be_lifted_entrywise_to_full_matter.md).

### 20.167 The factor-local selector preserves the complete Yukawa operator

Let the neutral response locking act as \(L_{\rm sel}\otimes I\), and let the full broken-phase one-generation Yukawa operator

\[
H_Y=
\begin{pmatrix}
0&\operatorname{diag}(m_uI_3,m_dI_3,m_\nu,m_e)\\
\mathrm{h.c.}&0
\end{pmatrix}
\]

act as \(I\otimes H_Y\). Then

\[
[L_{\rm sel}\otimes I,\;I\otimes H_Y]=0
\]

for arbitrary complex masses. The same factorization preserves electromagnetic charge and complex three-generation flavor matrices.

This is the viable replacement for universal reality: the selector fixes only the neutral response face, while matter and flavor remain complex. Protection against symmetry-allowed mixed counterterms is the next gate.

See [A factor-local selector commutes with the full one-generation Yukawa operator](../0200-0299/255_factor_local_selector_commutes_with_full_one_generation_yukawa_operator.md).

### 20.168 Exchange symmetry leaves exactly three dangerous selector mixings

The exchange-even response sector contains the three light \(H_2(\mathbb R)\) coordinates and one heavy imaginary anti-diagonal mode. Consequently exchange symmetry permits exactly three light/heavy couplings.

An independent conjugation acting only on the neutral response factor makes the light coordinates even and the heavy imaginary coordinate odd, forbidding all three. If they are present, integrating out the heavy mode produces

\[
\Sigma(z)=\frac{vv^T}{M_h-z},
\]

a real rank-one correction. Reality survives, but exact kernel invariance, Jordan determinant symmetry and predictivity need not.

See [Exchange symmetry allows three dangerous selector mixings](../0200-0299/256_exchange_symmetry_allows_three_dangerous_selector_mixings.md).

### 20.169 A real rank-one self-energy still breaks the Jordan determinant

For the Lorentz metric \(\eta=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1,-1)\), conformal generators obey

\[
A^T\eta+\eta A=\lambda\eta.
\]

Substituting the selector self-energy residue \(A=vv^T\) forces \(v=0\). Therefore every nonzero single-heavy-mode Schur correction breaks the \(H_2(\mathbb R)\) determinant symmetry even though it remains a real symmetric operator on the three coordinates.

Exact carrier symmetry requires response-conjugation protection or a symmetry-aligned multi-mode residue completion. Otherwise Spin\((2,3)\) is only approximate, with a calculable determinant anisotropy.

See [Any nonzero rank-one selector Schur correction breaks Lorentz-determinant symmetry](../0200-0299/257_any_nonzero_rank_one_selector_schur_correction_breaks_lorentz_determinant_symmetry.md).

### 20.170 Positive determinant-preserving self-energy needs a degenerate multiplet

A positive symmetric residue preserves the Lorentz determinant infinitesimally exactly when

\[
S=
\begin{pmatrix}
a&b&c\\
b&a&0\\
c&0&a
\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
a\geq\sqrt{b^2+c^2}.
\]

The minimum nonzero rank is two. Hence at least two heavy channels with aligned coupling vectors are required. Their poles must be exactly degenerate; otherwise the energy-dependent residue weights separate and each nonconformal rank-one term reappears.

The selector is therefore protected either by response conjugation, which forbids mixing, or by a source-forced degenerate response multiplet. The minimal current Peirce locking contains only one dangerous heavy response mode and does not automatically realize the second option.

See [A Lorentz-symmetric positive Schur residue requires an aligned degenerate multiplet](../0200-0299/258_lorentz_symmetric_positive_schur_residue_requires_aligned_degenerate_multiplet.md).

### 20.171 The full linking response has the right heavy-mode count but no automatic multiplet

Restoring the \(C\)-face population omitted by the neutrino Peirce compression enlarges the paired gauge-neutral response to ten real dimensions. Its exchange-even sector contains the three light \(H_2(\mathbb R)\) coordinates and exactly two heavy modes: the diagonal \(C\)-population and the imaginary anti-diagonal neutrino coherence.

This is the minimum capacity required for a positive conformal rank-two residue. Yet their generic mass-squares are \(\rho\) and \(2\mu\), and their coupling vectors are unrelated. Exact completion requires the tuned relation \(\rho=2\mu\) plus residue alignment unless a larger source symmetry forces both.

See [The full \(M_3\) response supplies two heavy channels but not their alignment](../0200-0299/259_full_m3_response_supplies_two_heavy_channels_but_not_their_alignment.md).

### 20.172 Hypercharge forbids the obvious heavy-mode unification

In the ordered \((E,C,D)\) linking basis,

\[
Y=\operatorname{diag}(0,1,0).
\]

Its stabilizer is \(S(U(2)_{E,D}\times U(1)_C)\). The \(C\)-population projector is fixed by this group, while the imaginary \(E\)-\(D\) coherence lies in the neutral \(SU(2)\) adjoint triplet. They are inequivalent stabilizer representations.

Consequently no gauge-preserving source automorphism rotates the two heavy exchange-even modes into one another. The aligned-degenerate completion is possible only through tuning, an enlarged pre-hypercharge symmetry, or approximate emergent dynamics. Exact Peirce compression plus response conjugation is the minimal surviving architecture.

See [The hypercharge stabilizer forbids a source rotation of the two heavy modes](../0200-0299/260_hypercharge_stabilizer_forbids_source_rotation_of_the_two_heavy_modes.md).

### 20.173 Peirce compression is positive but exact closure is dynamical

The neutral-corner map

\[
\mathcal E_p(X)=pXp
\]

is a completely positive idempotent bimodule retraction and commutes with response conjugation. It is not a unital expectation on \(M_3\), because \(\mathcal E_p(I)=p\); the unital block expectation retains the \(C\)-population.

Unitary dynamics preserves the corner exactly iff \([H,p]=0\). Bare hypercharge-commuting face dynamics pass this test, but a charged off-block operator dressed by a compensating Higgs field can be gauge invariant in the total tensor product while violating Peirce closure. Full Higgs-dressed leakage is therefore the remaining compression gate.

See [Peirce compression is a CP retraction, not a unital full-algebra expectation](../0200-0299/261_peirce_compression_is_a_cp_retraction_not_a_unital_full_algebra_expectation.md).

### 20.174 Higgs compensation can preserve gauge charge while violating the corner

A charged face transition \(T_{EC}\) can be dressed by a scalar raising operator so that

\[
[H_c,Q_{\rm total}]=0
\]

while

\[
[H_c,p\otimes I]\ne0.
\]

The neutral \(D\to E\) transition satisfies both commutators. Eliminating the charged complement produces a rank-one self-energy \(g^2|\ell\rangle\langle\ell|/(\Delta-z)\), which is real but fails the Lorentz-determinant condition.

Gauge covariance and Peirce closure are therefore independent tests. Charged Higgs channels must decouple from the response factor, remain as controlled leakage, or force an enlarged carrier.

See [Higgs compensation restores gauge invariance but can break Peirce closure](../0200-0299/262_higgs_compensation_restores_gauge_invariance_but_can_break_peirce_closure.md).

### 20.175 The neutrino corner does not carry any complete Furey Higgs cycle

Relative to the neutral object pair \(\{D,E\}\), the up cycle is wholly external; the down and charged-lepton cycles each cross the boundary twice; and the neutrino cycle contains the internal \(D\to E\) arrow but also crosses through \(H\) twice.

Thus no complete cyclic Yukawa interaction preserves the Peirce corner as a same-carrier subsystem. Cyclic trace closure in the full block algebra does not imply invariance of every intermediate subspace.

The internal corner can still canonically label a separate neutral response factor or positive composite functor. That factor separation is now required, not optional.

See [No Furey Higgs cycle is internal to the neutrino Peirce corner](../0200-0299/263_no_furey_higgs_cycle_is_internal_to_the_neutrino_peirce_corner.md).

### 20.176 The four Yukawa cycles nevertheless close after passage to neutral response

The failure of same-carrier closure is not the failure of the matter/response bridge. For each one-generation channel, Higgs dressing produces two faces in the same Standard-Model representation:

\[
(\widetilde H^\dagger Q,u^{c\dagger}),\quad
(H^\dagger Q,d^{c\dagger}),\quad
(H^\dagger L,e^{c\dagger}),\quad
(\widetilde H^\dagger L,\nu^{c\dagger}).
\]

The Gram matrix of either pair has gauge-singlet entries and is positive semidefinite. Entrywise real projection therefore lands in the positive cone of \(H_2(\mathbb R)\), and every positive weighted channel sum remains there. This supplies the missing response functor:

\[
\text{crossing gauge-covariant matter cycle}
\longmapsto
\text{matched composite faces}
\longmapsto
H_2(\mathbb R)_+.
\]

What remains open is precisely dynamical rather than representational: the Standard-Model stress tensor or boundary flux must derive the weights, causal spectral measure and sewing rule. The construction therefore advances \(Spin(2,3)\) from a single charged-lepton analogy to a uniform four-channel target without pretending that cone membership already proves a universal physical symmetry.

See [All four Yukawa cycles induce gauge-neutral two-face Gram responses](../0200-0299/264_all_four_yukawa_cycles_induce_gauge_neutral_two_face_gram_responses.md).

### 20.177 Shared fields obstruct a naïve stress-derived channel sum

The attractive channel weights \((3,3,1,1)\) have a valid but limited origin: they are the color multiplicities of the quark and lepton composites. They are not obtained by assigning every fundamental field's complete stress contribution to every Yukawa cycle in which it appears.

The cycle-incidence equations make the obstruction exact. The right-singlet rows uniquely fix \((3,3,1,1)\), and the same vector correctly gives six \(Q\) and two \(L\) components. But all four cycles use the same Higgs doublet, so the naïve sum assigns it weight eight rather than its two complex components. Cone positivity cannot select a repair because every positive weight vector preserves positivity.

This moves the programme to the correct dynamical target: channel aggregation must be obtained from positive stress discontinuities, normalized boundary fluxes or a source-derived partition of the shared sector. The Jordan cone controls the response geometry; it does not manufacture the spectral measure.

See [Shared-field incidence obstructs naive stress-derived Yukawa weights](../0200-0299/265_shared_field_incidence_obstructs_naive_stress_derived_yukawa_weights.md).

### 20.178 A common sewing kernel is equality of normalized interior couplings

For channel blocks with a positive scalar interior pivot \(c_f\) and two-face coupling \(x_f\), channel aggregation and Schur elimination differ by

\[
S_{\rm after}-S_{\rm before}
=
\sum_f w_fc_f(r_f-\bar r)(r_f-\bar r)^T\succeq0,
\qquad r_f=x_f/c_f.
\]

This is an exact coupling-covariance identity. It proves that sharing the \(H_2(\mathbb R)\) cone is weaker than sharing the dynamics: aggregation commutes with recursive sewing exactly when all four normalized coupling ratios agree.

The hierarchy is therefore now explicit: common carrier, common causal class, then common sewing kernel. A Standard-Model derivation must climb all three rungs; the present four-channel construction has rigorously reached the first.

See [Channel aggregation and Schur sewing differ by a positive covariance](../0200-0299/266_channel_aggregation_and_schur_sewing_differ_by_positive_covariance.md).

### 20.179 The sewing covariance theorem survives noncommuting matrix interiors

For arbitrary positive-definite channel pivots \(C_f\), set \(R_f=X_fC_f^{-1}\), \(C=\sum_fw_fC_f\), \(X=\sum_fw_fX_f\) and \(\bar R=XC^{-1}\). Then

\[
\sum_fw_fX_fC_f^{-1}X_f^T-XC^{-1}X^T
=
\sum_fw_f(R_f-\bar R)C_f(R_f-\bar R)^T\succeq0.
\]

No \(C_f\) matrices are reordered in the proof, so they need not commute. Equality holds exactly when \(X_fC_f^{-1}\) is one common operator. This removes noncommutativity as a candidate failure mode and relocates the real problem to canonical interior identification, singular Ward kernels and analytic rank changes.

See [Matrix-interior Schur covariance needs no commutativity](../0200-0299/267_matrix_interior_schur_covariance_needs_no_commutativity.md).

### 20.180 Ward-singular channels retain positive sewing covariance

If \(C_f\succeq0\) and each coupling satisfies \(X_f=X_fC_f^+C_f\), then positive aggregation preserves the range condition and

\[
\sum_fw_fX_fC_f^+X_f^T-XC^+X^T
=
\sum_fw_f(R_f-\bar R)C_f(R_f-\bar R)^T\succeq0,
\]

with \(R_f=X_fC_f^+\) and \(\bar R=XC^+\). Equality now means alignment on the active supports of the channel pivots. Values on Ward-null complements are physically irrelevant.

This joins two previously separate branches: the Ward quotient is exactly the support condition needed for multi-channel Schur covariance. Fixed degeneracy is harmless; coupling to a null direction or crossing a rank-changing analytic locus is the genuine obstruction.

See [Singular-channel Schur covariance is a Ward-support theorem](../0200-0299/268_singular_channel_schur_covariance_is_a_ward_support_theorem.md).

### 20.181 Rank change is controlled by relative vanishing order

For one analytic pivot eigenvalue \(c(t)\sim at^m\) and projected coupling \(x(t)\sim bt^p\), the eliminated term scales as

\[
\frac{x(t)^2}{c(t)}\sim\frac{b^2}{a}t^{2p-m}.
\]

This yields an exact three-way gate: \(2p<m\) gives a pole, \(2p=m\) gives a finite nonzero analytic remnant that the isolated Moore--Penrose fiber misses, and \(2p>m\) gives a removable zero agreeing with that fiber. Pointwise Ward-range compatibility is therefore necessary but not sufficient across a changing rank.

The equality case is especially relevant to the nested-doll intuition: a disappearing interior carrier and disappearing coupling can leave a finite relational term. It becomes physical only if a concrete Lorentz/Ward-normalized kernel supplies it.

See [Rank-changing Schur channels have a three-way analytic gate](../0200-0299/269_rank_changing_schur_channels_have_a_three_way_analytic_gate.md).

### 20.182 Analytic support rotation changes gluing, not the local Schur gate

For \(C(t)=O(t)D(t)O(t)^T\) and \(X(t)=Y(t)O(t)^T\), orthogonality gives

\[
X(t)C(t)^+X(t)^T=Y(t)D(t)^+Y(t)^T.
\]

Hence an analytic moving eigenframe leaves the local pole/remnant/zero classification unchanged. The twist survives in derivative connections \(O^TdO\), transition functions and global holonomy, not as an extra term in the pointwise Schur norm.

This sharpens the braid/twist intuition: the local Jordan response can remain standard while the carrier's global return map is nontrivial. A common four-channel kernel is then a bundle-intertwining problem rather than a coordinate-alignment problem.

See [Analytic support rotation does not change the Schur rank gate](../0200-0299/270_analytic_support_rotation_does_not_change_the_schur_rank_gate.md).

### 20.183 A two-parameter support defect leaves an exact finite remnant

The polynomial family

\[
C(x,y)=vv^T,
\qquad X(x,y)=bv^T,
\qquad v=(x,y)^T,
\]

has rank one off the origin and rank zero at it. Nevertheless,

\[
XC^+X^T=bb^T
\]

at every punctured point, independent of approach. The pointwise origin fiber gives zero, so family reduction retains information that fiberwise pseudoinversion discards. Meanwhile the support projector winds twice around \(\mathbb RP^1\) and cannot extend through the defect.

This is an exact nested-doll mechanism: carrier and coupling vanish while a finite positive relational form remains. It is only a rank-one Jordan boundary ray, not yet a mass or the full \(Spin(2,3)\) carrier. The new question is whether several canonically oriented defects can span the relational cone.

See [Two-parameter rank collapse leaves a finite relational remnant](../0200-0299/271_two_parameter_rank_collapse_leaves_a_finite_relational_remnant.md).

### 20.184 Three projective relationship rays minimally span the Jordan carrier

For \(b_i=(x_i,y_i)^T\), vectorize \(b_ib_i^T\) as \(q_i=(x_i^2,2x_iy_i,y_i^2)^T\). Then

\[
\det[q_1\ q_2\ q_3]
=2\det(b_1,b_2)\det(b_1,b_3)\det(b_2,b_3).
\]

Hence three pairwise distinct face directions minimally span the three-dimensional space \(H_2(\mathbb R)\). This gives an exact reading of one carrier, two faces and three relationships: the relationship space is \(\operatorname{Sym}^2(\mathbb R^2)\).

Each remnant is only a null boundary ray. Three such rays span by signed combinations, but no finite positive inventory generates the entire round cone. A physical \(Spin(2,3)\) claim still needs a continuous sewing/group orbit, not merely a finite frame.

See [Three relationship rays span the two-face Jordan space](../0200-0299/272_three_relationship_rays_span_the_two_face_jordan_space.md).

### 20.185 Gauge neutrality permits aggregation but does not orient the four channel rays

The dressed endpoint representations are

\[
(\mathbf3,\mathbf1)_4,
\quad(\mathbf3,\mathbf1)_{-2},
\quad(\mathbf1,\mathbf1)_{-6},
\quad(\mathbf1,\mathbf1)_0.
\]

They are pairwise inequivalent, so Schur's lemma gives no nonzero bare gauge-equivariant linear intertwiner between different channels. Each quadratic Gram output is nevertheless neutral and can land in an abstract copy of \(H_2(\mathbb R)_+\).

Thus gauge symmetry supplies a common codomain type but not a canonical relative orientation within that codomain. A three-ray or four-channel frame becomes physical only after common probes, normalizations or Furey/linking intertwiners identify the copies.

See [Gauge symmetry does not orient the four Yukawa remnant rays](../0200-0299/273_gauge_symmetry_does_not_orient_the_four_yukawa_remnant_rays.md).

### 20.186 The real projector defect has an exact fermion-two/stress-eight clutching ladder

For an oriented rank-one real projector define

\[
\zeta(P)=(P_{11}-P_{22})+2iP_{12}.
\]

The radial defect gives \(\zeta=e^{2i\theta}\). Used as an equatorial clutching function, it constructs a complex line over \(S^2\) with \(c_1=2\); its fourth tensor power has \(c_1=8\). Thus

\[
\text{projector degree }2
\longrightarrow
\text{fermion relationship }c_1=2
\xrightarrow{\otimes4}
\text{stress relationship }c_1=8
\]

is an exact topological construction, not bare arithmetic. It is not yet a physical identification: the response-defect base must be related to the celestial momentum sphere, chirality must fix orientation and a nonzero gauge/Lorentz-compatible operator must realize the bundle morphism.

See [The projector defect clutches to the fermion-two and stress-eight ladder](../0200-0299/274_projector_defect_clutches_to_the_fermion_two_and_stress_eight_ladder.md).

### 20.187 The obvious degree-two sphere map is topologically right but rotationally wrong

The extension \(F(z)=z^2\) reproduces the doubled equator and pulls a unit Hopf line back to \(c_1=2\). But it is a branched degree-two map and cannot be equivariant under identical standard \(SO(3)\) actions on source and target; an equivariant self-map must be identity or antipodal.

Moreover, the pulled-back Hopf curvature vanishes at the branch points, unlike the rotationally uniform charge-two monopole curvature. Equal Chern class therefore does not mean equal Berry connection.

The doubled relationship action is valid, but treating its projective sphere as an ordinary spatial-direction sphere is not. A different representation target or dynamical soldering field is required.

See [A degree-two base map matches the Chern class but breaks full rotation equivariance](../0200-0299/275_degree_two_base_map_matches_chern_class_but_breaks_full_rotation_equivariance.md).

### 20.188 Symmetric-square equivariance puts the doubling in the relationship representation

The preferred rotational construction is not \(z\mapsto z^2\) on one sphere but

\[
\nu_2:\mathbb CP^1\hookrightarrow\mathbb CP^2,
\qquad [u:v]\mapsto[u^2:\sqrt2uv:v^2].
\]

It is fully \(SU(2)\)-equivariant into the spin-one symmetric-square representation, unbranched onto its conic image and satisfies \(\nu_2^*\mathcal O(1)=\mathcal O(2)\). The real form is precisely

\[
\operatorname{Sym}^2(\mathbb R^2)\cong H_2(\mathbb R).
\]

Thus two faces and three relationships are not merely a dimension match: the Jordan carrier is the real quadratic relationship representation. The fourth tensor power still produces relationship weight eight. What remains is a statistics-safe physical operator and noncompact response dynamics.

See [The symmetric-square Veronese embedding preserves rotations and relationship doubling](../0200-0299/276_symmetric_square_veronese_embedding_preserves_rotations_and_relationship_doubling.md).

### 20.189 Squaring the three relationships yields determinant singlet plus spin-two fiveplet

With \(W=\operatorname{Sym}^2\mathbb C^2\),

\[
\operatorname{Sym}^2W
\cong
\operatorname{Sym}^4\mathbb C^2\oplus\mathbf1.
\]

The invariant singlet is

\[
\det\begin{pmatrix}a&b\\b&c\end{pmatrix}=ac-b^2,
\]

and the other five components form spin two. Thus the Jordan determinant is exactly the scalar consistency channel left when the relationship triplet is squared.

This explains the recurring singlet/fiveplet pattern and provides a representation-level bridge to the custodial branch. It does not identify the locking scalar with the response carrier or the fiveplet with four-dimensional stress without matching their gauge and dynamical data.

See [The relationship square splits into Jordan determinant and a spin-two fiveplet](../0200-0299/277_the_relationship_square_splits_into_jordan_determinant_and_spin_two_fiveplet.md).

### 20.190 The Veronese representation is physical kinematics before it is a fermion composite

For one local Grassmann Weyl field,

\[
\psi_{(\alpha}\psi_{\beta)}=0.
\]

Two distinct fields can give a nonzero symmetric-spinor bilinear, antisymmetric in their species labels, but gauge neutrality additionally requires their internal representations to contain a singlet. A pair of distinct sterile-neutrino flavors is a limited example; the four charged Yukawa channels do not inherit a universal bare operator.

By contrast, commuting momentum spinors have nonzero \(\lambda^2\) and \(\lambda^4\), so the spin-one/spin-two/helicity-bundle ladder is already valid for polarizations and form factors. This supports the geometry without implying that stress or gravity is a multi-fermion bound state.

See [A statistics-safe Veronese operator requires distinct fermion labels](../0200-0299/278_a_statistics_safe_veronese_operator_requires_distinct_fermion_labels.md).

### 20.191 Spin-two form factors give the weight-eight positive Gram carrier explicitly

The commuting null-spinor quartic

\[
C_{\alpha\beta\gamma\delta}=\lambda_\alpha\lambda_\beta\lambda_\gamma\lambda_\delta
\]

is the five-component spin-two face of weight four. Pairing opposite helicities gives coherence of weight eight. For face amplitudes \((A_+,A_-)\),

\[
G=\begin{pmatrix}A_+\\A_-\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}A_+\\A_-\end{pmatrix}^{\!\dagger}\succeq0,
\]

and positive spectral sums can enter the cone interior. This is the concrete local \(H_2(\mathbb C)\) stress/helicity carrier whose real projection is patchwise positive and whose off-diagonal transition carries Chern eight.

It proves the kinematics and positivity, not a graviton pole or full \(Spin(2,3)\) dynamics.

See [Spin-two curvature form factors realize the weight-eight positive carrier](../0200-0299/279_spin_two_curvature_form_factors_realize_the_weight_eight_positive_carrier.md).

### 20.192 Three sterile flavors give an exact three-operator positive spectral sector

For gauge-singlet Weyl fields \(N_i\),

\[
\mathcal O^{ij}_{\alpha\beta}=N^i_{(\alpha}N^j_{\beta)}
\]

is antisymmetric in \(i,j\). Three flavors therefore supply exactly three independent spin-one operators. Their generic two-particle form factor is nonzero, and its physical spectral cut is a positive sum of two-probe outer products.

This is the first Standard-Model-completion sector with an exact three-relationship operator count and positive response. It is not yet \(H_2(\mathbb R)\): the operators form \(\Lambda^2\mathbb C^3\), a complex flavor antitriplet, so a real structure and physically normalized intertwiner are still required.

See [Three sterile flavors supply three nonzero spin-one pair operators](../0200-0299/280_three_sterile_flavors_supply_three_nonzero_spin_one_pair_operators.md).

### 20.193 Majorana reality supplies three real operators but not the Jordan signature

The sterile antitriplet \(\Lambda^2\mathbb C^3\cong\overline{\mathbf3}\) has no \(SU(3)\)-equivariant real structure, as shown immediately by the center phases. A real Majorana metric can reduce flavor symmetry to \(O(3)\), after which Hodge duality gives a real triplet.

That triplet is Euclidean. Sylvester inertia forbids identifying its \((3,0)\) norm with the \((1,2)\) Jordan determinant by a real change of basis. One further selector axis is necessary:

\[
\eta_n=2nn^T-I.
\]

This creates the split signature and breaks \(O(3)\to O(2)\). The neutrino branch therefore reproduces the programme's central selector problem in an explicit, physically located form.

See [Majorana reality gives a sterile triplet, but a selector must create Jordan signature](../0200-0299/281_majorana_reality_gives_a_sterile_triplet_but_a_selector_must_create_jordan_signature.md).

### 20.194 An isolated real spectral eigenline supplies a non-arbitrary selector

For a real symmetric physical matrix \(K\) with isolated largest eigenvalue \(\kappa_3\),

\[
P_3=\frac{(K-\kappa_1I)(K-\kappa_2I)}
{(\kappa_3-\kappa_1)(\kappa_3-\kappa_2)}
\]

is a basis-covariant rank-one projector. Then \(\eta_K=2P_3-I\) has signature \((1,2)\) and gives the required Jordan split without choosing coordinates by hand.

The eigenvalue gap controls stability. Degeneracy removes the axis, CP phases can make the eigenline nonreal relative to the Majorana conjugation, and the full causal response must preserve or transport the projector. The selector problem is therefore reduced to a concrete spectral and dynamical audit.

See [An isolated real neutrino eigenline gives a covariant, stable Jordan selector](../0200-0299/282_an_isolated_real_neutrino_eigenline_gives_a_covariant_stable_jordan_selector.md).

### 20.195 A fixed selector preserves positivity but removes the boost directions

In a basis with \(P=\operatorname{diag}(1,0,0)\), a symmetric response commuting with \(P\) is \(1\oplus2\) block diagonal. The commutant has dimension four rather than six. Within \(SO(1,2)\), exact selector preservation removes both boosts and leaves only plane rotation; including scale gives

\[
\mathbb R_+\times SO(2).
\]

Positive responses still exist, but this fixed-selector group cannot generate an open cone from one aligned ray. Full carrier exploration must come from independent sources, covariant transport, spontaneous selector dynamics or a larger gauge-redundant parent.

See [Exact selector preservation reduces the response group to scale times rotation](../0200-0299/283_exact_selector_preservation_reduces_the_response_group_to_scale_times_rotation.md).

### 20.196 A transported selector can close projectively with one sign twist

There exist real symmetric response loops with a fixed nonzero eigenvalue gap for which

\[
n(2\pi)=-n(0),
\qquad
P(2\pi)=P(0),
\qquad
\eta(2\pi)=\eta(0).
\]

The selected eigenline is Möbius, with \(w_1=1\). The Jordan signature and unoriented double cone are global, but a future orientation is not. In a moving frame the connection integrates to a half-turn, providing an exact version of a looped carrier with one twist.

This is compatible with covariant selector transport but forces a double cover, compensating sign bundle or restriction of the physical parameter domain.

See [A gapped selector projector can be global while time orientation has one twist](../0200-0299/284_a_gapped_selector_projector_can_be_global_while_time_orientation_has_one_twist.md).

### 20.197 A spinorial root can orient the selector product but cannot cancel Chern eight

If the selector eigenline and a spinor/sign line both have \(w_1=1\) over the same loop, then

\[
w_1(L_{\rm sel}\otimes L_{\rm spin})=1+1=0.
\]

Their \(-1\) holonomies cancel, giving an oriented tensor product. This requires a physical pullback to the same base loop and a locking morphism; matching signs alone is insufficient.

The mechanism is strictly mod two. It does not cancel \(c_1=8\in H^2(S^2;\mathbb Z)\), whose parity is trivial while the integral class remains nonzero. Time-orientation compensation and celestial relationship compensation are separate gates.

See [A spinor sign line can cancel selector orientation but not Chern eight](../0200-0299/285_a_spinor_sign_line_can_cancel_selector_orientation_but_not_chern_eight.md).

### 20.198 A common selector survives positive sector aggregation without full commutativity

Let several sector matrices share one rank-one projector \(P\) but have noncommuting dynamics in its orthogonal plane. If each selected eigenvalue exceeds the largest plane eigenvalue by \(\delta_a>0\), then a positive sum has gap

\[
\delta_{\rm sum}\geq\sum_aw_a\delta_a>0.
\]

Thus a universal selector needs a common invariant line, not simultaneous diagonalization of all response sectors. However, one integrated moment can commute with \(P\) by accidental cancellation even when the spectral density does not. The strong target is pointwise common-projector closure after physically derived cross-sector intertwiners.

See [Common selector lines survive positive spectral sums without full commutativity](../0200-0299/286_common_selector_lines_survive_positive_spectral_sums_without_full_commutativity.md).

### 20.199 The three triplet branches are isomorphic only after selection, with a residual torsor

The Furey real block and stress two-probe carrier are copies of \(H_2(\mathbb R)\). The sterile Hodge triplet becomes determinant-isometric to them only after Majorana reality and a split selector:

\[
(t,x,y)\mapsto
\begin{pmatrix}t+x&y\\y&t-x\end{pmatrix}.
\]

Thus compatible linear isomorphisms exist. They are not canonical: fixing the time line leaves an \(SO(2)\) plane rotation, implemented by a half-angle face congruence, while general determinant-preserving face changes form an \(SL(2,\mathbb R)\) torsor.

A genuine synthesis now requires shared physical probes or operators to fix this torsor and make the Jordan, positive-cone, selector, dynamical, gauge/Ward and normalization squares commute.

See [The three triplet branches admit isomorphisms but not yet a canonical intertwiner](../0200-0299/287_the_three_triplet_branches_admit_isomorphisms_but_not_yet_a_canonical_intertwiner.md).

### 20.200 Flavor noncommutativity can leak out of the real face under inversion

Factor-local reality is not automatically inverse closed. A positive operator

\[
M=aI+b\,\sigma_x\otimes\tau_x+c\,\sigma_z\otimes\tau_z
\]

is fixed by face partial transpose, but its inverse generically contains

\[
\delta\,\sigma_y\otimes\tau_y,
\qquad \delta\neq0,
\]

which is face-transpose odd. More generally the leakage is proportional to flavor commutators attached to different face directions.

Thus real faces and complex flavor CP coexist kinematically, but Schur/Jordan recursion additionally requires an inverse-closed coefficient algebra, flavor-central pivots, a graded selector or controlled passage through the complex parent carrier.

See [Noncommuting flavor kernels can break real-face closure under Schur inversion](../0200-0299/288_noncommuting_flavor_kernels_can_break_real_face_closure_under_schur_inversion.md).

### 20.201 The minimal graded-real inverse closure is a 21-dimensional parent

Pairing transpose parities gives

\[
(\operatorname{Sym}_2\otimes\operatorname{Sym}_n)
\oplus
(\operatorname{Alt}_2\otimes\operatorname{Alt}_n)
=
\operatorname{Sym}_{2n}(\mathbb R).
\]

For three flavors this is \(H_6(\mathbb R)\), dimension \(18+3=21\). It is positive-inverse and Schur closed and contains the correlated antisymmetric leakage excluded by simple face reality.

The external \(H_2(\mathbb R)\) can survive after unweighted flavor trace because the odd flavor coefficients are traceless. The cost is a much larger interacting parent, whose extra modes and CP content require physical control. Exact three-dimensional closure is therefore not generic once noncommuting flavor dynamics enter the inverted pivots.

See [The inverse-closed graded-real escape is the full combined real-symmetric algebra](../0200-0299/289_the_inverse_closed_graded_real_escape_is_the_full_combined_real_symmetric_algebra.md).

### 20.202 Graded realification can retain a nonzero flavor CP invariant

A complex Hermitian flavor matrix \(H=A+iB\) realifies as

\[
R(H)=\begin{pmatrix}A&-B\\B&A\end{pmatrix}\in H_6(\mathbb R),
\]

commuting with \(J=\bigl(\begin{smallmatrix}0&-I\\I&0\end{smallmatrix}\bigr)\). For the explicit CP-violating pair,

\[
-\frac12\operatorname{Tr}\left(J[R_u,R_d]^3\right)=36.
\]

Physical conjugation is a different involution \(K\) with \(KJ=-JK\), and the CP-violating response is not \(K\)-invariant. Thus real parent matrices do not erase CP when the complex structure is retained. Even reductions hide the odd sector; graded probes can expose it.

See [Flavor CP survives the graded-real parent when the complex structure is retained](../0200-0299/290_flavor_cp_survives_the_graded_real_parent_when_the_complex_structure_is_retained.md).

### 20.203 Positive flavor reduction does not inherit parent dynamics

Normalized flavor trace \(E\) preserves positivity and the unit, but an explicit centered correlation satisfies

\[
E(X)=0,\qquad E(X\circ X)=I\neq0=E(X)\circ E(X).
\]

Likewise \(E(M^{-1})\neq E(M)^{-1}\). Consequently the external \(H_2(\mathbb R)\) carrier is not an automatic Jordan quotient of the full \(H_6(\mathbb R)\) parent, and the parent's \(Sp(12,\mathbb R)\) structure does not automatically descend to \(Spin_0(2,3)\). Exact descent needs an invariant subalgebra or factor-central pivots; otherwise eliminated flavor correlations reappear as causal self-energy and memory.

See [Flavor trace is positive but does not transmit parent Jordan or Schur dynamics](../0200-0299/291_flavor_trace_is_positive_but_does_not_transmit_parent_jordan_or_schur_dynamics.md).

### 20.204 A gap turns the external carrier into a controlled approximation

For

\[
M=A\otimes I+\varepsilon V,\qquad A\geq\mu I,\qquad E(V)=0,
\]

the first-order hidden correction vanishes and

\[
\left\|E(M^{-1})-A^{-1}\right\|
\leq
\frac{\varepsilon^2\|V\|^2}{\mu^2(\mu-|\varepsilon|\|V\|)}.
\]

This supplies the missing middle position between exact symmetry inheritance and uncontrolled truncation. External \(Spin(2,3)\) can govern a reduced response to quantified accuracy if the Standard-Model/Furey sector supplies the gap and centering. As the denominator closes, the carrier description predicts its own failure and must be replaced by the full parent or an energy-dependent open-system response.

See [A flavor gap makes the external \(H_2(\mathbb R)\) carrier a controlled second-order approximation](../0200-0299/292_flavor_gap_makes_the_external_h2r_carrier_a_controlled_second_order_approximation.md).

### 20.205 Causality descends even when the Jordan algebra does not

For a self-adjoint parent \(H\), the reduced resolvent

\[
G(z)=E\big((H-zI)^{-1}\big),\qquad \operatorname{Im}z>0,
\]

has \(\operatorname{Im}G(z)\geq0\): positive flavor reduction preserves the matrix Herglotz condition. Yet generally \(G(z)\neq(E(H)-zI)^{-1}\). With a centered hidden perturbation, the mismatch obeys

\[
\left\|G(z)-(A-zI)^{-1}\right\|
\leq\frac{\varepsilon^2\|V\|^2}{(\operatorname{Im}z)^3}.
\]

The external carrier can therefore inherit causal response without inheriting the full microscopic Jordan product. The exact two-state model makes the cost visible: a single reduced pole is really a positive average of two parent poles. This turns hidden flavor structure into a concrete spectral-resolution and memory question.

See [Herglotz reduction preserves causality while hiding second-order memory](../0200-0299/293_h_erglotz_reduction_preserves_causality_while_hiding_second_order_memory.md).

### 20.206 Flavor complex structure cannot silently double as the full face carrier

The realification complex structure

\[
J=\begin{pmatrix}0&-I_3\\I_3&0\end{pmatrix}
\]

uses the same two-dimensional block index previously called the external face. Exact \([M,J]=0\) restricts symmetric \(6\times6\) responses to

\[
\operatorname{Sym}_6(\mathbb R)\cap\operatorname{Cent}(J)
\cong H_3(\mathbb C).
\]

Every positive flavor-state reduction of this subspace is proportional to \(I_2\). The \(\sigma_x\) and \(\sigma_z\) directions needed for a full \(H_2(\mathbb R)\) carrier break the shared-index complex-linearity. Thus the CP-realification result remains valid, but it cannot simultaneously furnish the entire external carrier without extra structure.

The clean repair makes the factors independent:

\[
\mathbb R^2_{\rm face}\otimes\mathbb R^6_{\rm flavor-realification},
\qquad J_{\rm total}=I_2\otimes J_{\rm flavor}.
\]

Then all three face directions commute with flavor \(J\), at the cost of a potentially much larger \(H_{12}(\mathbb R)\) ambient response. This makes the missing intertwiner hypothesis explicit rather than hiding it in notation.

See [Exact flavor complex structure collapses the shared face reduction to a scalar](../0200-0299/294_exact_flavor_complex_structure_collapses_the_shared_face_reduction_to_a_scalar.md).

### 20.207 Independent factors close on a complex parent and regenerate \(Spin(2,4)\)

The independent-factor repair has a tighter closure than all of \(H_{12}(\mathbb R)\):

\[
M_2(\mathbb R)\otimes_{\mathbb R}M_3(\mathbb C)
\cong M_6(\mathbb C),
\]

with self-adjoint Jordan part \(H_6(\mathbb C)\), dimension 36. Positive flavor trace maps this parent onto all of

\[
H_2(\mathbb C)=\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb R}
\{I,\sigma_x,\sigma_y,\sigma_z\},
\]

because \(\sigma_y\otimes I_3\) lies in the natural associative envelope. Thus separating face from flavor complex structure resolves the CP conflation but produces a complex carrier one rung above the desired real form:

\[
H_6(\mathbb C)
\longrightarrow H_2(\mathbb C)
\longrightarrow H_2(\mathbb R),
\]

or geometrically \(SU(6,6)\to Spin_0(2,4)\to Spin_0(2,3)\). The remaining problem is now exactly one-dimensional: remove or gap the \(\sigma_y\) response without conjugating away flavor CP.

See [Independent face and complex flavor close naturally on \(H_6(\mathbb C)\), not all of \(H_{12}(\mathbb R)\)](../0200-0299/295_independent_face_and_complex_flavor_close_naturally_on_h6c_not_h12r.md).

### 20.208 The real-form selector is a reduced operation, not parent partial transpose

Real-type antiunitary involutions of \(H_2(\mathbb C)\) fix rotated copies of \(H_2(\mathbb R)\) and remove one Bloch direction. The embeddings form an unoriented \(\mathbb{RP}^2\) family. Quaternionic square-(-1\) antiunitaries fix only the scalar ray.

A face-only lift to the entangled face–flavor parent is partial transpose. Its action on a Bell state has eigenvalue \(-1/2\), so it is not a positive global reduction. Global conjugation is positive but conjugates flavor matrices and can erase CP. The consistent order is therefore

\[
H_6(\mathbb C)
\xrightarrow{\text{positive causal reduction}}
H_2(\mathbb C)
\xrightarrow{\text{real-form selection}}
H_2(\mathbb R),
\]

unless a more structured microscopic mechanism is supplied.

See [The real-form selector is valid after reduction but not as face-only partial transpose](../0200-0299/296_the_real_form_selector_is_valid_after_reduction_but_not_as_face_only_partial_transpose.md).

### 20.209 A dynamical selector realizes the next-rung Goldstone idea

If the real-form embedding is dynamical, its order parameter is a director \([n]\in\mathbb{RP}^2\). An isotropic potential has Hessian eigenvalues

\[
0,\quad0,\quad2\lambda v^2,
\]

so choosing \(Spin(2,3)\) inside the complex carrier produces two orientation modes. Gauging eats them and leaves a local \(SO(2)\); explicit anisotropy gives both a mass \(\kappa\). The global topology \(\pi_1=\mathbb Z_2\), \(\pi_2=\mathbb Z\) permits twisted line and point sectors, but does not by itself turn them into particles or braids.

This is the first exact realization of the proposed “Goldstone modes on the next holonomy rung”: the statement now has a specified orbit, spectrum and falsifiers.

See [A dynamical real-form selector has \(\mathbb{RP}^2\) order parameter and two orientation modes](../0200-0299/297_a_dynamical_real_form_selector_has_rp2_order_parameter_and_two_orientation_modes.md).

### 20.210 Stress supplies a covariant selector only through a physical channel triplet

If three carrier-valued stress channels exist, their Lorentz-scalar Gram matrix

\[
Q_{ab}=T_a^{\mu\nu}T_{b\mu\nu}
\]

can select the \(\mathbb{RP}^2\) director by an isolated eigenline. For eigenvalues \(q_1<q_2\leq q_3\), the two orientation masses are

\[
m_2^2=\kappa(q_2-q_1),
\qquad
m_3^2=\kappa(q_3-q_1).
\]

This is Lorentz scalar and converts spectral isolation directly into selector stability. But the total Standard-Model stress tensor is an internal singlet. It cannot produce a nonzero \(O(3)\) director equivariantly. The construction therefore advances the stress branch while exposing its precise missing arrow:

\[
\text{Furey/Jordan response}
\stackrel{?}{\longrightarrow}
\{T_a^{\mu\nu}\}_{a=1}^3
\longrightarrow Q_{ab}
\longrightarrow[n].
\]

Calling gauge, Higgs and fermion stresses a triplet does not fill that arrow without a transformation and renormalization theorem.

See [Stress can select the \(\mathbb{RP}^2\) director only after a physical channel triplet exists](../0200-0299/298_stress_can_select_the_rp2_director_only_after_a_physical_channel_triplet_exists.md).

### 20.211 The \(AXB\) left/right/cross data become a triplet through the linking face matrix

Furey’s TRO places left products, right products and relationships in different linking corners. They become one covariant object only as

\[
\mathbb T^{\mu\nu}=
\begin{pmatrix}T_{LL}^{\mu\nu}&T_{LR}^{\mu\nu}\\
T_{RL}^{\mu\nu}&T_{RR}^{\mu\nu}\end{pmatrix}
=T_0^{\mu\nu}I+T_a^{\mu\nu}\sigma_a.
\]

The trace is a singlet; the three Pauli coefficients form the required \(SO(3)\) triplet. Their stress Gram matrix can select the real-form director before reduction. At the response level,

\[
\det\begin{pmatrix}\ell&c\\\bar c&r\end{pmatrix}
=t_0^2-t_x^2-t_y^2-t_z^2,
\]

so the construction naturally begins at \(H_2(\mathbb C)\). Removing the derived normal then gives the \(H_2(\mathbb R)\) determinant.

The remaining Standard-Model obstruction is sharp: \(T_{LR}\) connects representations with different electroweak charges and is not generally observable without Higgs/Yukawa dressing. If Furey’s cyclic Higgs orientation supplies that unique dressing, three previously separate branches would lock at once.

See [Left, right and cross stress form a triplet only as the Pauli part of a face matrix](../0200-0299/299_left_right_and_cross_stress_form_a_triplet_only_as_the_pauli_part_of_a_face_matrix.md).

### 20.212 The minimal physical cross channel is Yukawa dressed but not separately conserved

Gauge neutrality fixes the dimension-four cross operators

\[
\bar Q_LHd_R,
\quad
\bar Q_L\widetilde Hu_R,
\quad
\bar L_LHe_R,
\quad
\bar L_L\widetilde H\nu_R.
\]

This exactly matches the up/down orientation found in Furey’s cyclic branch, but gauge quantum numbers alone already enforce it. The Yukawa contribution to Hilbert stress is metric proportional,

\[
T_Y^{\mu\nu}=-g^{\mu\nu}\mathcal L_Y,
\]

and its complex quadratures are not separately conserved. For one classical background their relationship-plane Gram has rank one; a chiral phase redefinition rotates its axis. Thus the bare Yukawa term supplies a legal cross insertion but not a canonical real-form selector.

The next viable object is the full three-channel connected spectral matrix, including population difference, both relationship quadratures, Higgs/gauge contact terms and Ward completion. Furey becomes predictive only if its cyclic action fixes more than the already-required charge dressing.

See [The minimal gauge-neutral cross stress is Yukawa-dressed but not independently conserved](../0300-0399/300_the_minimal_gauge_neutral_cross_stress_is_yukawa_dressed_but_not_independently_conserved.md).

### 20.213 Exact rephasing selects a different real form than entrywise reality

After the conserved-source quotient, a positive three-channel spectral moment can be written as a sum of positive residues. Exact relative-face rephasing rotates \((T_x,T_y)\) and forces

\[
Q=\operatorname{diag}(q_\perp,q_\perp,q_z).
\]

It cannot choose one real/imaginary relationship quadrature. If \(q_z\neq q_\perp\), it can instead choose the population normal. The resulting fixed algebra is

\[
\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb R}\{I,\sigma_x,\sigma_y\}
=\left\{
\begin{pmatrix}t&x-iy\\x+iy&t\end{pmatrix}
\right\}
\cong H_2(\mathbb R),
\]

with determinant \(t^2-x^2-y^2\). This real form is algebraically valid but enforces equal diagonal populations. The familiar entrywise-real carrier keeps \(\sigma_z\) and instead removes \(\sigma_y\); it therefore needs a phase-breaking or covariantly transforming Higgs/Furey spurion.

This is a productive fork: either the physical carrier really is population-normal, or the mechanism selecting an off-diagonal phase direction must be exhibited. Flavor CP scalars alone cannot provide that charged direction.

See [Rephasing-invariant positive spectra can select only the population axis](../0300-0399/301_rephasing_invariant_positive_spectra_can_select_only_the_population_axis.md).

### 20.214 Continuous charge does not forbid every \(H_2(\mathbb R)\) embedding

The fixed-real-line theorem excludes the entrywise-real carrier because a charged complex relationship has no invariant real line. Over the full selector family, however, relative-face \(U(1)\) uniquely preserves the population normal. Exchange conjugation

\[
\Theta=\sigma_xK
\]

fixes

\[
J_z=left\{
\begin{pmatrix}t&z\\\bar z&t\end{pmatrix}
\right\}
=\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb R}\{I,\sigma_x,\sigma_y\}
\cong H_2(\mathbb R).
\]

The charged relation \(z\mapsto e^{iq\phi}z\) stays entirely inside this algebra and rotates its two spacelike coordinates. The determinant \(t^2-|z|^2\) is preserved. The escape is exact, but it removes \(\sigma_z\): both face populations are equal.

The programme therefore has two inequivalent physical real forms. Entrywise reality retains population imbalance but needs phase dressing; population-normal reality retains continuous charge but loses independent populations. Determining which coordinates actual stress and Furey probes measure is now more important than choosing a convenient matrix basis.

See [Continuous charge selects the population-normal \(H_2(\mathbb R)\) embedding](../0300-0399/302_continuous_charge_selects_the_population_normal_h2r_embedding.md).

### 20.215 Furey survivor exchange is exactly the charge-compatible selector on the completed carrier

The two surviving Furey TRO topologies obey

\[
\Theta_{\rm ex}(v_A,v_B)
=(\bar v_B,\bar v_A)
=\sigma_xK(v_A,v_B).
\]

On Hermitian observables of the survivor pair, its fixed algebra is

\[
\operatorname{Fix}(\Theta_{\rm ex})
=\left\{\begin{pmatrix}t&c\\\bar c&t\end{pmatrix}\right\}
=J_z\cong H_2(\mathbb R).
\]

The equality of diagonal populations follows from \(v_B=\bar v_A\), while complex relationship data survive. Relative \(U(1)\) acts inside this algebra. Consequently the completed Furey carrier and the unique charge-compatible real-form selector now meet exactly:

\[
\text{survivor exchange}
\Longrightarrow J_z
\Longrightarrow Sp(4,\mathbb R)\cong Spin_0(2,3).
\]

This is currently the strongest algebraic Furey–\(Spin(2,3)\) bridge compatible with continuous charge. Its limitation is equally exact: the exchange is emergent on the completed carrier, not an automorphism of the native real division-algebra source, and the survivor pair has not yet been operationally identified with the external stress faces.

See [Furey survivor exchange induces the charge-compatible population-normal real form](../0300-0399/303_furey_survivor_exchange_induces_the_charge_compatible_population_normal_real_form.md).

### 20.216 Exchange-fixed amplitudes supply the positive causal carrier directly

For survivor amplitudes \((a,b)\), define

\[
\Gamma(a,b)=
\begin{pmatrix}\langle a,a\rangle&\langle a,b\rangle\\
\langle b,a\rangle&\langle b,b\rangle\end{pmatrix}\geq0.
\]

The map intertwines antiunitaries:

\[
\Gamma(Cb,Ca)=\sigma_x\overline{\Gamma(a,b)}\sigma_x.
\]

For an exchange-fixed pair \(b=Ca\),

\[
\Gamma(a,Ca)=
\begin{pmatrix}\|a\|^2&\langle a,Ca\rangle\\
\overline{\langle a,Ca\rangle}&\|a\|^2\end{pmatrix}
\in J_z^+,
\]

with determinant \(\|a\|^4-|\langle a,Ca\rangle|^2\geq0\). Positive spectral sums and their upper-half-plane resolvents preserve both the exchange-fixed real form and Herglotz sign.

This fills positivity, selector and causal squares in the previously open intertwiner diagram. The surviving gap is operational rather than algebraic: derive \(a\) from gauge-neutral Ward-quotiented physical probes and show exchange holds pointwise under renormalization.

See [Exchange-fixed survivor amplitudes compress to a positive \(H_2(\mathbb R)\) spectral carrier](../0300-0399/304_exchange_fixed_survivor_amplitudes_compress_to_a_positive_h2r_spectral_carrier.md).

### 20.217 Furey exchange can retain three-family CP through its complex structure

For flavor observables \(H\), the exchange-fixed doubled form is

\[
\mathcal D(H)=\operatorname{diag}(H,\bar H).
\]

The ordinary doubled CP trace cancels:

\[
\operatorname{Tr}[\mathcal D(H_u),\mathcal D(H_d)]^3=0.
\]

But the exchange also preserves

\[
\mathcal J=\operatorname{diag}(iI_3,-iI_3),
\qquad \mathcal J^2=-I_6,
\]

and

\[
-\frac12\operatorname{Tr}
\left(\mathcal J[\mathcal D(H_u),\mathcal D(H_d)]^3\right)
=-i\operatorname{Tr}[H_u,H_d]^3.
\]

For the explicit test pair this equals 36. Thus the Furey exchange-fixed presentation is real without erasing complex flavor orientation. CP becomes a graded internal observable rather than an external carrier coordinate. The next physical gate is whether actual gauge-invariant CP asymmetries insert \(\mathcal J\), and whether the exchange-fixed Fock theory is chiral rather than vectorlike.

See [Three-family CP survives Furey exchange pairing as a complex-structure-graded invariant](../0300-0399/305_three_family_cp_survives_furey_exchange_pairing_as_a_complex_structure_graded_invariant.md).

### 20.218 Exchange breaking is directly measurable population imbalance

The sole Hermitian direction outside the population-normal carrier is \(\sigma_z\). For

\[
G= tI+x\sigma_x+y\sigma_y+\delta\sigma_z,
\]

\[
\det G=(t^2-x^2-y^2)-\delta^2,
\qquad
\mathcal A=\frac{G_{11}-G_{22}}{G_{11}+G_{22}}=\frac\delta t.
\]

Thus exchange breaking appears linearly in face-population asymmetry but quadratically in the Jordan determinant. Positivity gives the exact tolerance

\[
|\delta|\leq\sqrt{\det G_0};
\]

rank-one boundary carriers tolerate none. The result cleanly separates \(\sigma_z\), which polarizes and breaks the survivor pair, from \(\mathcal J=i\sigma_z\), which is anti-Hermitian and remains exchange invariant as the CP grading.

This provides a radiative gate: exact exchange forbids the imbalance counterterm pointwise; an integrated cancellation is not enough because resolved spectral channels can retain opposite splittings.

See [Exchange breaking is population imbalance and reduces the Jordan determinant quadratically](../0300-0399/306_exchange_breaking_is_population_imbalance_and_reduces_the_jordan_determinant_quadratically.md).

### 20.219 The response selector is not the fermionic adjoint

The same-charge survivor exchange

\[
\Theta_{\rm sel}=sK_0
\]

correctly fixes the population-normal Gram response, but coefficient conjugation reverses gauge phase while the target survivor retains the original charge. It therefore cannot be the ordinary gauge-equivariant CAR adjoint.

The self-dual Fock construction requires

\[
\mathcal K=K\oplus\bar K,
\qquad
\Gamma_{\rm CAR}(v,\bar w)=(w,\bar v),
\]

with conjugate gauge and Lorentz action. Furey’s source-derived \(C_F\) supplies that conjugation conditionally, so the candidate is \(\Gamma_{\rm CAR}=sC_F\), not bare \(sK_0\).

For \(\dim_{\mathbb C}K=15\), the doubled self-dual carrier has dimension 30 but a rank-15 basis projection. It therefore represents 15 independent annihilation modes and Fock dimension \(2^{15}\). Quantizing both halves independently would give \(2^{30}\) and a real mirror problem.

The architecture now has two noninterchangeable antiunitaries: one selects the external Jordan response; the other defines particle/adjoint reality. A common completed module carrying both is the next stop-everything target.

See [The response selector and the CAR adjoint are two distinct antiunitaries](../0300-0399/307_the_response_selector_and_the_car_adjoint_are_two_distinct_antiunitaries.md).

### 20.220 Two real structures either grade the carrier or generate its complex orientation

Let \(A^2=B^2=1\) be the response and CAR antiunitaries. Their product \(C=AB\) is linear. If they commute, \(C^2=+1\) and it is a grading. If they anticommute, \(C^2=-1\) and it is a complex structure.

For the candidates

\[
\Theta_{\rm sel}=sK_0,
\qquad
\Gamma_{\rm CAR}=sC_F,
\]

the product is the linear difference \(K_0C_F\) between coefficient conjugation and physical gauge/Lorentz conjugation. A common basis has not yet been constructed, so the commutation sign is unknown.

This creates a sharp fork. Anticommutation could derive the CP-retaining \(\mathcal J\) from the two reality structures; commutation would instead produce a chirality/survivor grading and leave \(\mathcal J\) as independent data. No KO dimension or spectral-triple identification is warranted until the kinetic operator and complete sign table are present.

See [Two real structures generate either a grading or a complex structure](../0300-0399/308_two_real_structures_generate_either_a_grading_or_a_complex_structure.md).

### 20.221 Anomaly freedom cannot prove the conjugate half is not a mirror

One Standard-Model generation is anomaly free, and its independent conjugate mirror is separately anomaly free. Their direct sum still has vanishing \(U(1)^3\), mixed gravitational, mixed non-Abelian and \(SU(3)^3\) anomalies. The weak-doublet count changes from four to eight, but both pass the Witten parity test.

The distinction appears elsewhere. A self-dual CAR carrier has a rank-15 basis projection and \(2^{15}\) finite-mode Fock dimension. An independent mirror has 30 annihilation modes and \(2^{30}\) states. It also doubles the one-generation fermion contributions

\[
(\Delta b_1,\Delta b_2,\Delta b_3)
=\left(\frac{20}{9},\frac43,\frac43\right)
\]

above its threshold. Consequently anomaly-free Furey TROs remain necessary, but anomaly cancellation cannot close the mirror question. The operator adjoint relation and basis projection are primary.

See [Anomaly cancellation cannot distinguish a CAR adjoint from an independent mirror generation](../0300-0399/309_anomaly_cancellation_cannot_distinguish_a_car_adjoint_from_an_independent_mirror_generation.md).

### 20.222 The selector pair and Nambu pair cannot be independent tensor factors

Starting from a 15-complex-dimensional chiral generation, self-dual CAR already uses

\[
\mathcal K=K\oplus\bar K,
\qquad \dim_{\mathbb C}\mathcal K=30,
\]

with a rank-15 basis projection. Tensoring an additional two-state survivor-selector factor gives dimension 60 and leaves 30 independent annihilation modes after the CAR projection. That is an extra generation or mirror sector.

The minimal kinetic reference is

\[
H_{\rm BdG}=\operatorname{diag}(h,-\bar h),
\]

which obeys

\[
\Gamma_{\rm CAR}H_{\rm BdG}\Gamma_{\rm CAR}^{-1}=-H_{\rm BdG},
\qquad
\Gamma_{\rm CAR}P\Gamma_{\rm CAR}=1-P.
\]

Accordingly, \(\Theta_{\rm sel}\) and \(\Gamma_{\rm CAR}\) must be realized on the same 30-dimensional carrier, or Furey/Jordan structure must select a canonical rank-30 subspace of the naive 60-dimensional product. This converts the vague “common completion” request into explicit matrix equations for \(P,H\) and both real structures.

See [Tensoring the selector pair with the Nambu pair overcounts the generation](../0300-0399/310_tensoring_the_selector_pair_with_the_nambu_pair_overcounts_the_generation.md).

### 20.223 The common-carrier problem reduces to one relative unitary

On \(K\oplus\bar K\) with standard CAR involution \(\Gamma=\tau_xK_0\), every second polarization-reversing real structure is

\[
\Theta_W=
\begin{pmatrix}0&W\\W^T&0\end{pmatrix}K_0,
\qquad W\in U(K).
\]

Their product is \(\operatorname{diag}(W,W^T)\). Hermitian \(W\) produces the commuting grading branch; anti-Hermitian \(W\) produces the anticommuting complex-structure branch. For

\[
H_{\rm BdG}(h)=\operatorname{diag}(h,-\bar h),
\]

the selector is a kinetic symmetry exactly when \(WhW^\dagger=-h\). If \(\dim K\) is odd, this forces \(\det h=0\). The broad common-intertwiner problem has therefore collapsed to deriving one relative unitary and its action on gauge, Lorentz, Yukawa and momentum data.

See [A second polarization-reversing real structure is parameterized by one unitary](../0300-0399/311_a_second_polarization_reversing_real_structure_is_parameterized_by_one_unitary.md).

### 20.224 The 15-state grading locates the forced zero mode at the neutrino

Without \(\nu^c\), one generation has eight weak-doublet components and seven singlet conjugates. Its Higgs/Yukawa mass operator is

\[
H_Y=\begin{pmatrix}0&M_{8\times7}\\M^\dagger&0\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
W=\operatorname{diag}(I_8,-I_7),
\]

so \(WH_YW^\dagger=-H_Y\). Rank-nullity forces at least one doublet-side zero mode, generically the neutrino after charged fermions are massive. Three generations force at least three.

Adding one \(\nu^c\) balances the sectors at \(8+8\) and permits a full Dirac gap. A Majorana or Weinberg block instead connects the doublet sector to itself, breaks the grading and lifts the zero. This recovers the existing 15-versus-16-state neutrino fork as the physical realization of the common-carrier odd-dimension theorem.

See [The fifteen-state Yukawa grading forces one neutrino zero mode per generation](../0300-0399/312_the_fifteen_state_yukawa_grading_forces_one_neutrino_zero_mode_per_generation.md).

### 20.225 The forced neutrino zero extends to a massless Clifford cone

Let \(\alpha_i,\beta\) satisfy the Dirac Clifford relations and define

\[
H(p)=\alpha\cdot p\otimes I_{15}+\beta\otimes M_Y,
\qquad
S=\beta\otimes W.
\]

Since \(\{\alpha_i,\beta\}=0\) and \(\{W,M_Y\}=0\),

\[
\{S,H(p)\}=0.
\]

On the unmatched neutrino vector \(M_Yv_\nu=0\),

\[
H(p)^2=|p|^2,
\]

so the static rank defect becomes a massless relativistic cone. A balanced \(8+8\) Dirac completion gaps it while preserving the grading; a Majorana/Weinberg block gaps it by breaking the grading.

This is the first exact Lorentz-symbol extension of the common-carrier zero-mode theorem. It remains conditional at field-theory level: Furey’s Lorentz factor must supply the Clifford matrices without introducing vectorlike mirrors, and gauge covariance, locality and the CAR projection must be verified.

See [The Yukawa zero mode extends to a massless Dirac-type cone](../0300-0399/313_the_yukawa_zero_mode_extends_to_a_massless_dirac_type_cone.md).

### 20.226 A fixed quarter-turn identifies the wall and Furey positive carriers

The finite domain-wall response naturally occupies

\[
J_y=\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb R}\{I,\sigma_x,\sigma_z\},
\]

whereas the exchange-fixed Furey survivor response occupies

\[
J_z=\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb R}\{I,\sigma_x,\sigma_y\}.
\]

They are related by the exact unitary

\[
U_x=\exp\!\left(-\frac{i\pi}{4}\sigma_x\right),
\qquad U_xJ_yU_x^\dagger=J_z.
\]

This map preserves the Jordan determinant, the positive cone, residue rank, Herglotz positivity and Schur-complement sewing. In particular, every real rank-one wall residue \(pp^T\) becomes an equal-population exchange ray \(U_xpp^TU_x^\dagger\), and ordinary conjugation becomes the Furey exchange antiunitary up to phase.

The algebraic bridge is therefore complete at response level. Its physical gate is phase resolution: \(U_x\) forms quadratures with relative phase \(\pi/2\), so actual equivalence requires coherent probes, a selector connection or boundary conditions that implement the rotation.

See [A quarter-turn maps the real domain-wall carrier to the population-normal Furey carrier](../0300-0399/314_a_quarter_turn_maps_the_real_domain_wall_carrier_to_the_population_normal_furey_carrier.md).

### 20.227 The quarter-turn is transverse to the surviving charge \(U(1)\)

The real-form embeddings are selector directors \([n]\in\mathbb{RP}^2\). The quarter-turn is the orbit motion

\[
R_x(\pi/2):[e_y]\longmapsto[e_z].
\]

It is not in the connected stabilizer of either endpoint. The retained Furey complex structure \(i\sigma_z\) generates rotations about \(e_z\), so it fixes the population-normal real form and cannot generate \(U_x\). The bridge therefore requires the broken generator \(i\sigma_x\), not the surviving \(U(1)_z\).

This clarifies the “next-rung Goldstone” proposal: the exact map aligning the wall and Furey carriers is one of the two selector orientation directions. Depending on realization it is a Goldstone or pseudo-Goldstone field, an eaten gauge direction, a selector holonomy, or a boundary quadrature—not automatically a new bulk particle.

The next decisive calculation is to derive \(i\sigma_x\) and its quarter-turn from stress transport, Furey multiplication or boundary dynamics while preserving chirality and positivity.

See [The carrier quarter-turn is a broken selector direction, not the surviving \(U(1)\)](../0300-0399/315_the_carrier_quarter_turn_is_a_broken_selector_direction_not_the_surviving_u1.md).

### 20.228 The one-twist selector loop, not the quarter-turn, is the zero-mode candidate

For a minimal one-dimensional Dirac operator whose mass angle follows the selector,

\[
H=-i\sigma_x\partial_x+
m(\cos\theta\,\sigma_z+\sin\theta\,\sigma_y),
\]

a sharp angular interface has

\[
\kappa=m\sin\frac{\Delta\theta}{2},
\qquad
|E|=m\left|\cos\frac{\Delta\theta}{2}\right|.
\]

The wall-to-Furey quarter-turn \(\Delta\theta=\pi/2\) therefore binds a subgap state at \(|E|=m/\sqrt2\), not an exact zero. The exact zero occurs at a lifted half-turn \(\Delta\theta=\pi\).

This half-turn has a distinctive selector meaning. It joins \(n\) to \(-n\) upstairs on \(S^2\), but those endpoints are the same director in \(\mathbb{RP}^2\); it is the nontrivial \(\mathbb Z_2\) loop, precisely the rigorous version of a “loop with one twist.”

There is also a non-negotiable bundle gate. A fermion mass linear in \(n\) changes sign under \(n\mapsto-n\), so it descends to the director space only if a fermionic transition function compensates that sign. The promising synthesis target is now exact: derive this holonomy from the Furey/CAR action and show that it acts on the unmatched \(8+7\) neutrino state. Until then, the internal rank zero and the spatial topological zero are two separate mechanisms.

See [The quarter-turn binds a subgap state while the \(\mathbb{RP}^2\) half-turn can bind a zero](../0300-0399/316_the_quarter_turn_binds_a_subgap_state_while_the_rp2_half_turn_can_bind_a_zero.md).

### 20.229 The one-twist bundle lift is uniquely exchange-shaped on the selector circle

For the great-circle mass

\[
M(n)=m(n_y\sigma_y+n_z\sigma_z),
\]

descent under the director identification requires an involution \(g\) satisfying

\[
gM(n)g^{-1}=-M(n).
\]

In two components the unique solution up to sign is

\[
g=\pm\sigma_x.
\]

This is the same matrix that exchanges the Furey survivor faces and generates the wall-to-Furey quarter-turn. Exchange, selector transport and antipodal bundle gluing are therefore controlled by one explicit matrix.

The operations remain distinct: the full antiunitary \(\sigma_xK\) does not act like unitary \(\sigma_x\) on a generic great-circle mass. Moreover, no two-component matrix flips all three Pauli masses. Full \(\mathbb{RP}^2\) motion needs a doubled lift such as \(\tau_x\otimes I\), which is admissible only if the \(\tau\) factor is the already existing CAR/Nambu polarization rather than a new mirror copy.

See [The selector great circle has a unique exchange bundle lift, but full \(\mathbb{RP}^2\) requires doubling](../0300-0399/317_the_selector_great_circle_has_a_unique_exchange_bundle_lift_but_full_rp2_requires_doubling.md).

### 20.230 A graded joint operator localizes one forced neutrino zero per generation

The spatial and internal zero mechanisms can be combined rather than compared. Let

\[
D_{\rm w}=-i\sigma_x\partial_x+m(x)\sigma_z,
\qquad
C_{\rm w}=\sigma_y,
\]

and let \(H_Y\) be the \(8+7\) Yukawa mass operator. Define

\[
\mathcal D=D_{\rm w}\otimes I+C_{\rm w}\otimes H_Y.
\]

Then

\[
\mathcal D^2=D_{\rm w}^2\otimes I+I\otimes H_Y^2,
\qquad
\ker\mathcal D=\ker D_{\rm w}\otimes\ker H_Y.
\]

An index-one sign wall and three-generation \(8+7\) Yukawa complex therefore give exactly three joint zeros: one localized forced neutrino per generation.

This theorem is grading-sensitive. A smooth selector rotation introduces a mass component proportional to \(C_{\rm w}\), breaks \(\{C_{\rm w},D_{\rm w}\}=0\), and destroys the sum-of-squares proof. Keeping a zero during full selector motion requires an enlarged Clifford factor or connection supplied by existing Lorentz/Nambu/Furey structure.

See [The graded wall–Yukawa sum localizes exactly one forced zero per generation](../0300-0399/318_the_graded_wall_yukawa_sum_localizes_exactly_one_forced_zero_per_generation.md).

### 20.231 Gauge transport preserves the deck lift but adds a Yukawa-gradient gate

On two identical gauge representations,

\[
G_{\rm deck}=\sigma_x\otimes I_{15}
\]

commutes with the complete Standard-Model gauge action. The unitary bundle lift therefore avoids the charge-reversal obstruction that applies to the antiunitary response selector \(\sigma_xK\).

For the covariant joint operator

\[
\mathcal D_A=
-i\sigma_x\nabla_x+m(x)\sigma_z+\sigma_yH_Y(x),
\]

direct expansion gives

\[
\mathcal D_A^2=
D_{\rm w,A}^2+H_Y^2+\sigma_z\nabla_xH_Y
\]

up to derivative sign convention. The exact kernel factorization survives when \(H_Y\) is covariantly constant, including transport in the unbroken Higgs stabilizer. A generic Higgs texture or broken-direction electroweak connection produces a cross term and requires a genuine index or spectral-flow calculation.

The next question is therefore not whether the deck lift can carry charge—it can—but whether the unmatched neutrino kernel is parallel under the Furey-derived Higgs/gauge connection.

See [Gauge covariance preserves the deck lift, but Yukawa transport controls kernel factorization](../0300-0399/319_gauge_covariance_preserves_the_deck_lift_but_yukawa_transport_controls_kernel_factorization.md).

### 20.232 The textured operator retains an integer AIII index

Although \(\nabla_xH_Y\ne0\) destroys the simple square factorization, it need not destroy zero-mode protection. Combine the wall and internal gradings:

\[
\mathscr S=C_{\rm w}\otimes W.
\]

If gauge transport commutes with \(W\) and all Dirac Yukawa terms remain off-diagonal under \(W\), then

\[
\{\mathscr S,\mathcal D_A\}=0
\]

for the full textured operator. Generic complex flavor phases leave class AIII, whose product index is

\[
\operatorname{ind}\mathcal D_A
=\nu_{\rm w}(8-7)N_g=N_g.
\]

For three supplied generations, generic nonfactorizing AIII textures therefore preserve a net three zero modes even though their wavefunctions no longer factor into wall and internal pieces. Dirac completion balances the internal index; Majorana blocks or transverse wall masses break the grading and can gap it.

See [The textured joint operator has a three-generation AIII index beyond kernel factorization](../0300-0399/320_the_textured_joint_operator_has_a_three_generation_aiii_index_beyond_kernel_factorization.md).

### 20.233 The present topology protects three but does not derive three

The equality \(\operatorname{ind}\mathcal D=3\) uses three copies of the \(8+7\) complex. It is not yet a generation theorem.

The selector bundle contributes only

\[
[E_{N_g}]=N_g\pmod2,
\]

so it cannot distinguish one, three and five. Perturbative Standard-Model anomalies cancel independently in each generation, and the Witten condition sees \(4N_g\) weak doublets, which is even for every \(N_g\).

The current construction therefore transports and protects a supplied generation multiplicity. Deriving three still requires an intrinsically rank-three mechanism—most plausibly a canonical exceptional-Jordan, arithmetic-orbit or flavor-monodromy construction that produces exactly three complete \(8+7\) complexes without inserting a flavor triplet.

See [Selector topology, anomalies and the AIII index do not by themselves select three generations](../0300-0399/321_selector_topology_anomalies_and_the_aiii_index_do_not_by_themselves_select_three_generations.md).

### 20.234 Triality supplies three overlapping choices of one exceptional generation

The strongest exceptional generation proposal realizes one \(16\)-complex \(Spin(10)\) generation as the tangent

\[
(\mathbb C\otimes\mathbb O)^2
\]

of the complex octonionic projective plane. In the magic-square decomposition, three \(16\)-real modules \(A,B,C\) give three tangent choices

\[
T_A=B\oplus C,\qquad
T_B=C\oplus A,\qquad
T_C=A\oplus B.
\]

Each tangent has the correct \(32\) real dimensions, but every pair intersects in one \(16\)-real module and their total span is \(48\), not \(96\), real dimensions. Triality therefore gives three equivalent choices of one generation, not three independent generation spaces.

The nested \(H_2(\mathbb C)\) flag further splits the three frame edges as \(1+2\). It also reveals a neutrino tension: the exceptional tangent is a completed \(16=8+8\) and has zero AIII imbalance, whereas the forced-zero Furey branch uses \(15=8+7\).
