See [Triality gives three overlapping generation choices, not three independent generations](../0300-0399/322_triality_gives_three_overlapping_generation_choices_not_three_independent_generations.md).

### 20.235 Quantizing the triality orbit creates a candidate flavor carrier

The overlap can be repaired by quantizing sections over the three-element orbit

\[
\Omega=S_3/S_2,
\qquad
\mathcal H_{\rm gen}=V_{16}\otimes\mathbb C[\Omega].
\]

This genuinely gives three independent \(16\)-complex fibers. Its flavor representation is the permutation module

\[
\mathbb C^3=\mathbf1\oplus\mathbf2.
\]

Exact \(S_3\) forces invariant Yukawa operators to have form \(aI+bJ\), producing a degenerate doublet and mutually commuting flavor squares. The nested flag reduces to \(S_2\), which removes generic degeneracy but leaves one common flavor eigenline and still kills the three-family Jarlskog invariant.

The viable sequence must therefore be

\[
S_3\longrightarrow S_2\longrightarrow1.
\]

The orbit supplies a canonical candidate flavor carrier, but quantizing its sheets and deriving the final breaking are additional physical steps.

See [Quantizing the triality orbit gives three flavor sheets, but exact \(S_3\) or \(S_2\) forbids observed mixing](../0300-0399/323_quantizing_the_triality_orbit_gives_three_flavor_sheets_but_exact_s3_or_s2_forbids_observed_mixing.md).

### 20.236 The minimal final breaking is a complex sheet doublet

In the residual \(S_2\) parity basis \(\mathbb C^3=E_+\oplus E_-\) with dimensions \(2+1\), the smallest odd Hermitian spurion is

\[
\Delta(z)=
\begin{pmatrix}
0&z\\
z^\dagger&0
\end{pmatrix},
\qquad z\in\mathbb C^2.
\]

For one flavor square diagonal and the other with even-plane mixing \(r\), the CP invariant is

\[
\operatorname{Tr}[H_u,H_d]^3
\propto
i\,r\,\operatorname{Im}(z_2\bar z_1).
\]

Both odd components, a relative complex phase, nondegenerate masses and even-plane misalignment are necessary. The exceptional branch is thus reduced to deriving one complex \(S_2\)-odd doublet with nonzero oriented area, rather than an arbitrary \(3\times3\) matrix.

See [A single complex \(S_2\)-odd doublet is the minimal triality-breaking source for three-family CP](../0300-0399/324_a_single_complex_s2_odd_doublet_is_the_minimal_triality_breaking_source_for_three_family_cp.md).

### 20.237 The triality orbit contains one canonical sign cubic

For the three-sheet permutation representation \(P=\mathbb C^3\),

\[
\operatorname{Sym}^3(P^*)
\cong3\mathbf1\oplus\mathbf1_{\rm sign}\oplus3\mathbf2.
\]

The unique sign cubic is

\[
\Delta_{\rm tri}
=(x_1-x_2)(x_2-x_3)(x_3-x_1).
\]

On the flag locus \(x_1=x_2=a,\ x_3=b\), it vanishes but has odd transverse derivative

\[
\left.\partial_\delta\Delta_{\rm tri}\right|_{\delta=0}
=-2(a-b)^2.
\]

Thus the nested flag supplies \(S_3\to S_2\), while the unique sign cubic supplies a canonical final \(S_2\)-breaking direction. This sheet parity remains distinct from the antiunitary parity of \(\operatorname{Im}\det Z\), and a triality-equivariant map between the two cubics is still required.

See [The triality orbit has a unique sign cubic, but it does not yet fix the CP doublet](../0300-0399/325_the_triality_orbit_has_a_unique_sign_cubic_but_it_does_not_yet_fix_the_cp_doublet.md).

### 20.238 The flag and retained complex structure complete a CP-capable odd operator

The unit, flag and sign gradient canonically select

\[
s=\frac{(1,1,1)}{\sqrt3},
\qquad
t=\frac{(1,1,-2)}{\sqrt6},
\qquad
o=\frac{(1,-1,0)}{\sqrt2}.
\]

The two canonical odd Hermitian maps are

\[
A=|s\rangle\langle o|+\mathrm{h.c.},
\qquad
B=i(|t\rangle\langle o|-\mathrm{h.c.}).
\]

For

\[
\Delta_*=\alpha A+\beta B,
\]

the odd flavor doublet is

\[
z=(\alpha,i\beta),
\qquad
\operatorname{Im}(z_2\bar z_1)=\alpha\beta.
\]

The triality orbit, nested flag, unique sign cubic and Furey-retained complex orientation therefore enter one exact CP-capable operator. The directions are canonical, but the two real scales \(\alpha,\beta\), their ratio and their relation across fermion sectors remain dynamical.

See [The flag, sign gradient and complex structure build a canonical CP-capable odd operator](../0300-0399/326_the_flag_sign_gradient_and_complex_structure_build_a_canonical_cp_capable_odd_operator.md).

### 20.239 The polarized exceptional determinant gives the sign cubic a complex coefficient

For three complement fields define

\[
F_Z(x)=\det(x_1Z_1+x_2Z_2+x_3Z_3).
\]

The canonical alternating projector gives

\[
\mathcal A_{\rm sign}F_Z
=c(Z_1,Z_2,Z_3)\Delta_{\rm tri}(x).
\]

The coefficient is a definite combination of polarized determinants,

\[
c=\frac12(-D_{112}+D_{113}+D_{122}-D_{133}-D_{223}+D_{233}).
\]

It obeys

\[
c\mapsto-c
\]

under sheet transposition and

\[
c\mapsto\bar c
\]

under exceptional antiunitary conjugation. Therefore

\[
\Delta(c)=\operatorname{Re}c\,A+\operatorname{Im}c\,B
\]

is the canonical CP-capable odd operator, with area \(\operatorname{Re}c\,\operatorname{Im}c\). The two real coefficients are now quadratures of one exceptional invariant, though the physical \(Z_i\) backgrounds and phase of \(c\) remain unpredicted.

See [The polarized exceptional determinant projects canonically onto the triality sign cubic](../0300-0399/327_the_polarized_exceptional_determinant_projects_canonically_onto_the_triality_sign_cubic.md).

### 20.240 Three-sheet CAR counting works, but selector lifting remains sector-dependent

The quantized orbit carrier has

\[
K=V_{16}\otimes\mathbb C^3,
\qquad \dim_{\mathbb C}K=48,
\]

and self-dual CAR completion \(K\oplus\bar K\) has \(96\) complex coordinates but only \(48\) independent annihilation modes.

Triality permutations are real and compatible with CAR. However, the unitary Nambu swap sends \(\rho\oplus\bar\rho\) to \(\bar\rho\oplus\rho\) and fails gauge equivariance on charged sectors; only the antiunitary CAR map repairs it. The residual exchange of two identical triality sheets is unitary and gauge-equivariant, but three sheets cannot be paired without one fixed sheet.

The consistent architecture therefore separates CAR conjugation, identical-sheet selector exchange and neutral-sector Nambu lifting. Their coexistence on one completed carrier remains the next construction.

See [The three-sheet CAR count is consistent, but the charged Nambu swap cannot be the full-selector lift](../0300-0399/328_the_three_sheet_car_count_is_consistent_but_the_charged_nambu_swap_cannot_be_the_full_selector_lift.md).

### 20.241 The same exceptional phase controls the Dirac/Majorana neutrino fork

With \(c=\alpha+i\beta\), the Hermitian Dirac sheet operator obeys

\[
\Delta_D^3=|c|^2\Delta_D
\]

and has eigenvalues \(0,\pm|c|\). Adding \(m_DI\) gives three generic Dirac levels and completes each generation to \(8+8\), making the AIII index zero without breaking its grading.

The Majorana insertion must instead be complex symmetric:

\[
M_-(c)=
\begin{pmatrix}
0&0&\alpha\\
0&0&i\beta\\
\alpha&i\beta&0
\end{pmatrix}.
\]

Alone it has Takagi singular values \((|c|,|c|,0)\). Adding the flag-even block gives

\[
\det M_R
=M_sM_tM_o+M_s\beta^2-M_t\alpha^2-M_or^2
+2ir\alpha\beta.
\]

Thus the same CP area that orients flavor also removes the sterile zero when the even mixing \(r\) is present. This Majorana route breaks the AIII grading rather than balancing it.

See [The exceptional cubic phase splits Dirac completion from Majorana index breaking](../0300-0399/329_the_exceptional_cubic_phase_splits_dirac_completion_from_majorana_index_breaking.md).

### 20.242 The exceptional Majorana phase is a closed three-projector invariant

Let \(P_e,P_\mu,P_\tau\) be charged-lepton spectral projectors and

\[
X_a=P_a^*MP_aM^\dagger.
\]

Then

\[
\boxed{
\mathcal I_\triangle
=-\operatorname{ImTr}(X_eX_\mu X_\tau)}
\]

is weak-basis invariant. In the charged-lepton frame it becomes

\[
\operatorname{Im}
\left[
M_{e\mu}M_{\mu\tau}M_{\tau e}
M_{ee}^*M_{\mu\mu}^*M_{\tau\tau}^*
\right].
\]

For the exceptional texture,

\[
\mathcal I_\triangle
=rM_sM_tM_o\operatorname{Re}c\,\operatorname{Im}c.
\]

Every pairwise Majorana quartet may vanish while this closed triple remains nonzero. The phase is therefore relationally three-body: each edge appears real or CP-trivial in isolation, but their loop has nonzero orientation.

See [The exceptional Majorana phase has a weak-basis three-projector triangle invariant](../0300-0399/330_the_exceptional_majorana_phase_has_a_weak_basis_three_projector_triangle_invariant.md).

### 20.243 Majorana CP is the obstruction to globally realifying three local \(Spin(2,3)\) edges

In the charged-lepton spectral frame define

\[
r_{ij}=\sqrt{M_{ii}M_{jj}}\,M_{ij}^*.
\]

The square-root signs act as vertex \(\mathbb Z_2\) gauge choices, while general flavor rephasings act by

\[
r_{ij}\mapsto e^{i(\theta_i-\theta_j)}r_{ij}.
\]

The closed loop is gauge invariant and satisfies

\[
\boxed{
\mathcal I_\triangle=-\operatorname{Im}(r_{12}r_{23}r_{31}).}
\]

Each principal two-port face can be rephased into \(H_2(\mathbb R)_+\), so each edge separately carries the local conformal symmetry

\[
Sp(4,\mathbb R)\cong Spin_0(2,3).
\]

All three faces admit one common real gauge if and only if

\[
\arg(r_{12}r_{23}r_{31})\in\pi\mathbb Z.
\]

Thus nonzero Majorana CP is precisely the obstruction to gluing the three local real carriers into one \(H_3(\mathbb R)\) object. The minimal global parent is instead \(H_3(\mathbb C)\).

If the third port is Schur-eliminated, with direct edge \(u=r_{12}\) and indirect path \(q=\bar r_{31}\bar r_{23}/c\), then

\[
\operatorname{Im}(u\bar q)
=\frac{1}{c}\operatorname{Im}(r_{12}r_{23}r_{31}).
\]

The global holonomy therefore survives local reduction as direct-versus-indirect path interference. A positive static completion is exact; a passive causal spectral realization and phase-resolved flavor-port protocol remain open.

See [Majorana CP is the holonomy obstructing three local Spin(2,3) edges from one global real carrier](../0300-0399/331_majorana_cp_is_the_holonomy_obstructing_three_local_spin23_edges_from_one_global_real_carrier.md).

### 20.244 Two positive spectral directions are the minimum for oriented causal gluing

A positive three-port residue (R\) immediately defines the passive causal response

\[
G(z)=\frac{R}{s_0-z},
\qquad
\operatorname{Im}G(z)\succeq0
\quad(\operatorname{Im}z>0).
\]

There is, however, a sharp spectral-rank gate. If (R=aa^\dagger\), then

\[
R_{12}R_{23}R_{31}=|a_1a_2a_3|^2\in\mathbb R_{\ge0}.
\]

One positive spectral direction cannot orient the three-port loop. Two suffice: for

\[
a=(1,1,1)^T,
\qquad
b=(1,i,2+i)^T,
\]

the rank-two residue (aa^\dagger+bb^\dagger\) has loop (12+4i\). A nondegenerate strict realization is

\[
G(z)=\frac{aa^\dagger}{2-z}
+\frac{bb^\dagger}{3-z}
+\frac{I_3}{5-z},
\]

whose edge loop at (z=0\) is

\[
\frac{157}{216}+\frac{5}{18}i.
\]

This closes the mathematical passive-causality gate and identifies the orientation as irreducibly cross-mode interference. The physical flavor-port and Standard-Model production/detection maps remain open.

See [Two spectral modes are the minimum for causal three-port orientation](../0300-0399/332_two_spectral_modes_are_the_minimum_for_causal_three_port_orientation.md).

### 20.245 The aligned seesaw transmits the exceptional phase only away from a cofactor zero

For

\[
M_R=
\begin{pmatrix}
S&r&a\\
r&T&ib\\
a&ib&O
\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
m_\nu=-v^2Y_DM_R^{-1}Y_D^T,
\]

take (Y_D=\operatorname{diag}(y_1,y_2,y_3)\) real. If

\[
D=\det M_R=STO+Sb^2-Ta^2-Or^2+2irab,
\]

then the light Majorana triangle is

\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathcal I_\nu
={}&\frac{v^{12}(y_1y_2y_3)^4}{|D|^6}
(TO+b^2)(SO-a^2)(ST-r^2)\\
&\times arb\,[Sb^2-r^2O-STO-a^2T].
\end{aligned}
\]

The real aligned Yukawas only rescale the invariant positively, but inversion adds cofactor-path interference. In particular,

\[
Sb^2-r^2O-STO-a^2T=0
\]

is a transmission-zero hypersurface. The heavy exceptional triangle can remain nonzero there while the light triangle vanishes. Exceptional CP therefore crosses the seesaw generically, not topologically; every phenomenological claim needs the explicit noncancellation condition.

See [The exceptional phase crosses the aligned seesaw but has a transmission zero](../0300-0399/333_the_exceptional_phase_crosses_the_aligned_seesaw_but_has_a_transmission_zero.md).

### 20.246 Unrestricted complex Yukawas erase seesaw phase predictivity

Factor any nonsingular complex symmetric heavy matrix as

\[
M_R=RR^T
\]

and any desired symmetric light congruence as (N=LL^T\). Choosing

\[
Y_D=LR^T
\]

gives

\[
Y_DM_R^{-1}Y_D^T=N.
\]

Hence a general invertible complex Dirac matrix makes the type-I seesaw map surjective onto nonsingular complex symmetric light textures. In particular, (Y_D=R^T\) erases an arbitrarily CP-oriented heavy matrix to (m_\nu\propto I\), while (M_R=I\) and complex (Y_D\) can manufacture arbitrary light CP.

The exceptional heavy phase is predictive only after the theory fixes the relative congruence frame of (Y_D\) and (M_R\). This elevates the Furey/exceptional intertwiner space from a representation-theory detail to the decisive physical gate.

See [General complex Yukawas make the type-I seesaw congruence surjective](../0300-0399/334_general_complex_yukawas_make_the_type_i_seesaw_congruence_surjective.md).

### 20.247 Exceptional CP is the incompatibility of two quarter-turned \(H_2(\mathbb R)\) carriers

The residual-(S_2\) odd vector selected by the exceptional determinant is

\[
z=(\alpha,i\beta)^T
=Q(\alpha,\beta)^T,
\qquad
Q=\operatorname{diag}(1,i).
\]

Its real plane (Q\mathbb R^2\) has complex-linear stabilizer

\[
QM_2(\mathbb R)Q^{-1},
\]

whose Hermitian part is the quarter-turned Jordan carrier

\[
QH_2(\mathbb R)Q^\dagger.
\]

Both this cone and the original (H_2(\mathbb R)\) cone have conformal group (Sp(4,\mathbb R)\cong Spin_0(2,3)\), but

\[
H_2(\mathbb R)\cap QH_2(\mathbb R)Q^\dagger
=\{\text{real diagonal matrices}\}.
\]

For an original real block (H=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}S&r\\r&T\end{smallmatrix}\right)\),

\[
Q^\dagger Hz
=
\begin{pmatrix}
S\alpha+ir\beta\\
T\beta-ir\alpha
\end{pmatrix}.
\]

The exceptional plane is preserved only when (r\beta=r\alpha=0\), whereas the Majorana orientation is proportional to (r\alpha\beta\). Nonzero CP therefore measures the incompatibility of two valid local real carriers, rather than a phase appended to one carrier.

See [The exceptional CP doublet exposes two incompatible \(H_2(\mathbb R)\) real forms](../0300-0399/335_the_exceptional_cp_doublet_exposes_two_incompatible_h2r_real_forms.md).

### 20.248 The triple cannot select the quarter-turn, but the pair of realities generates the flag

For the Hermitian triple

\[
\{A,B,C\}=\tfrac12(AB^\dagger C+CB^\dagger A),
\]

every unitary conjugation is a triple automorphism. Hence (H_2(\mathbb R)\) and (QH_2(\mathbb R)Q^\dagger\), with (Q=\operatorname{diag}(1,i)\), have identical intrinsic Jordan data. The triple alone cannot select their relative quarter-turn.

Let (\kappa_0=K\) fix (\mathbb R^2\), and let (\kappa_Q=QKQ^{-1}\) fix (Q\mathbb R^2\). Then

\[
\boxed{
\kappa_Q\kappa_0
=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1)
=\Gamma.}
\]

The relative quarter-turn is therefore retained as the flag grading produced by the two antiunitary realities. Diagonal operators are (\Gamma\)-even and relational off-diagonal operators are (\Gamma\)-odd.

This closes the algebraic loop while leaving the physical selection problem honest: the programme must derive a second gauge-compatible real structure from CAR, stress response or boundary dynamics.

See [The Jordan triple cannot choose the quarter-turn, but two real structures generate the flag](../0300-0399/336_the_jordan_triple_cannot_choose_the_quarter_turn_but_two_real_structures_generate_the_flag.md).

### 20.249 The second reality exists in gauge multiplicity space, but CP must break it

For a gauge representation \(\rho\), an antiunitary \(J=UK\) is gauge equivariant exactly when

\[
U\bar\rho(g)U^\dagger=\rho(g).
\]

On a charged self-dual CAR carrier, the standard particle/adjoint reality supplies one such map. A second one differs by a unitary \(W\) in the gauge commutant. For two identical sheets,

\[
W=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1)
\]

is gauge equivariant and its product with the CAR reality is the flag grading. Gauge-neutral sterile flavor space also admits this construction directly. Multiplicity-one complex irreps do not.

Generic misaligned Yukawa matrices reduce their common family commutant to scalar phases, so the flag cannot remain an exact symmetry of realistic flavor mixing. In the exceptional Majorana texture, ordinary generalized CP requires \(\beta=0\), while the quarter-turned generalized CP requires \(r=0\). Therefore

\[
\mathcal I_\triangle\propto r\alpha\beta\ne0
\]

measures complementary breaking of the two available realities. The second antiunitary is a gauge-compatible kinematic reference structure, not an unbroken symmetry of the CP-violating mass matrix.

See [The flag antiunitary lives in the gauge multiplicity commutant, and CP breaks it](../0300-0399/337_the_flag_antiunitary_lives_in_the_gauge_multiplicity_commutant_and_cp_breaks_it.md).

### 20.250 Triality selects the multiplicity-space reality grading uniquely up to sign

The three-sheet permutation carrier decomposes multiplicity-freely:

\[
\mathbb C^3=\mathbf1\oplus\mathbf2.
\]

Let \(s=(1,1,1)^T/\sqrt3\) and \(P_s=|s\rangle\langle s|\). Schur’s lemma implies every \(S_3\)-equivariant Hermitian involution is a sign on each irreducible summand. Apart from \(\pm I\), the only possibility is

\[
\boxed{
W=P_s-(I-P_s)=2P_s-I}
\]

and its overall negative. It has eigenvalues \(+--\) on the canonical basis \((s,t,o)\). The nested flag selects \(t\) and the sign-cubic gradient selects \(o\) inside the negative doublet.

For the canonical CP operators,

\[
A=|s\rangle\langle o|+\mathrm{h.c.},
\qquad
B=i(|t\rangle\langle o|-\mathrm{h.c.}),
\]

one finds

\[
\bar A=A,\quad WAW=-A,
\qquad
\bar B=-B,\quad WBW=B.
\]

Thus triality resolves the algebraic choice of the second reality inside the gauge commutant, while a complex exceptional coefficient combines two complementary breaking characters. What remains undetermined is the dynamics fixing the quadrature coefficients.

See [Triality selects a unique singlet–doublet reality grading up to sign](../0300-0399/338_triality_selects_a_unique_singlet_doublet_reality_grading_up_to_sign.md).

### 20.251 The three-port holonomy has an exact quadrature lock-in observable

Let \(u=r_{12}\) be the direct edge and

\[
q=\frac{\bar r_{31}\bar r_{23}}{c}
\]

the indirect path through the Schur-eliminated third port. Apply a controllable phase \(\phi\) to the indirect path. The coherent intensity is

\[
I(\phi)=|u-e^{i\phi}q|^2.
\]

The two quadrature settings isolate the oriented interference:

\[
\boxed{
I(-\pi/2)-I(+\pi/2)
=4\operatorname{Im}(u\bar q).}
\]

Since

\[
\operatorname{Im}(u\bar q)
=\frac1c\operatorname{Im}(r_{12}r_{23}r_{31}),
\]

the loop follows from a calibrated intensity difference. The observable is invariant under independent port rephasings and reverses under complex conjugation.

This closes the abstract measurement protocol for a coherent passive response network. It does not make ordinary neutrino oscillations sensitive to Majorana phases: a neutrino implementation requires a coherent lepton-number-violating production–propagation–detection channel.

See [A quadrature lock-in protocol measures the three-port Schur holonomy](../0300-0399/339_a_quadrature_lockin_protocol_measures_the_three_port_schur_holonomy.md).

### 20.252 The textured AIII defect has a conditional continuum Fredholm theorem

For the physical one-dimensional wall, the total \(\mathscr S=C_{\rm w}\otimes W\) fibers are balanced:

\[
\operatorname{rank}\mathcal K_+
=\operatorname{rank}\mathcal K_-
=15N_g.
\]

The continuum index is therefore not the finite toy model’s rank imbalance. It is the analytic index of the wall. Under bounded Hermitian \(W\)-odd Yukawa textures, grading-compatible gauge transport, nonzero wall-mass limits and coefficient convergence at both ends, the asymptotic symbol satisfies

\[
\mathcal D_\pm(k)^2
=k^2+m_\pm^2+H_{Y,\pm}^2.
\]

Thus the essential gap is at least \(\min(|m_-|,|m_+|)\). Vanishing coefficient differences are relatively compact, so the chiral block is Fredholm. Scaling the bounded Yukawa texture to zero preserves both the gap and AIII symmetry, yielding

\[
\boxed{
\operatorname{ind}_{\mathscr S}\mathcal D
=\nu_{\rm w}(\dim V_+-\dim V_-)
=\nu_{\rm w}N_g.}
\]

For a sign wall and three supplied generations, the index is three. Dirac completion changes \(8+7\) to \(8+8\) and balances it; Majorana mass breaks the grading. The remaining question is physical: whether the Furey/Standard-Model action supplies the required spacetime wall and analytic domain.

See [The textured AIII operator is Fredholm when the wall mass stays gapped at infinity](../0300-0399/340_the_textured_aiii_operator_is_fredholm_when_the_wall_mass_stays_gapped_at_infinity.md).

### 20.253 A scalar kink realizes the Fredholm wall, but the selector supplies a loop instead

The real scalar theory

\[
\mathcal L_\phi
=\tfrac12(\partial\phi)^2-\tfrac\lambda4(\phi^2-v^2)^2
\]

has the exact kink

\[
\phi(x)=v\tanh\!\left(v\sqrt{\lambda/2}\,x\right),
\]

with zero normal pressure and tension

\[
\tau=\frac{2\sqrt{2\lambda}}3v^3.
\]

The Dirac mass \(m(x)=g\phi(x)\) supplies the nonzero asymptotic gaps required by the Fredholm theorem and binds the normalizable profile

\[
\psi_0(x)\propto\cosh(\kappa x)^{-gv/\kappa}.
\]

But this is a genuine wall because \(\{-v,+v\}\) has nontrivial \(\pi_0\). The selector has vacuum space \(\mathbb{RP}^2\), where \(n\sim-n\) and \(\pi_0=0\). Its half-turn is instead the nontrivial class in

\[
\pi_1(\mathbb{RP}^2)=\mathbb Z_2.
\]

The minimal smooth selector loop uses a transverse mass and breaks the fixed AIII grading in its interior. The physical programme therefore needs either a genuine disconnected scalar already present in the theory or a larger grading-preserving Clifford/CAR lift of the selector loop.

See [A \(\phi^4\) field generates the Fredholm wall, but the \(\mathbb{RP}^2\) selector requires a loop lift](../0300-0399/341_a_phi4_field_generates_the_fredholm_wall_but_the_rp2_selector_requires_a_loop_lift.md).

### 20.254 A concrete LNV amplitude carries the Majorana triangle

Same-sign weak-boson scattering through Majorana-neutrino exchange has flavor kernel

\[
\boxed{
F_{\alpha\beta}(q^2)
=\sum_iU_{\alpha i}U_{\beta i}
\frac{m_i}{q^2-m_i^2}.}
\]

Its closed six-amplitude invariant

\[
\mathcal I_F
=\operatorname{Im}\!\left[
F_{e\mu}F_{\mu\tau}F_{\tau e}
F_{ee}^*F_{\mu\mu}^*F_{\tau\tau}^*
\right]
\]

is charged-flavor rephasing invariant. At spacelike \(q^2=-Q^2\),

\[
F(-Q^2)
=-\frac{M_\nu^*}{Q^2}+O(Q^{-4}),
\]

so

\[
\boxed{
\mathcal I_F(-Q^2)
=-\frac{\mathcal I_{M_\nu}}{Q^{12}}
+O(m_{\max}^2Q^{-14}).}
\]

The amplitude-level bridge therefore exists. Each isolated channel rate is still invariant under complex conjugation, so orientation requires coherent cross-flavor phase tomography or an equivalent reference-amplitude network. Ordinary oscillations and one diagonal \(0\nu\beta\beta\) rate do not reconstruct the triangle.

See [Same-sign weak-boson scattering carries the Majorana triangle at amplitude level](../0300-0399/342_same_sign_weak_boson_scattering_carries_the_majorana_triangle_at_amplitude_level.md).

### 20.255 A minimal exceptional-coefficient potential fixes maximal quadrature mixing, but symmetry does not

The known transformations \(c\mapsto-c\) and \(c\mapsto\bar c\) permit

\[
V_{\rm min}
=\lambda(|c|^2-v^2)^2
+\kappa\left[(\operatorname{Re}c)^2-(\operatorname{Im}c)^2\right]^2.
\]

For \(\lambda,\kappa>0\), its vacua satisfy

\[
\boxed{
|\operatorname{Re}c|
=|\operatorname{Im}c|
=\frac{v}{\sqrt2},
\qquad
\arg c=\frac\pi4+\frac{n\pi}{2}.}
\]

The CP-area magnitude is \(v^2/2\), while the radial and phase-locking Hessian eigenvalues are \(8\lambda v^2\) and \(8\kappa v^2\).

However, the general symmetry-allowed quartic contains \(c^2+c^{*2}\), \(|c|^2(c^2+c^{*2})\) and \(c^4+c^{*4}\). Its nontrivial phase obeys

\[
\cos2\theta
=-\frac{b+\kappa_1\rho^2}{4\eta\rho^2},
\]

so the vacuum angle moves continuously. Equal quadratures require a restricted coefficient locus or an additional arithmetic/dynamical principle. Moreover, because \(c\) is cubic in complement fields, \(V(c)\) is an effective rather than renormalizable microscopic potential.

See [A minimal exceptional-coefficient potential fixes equal CP quadratures, but not uniquely](../0300-0399/343_a_minimal_exceptional_coefficient_potential_fixes_equal_cp_quadratures_but_not_uniquely.md).

### 20.256 Integrality alone does not quantize the exceptional phase

If \(c\) lies in a full rank-two lattice in \(\mathbb C\), the slopes of primitive lattice vectors are dense on the projective line. Therefore

\[
\boxed{
c\text{ integral}
\not\Rightarrow
\arg c\text{ belongs to a finite set}.}
\]

In the Gaussian model, norm-one units are \(\pm1,\pm i\) and have zero CP area. By contrast,

\[
N(c)=2
\]

has exactly the orbit

\[
\boxed{
c\in\{\pm1\pm i\},}
\]

which reproduces the equal-quadrature phases of the minimal potential. Norm five already gives unequal quadratures. Arithmetic predictivity therefore requires a derived norm shell or finite automorphism orbit, not mere integrality.

Because the polarized determinant and alternating projector introduce denominators, even the coefficient lattice must first be calculated for a specific integral exceptional order.

See [Integrality does not quantize \(\arg c\), but a norm-two orbit would](../0300-0399/344_integrality_does_not_quantize_arg_c_but_a_norm_two_orbit_would.md).

### 20.257 The full selector is locally four-component but globally graded only after a minimal double

A full selector requires five pairwise anticommuting complex Clifford generators:

\[
\alpha=\sigma_x\otimes I,\qquad
\beta_a=\sigma_z\otimes\sigma_a,\qquad
C=\sigma_y\otimes I.
\]

This four-component module preserves a fixed local grading for every \(n\in S^2\). The antipodal deck lift \(G_4=\alpha\) satisfies

\[
[G_4,\alpha]=0,\qquad
G_4\beta_aG_4^{-1}=-\beta_a,
\]

but

\[
\boxed{G_4CG_4^{-1}=-C.}
\]

No alternative four-component operator can both preserve \(C\) and flip all three selector masses. An eight-component lift resolves the obstruction:

\[
\beta_{a,8}=\sigma_z\otimes\sigma_a\otimes\tau_z,
\qquad
G_8=I\otimes I\otimes\tau_x,
\]

with \([G_8,C_8]=0\). The extra two-state factor must be an existing neutral Nambu or identical-sheet multiplicity, not new mirror matter.

The internal \(8+7\) grading cannot compensate the four-component deck flip because an invertible parity exchange requires equal eigenspace dimensions. Dirac completion to \(8+8\) permits compensation but removes the integer product index. The remaining alternative is a genuinely twisted selector-bundle index.

See [The full selector has a four-component local Clifford lift but needs eight for a global AIII grading](../0300-0399/345_the_full_selector_has_a_four_component_local_clifford_lift_but_needs_eight_for_a_global_aiii_grading.md).

### 20.258 The minimal selector bundle retains parity, not the signed integer

Because the four-component deck transition sends \(C\mapsto-C\), it transports the local chiral index as

\[
\nu\mapsto-\nu.
\]

On the nontrivial selector loop, the integer local system therefore has monodromy \(t=-1\). Its cellular boundary is

\[
\partial=t-1=-2,
\]

so

\[
\boxed{
H_0(S^1;\mathbb Z_-)=\mathbb Z_2.}
\]

The globally meaningful additive class is

\[
[\nu]=\nu\bmod2.
\]

Thus a local index three remains nontrivial but is indistinguishable from one or five. The minimal selector topology detects odd/even generation parity, not exactly three.

The eight-component lift preserves \(C\), changes the monodromy to \(+1\), and restores the full \(\mathbb Z\) index. For the four-component bundle, a physical zero-mode theorem still requires a real/Pfaffian, particle-hole or twisted-Fredholm analytic realization.

See [The four-component selector retains only index parity, while the global double restores \(\mathbb Z\)](../0300-0399/346_the_four_component_selector_retains_only_index_parity_while_the_global_double_restores_z.md).

**Correction from Sections 20.287--20.290:** the local-system theorem is
retained, but the conventional vortex index three cannot be inserted as the
index of the same exact grading-reversing deck-symmetric operator. For that
operator the ordinary complex cover index would be zero.

### 20.259 CAR particle–hole symmetry turns selector parity into a Pfaffian invariant

If the selector defect admits a gauge-compatible Majorana/BdG form

\[
H=iA,
\qquad
A^T=-A,
\qquad
A\text{ real},
\]

then the sign of \(\operatorname{Pf}A\) cannot change while the bulk remains gapped. The domain-wall invariant is

\[
\boxed{
\mathcal Q
=\operatorname{sgn}
\left[\operatorname{Pf}A_-\operatorname{Pf}A_+\right].}
\]

For \(N\) channels reversing mass sign,

\[
\mathcal Q=(-1)^N.
\]

Thus the local index-three selector gives \(\mathcal Q=-1\), while a Dirac-balanced index zero is trivial. Real antisymmetric channel mixing cannot remove the odd crossing without closing an endpoint gap.

This supplies the analytic pairing mechanism missing from the bare \(\mathbb Z_2\) local system. It is credible in neutral Majorana or gauge-equivariant CAR sectors, but it is not automatically a physical BdG description of charged chiral Standard-Model matter.

See [Particle–hole symmetry upgrades selector parity to a Pfaffian zero-mode invariant](../0300-0399/347_particle_hole_symmetry_upgrades_selector_parity_to_a_pfaffian_zero_mode_invariant.md).

**Correction from Sections 20.287--20.290:** this Pfaffian wall theorem remains

### 20.260 The explicit Gaussian benchmark has coefficient lattice \(\frac16\mathbb Z[i]\)

For unrestricted complement triples

\[
Z_i\in M_3(\mathbb Z[i]),
\]

the determinant polynomial has Gaussian-integer coefficients, while the normalized alternating projector divides by six. Hence \(c\in\frac16\mathbb Z[i]\).

This bound is sharp. The diagonal pencil

\[
\operatorname{diag}(x_1,x_1,qx_2)
\]

has determinant \(q x_1^2x_2\), whose raw alternant is \(-q\Delta\). Therefore

\[
\boxed{c=-\frac q6,}
\]

and every point of \(\frac16\mathbb Z[i]\) occurs.

The shortest nonzero shell,

\[
c\in\{\pm1/6,\pm i/6\},
\]

is CP trivial. The shortest shell with both quadratures nonzero is

\[
\boxed{
c\in\{(\pm1\pm i)/6\},}
\]

which has equal quadratures. This makes “shortest CP-capable coefficient” an exact arithmetic mechanism in the benchmark, while leaving the actual exceptional-order sublattice and exclusion of the shorter axis shell open.

See [The Gaussian matrix pencil has exact sign-coefficient lattice \(\frac16\mathbb Z[i]\)](../0300-0399/348_the_gaussian_matrix_pencil_has_exact_sign_coefficient_lattice_one_sixth_z_i.md).

### 20.261 A fixed Hermitian exceptional slice makes the sign coefficient real

If

\[
Z_i\in H_3(\mathbb Z[i]),
\]

then \(X(x)=\sum_i x_iZ_i\) is Hermitian for real \(x_i\), so \(\det X(x)\) is a real polynomial with integer coefficients. Its normalized alternating projection therefore has

\[
c\in\frac16\mathbb Z.
\]

Diagonal Hermitian pencils realize every such value, giving

\[
\boxed{
\Lambda_c^{\rm Herm}
=\frac16\mathbb Z.}
\]

The same no-go holds for the real exceptional Jordan algebra \(H_3(\mathbb O)\): its cubic norm and full polarization are real. Three elements in one fixed real Jordan slice cannot directly produce a complex \(c\).

Thus the imaginary CP quadrature must enter through complexification, non-Hermitian operator data, comparison of distinct real structures, or causal response phases. The earlier \(c=1+i\) example used a complex non-Hermitian diagonal entry and was already testing this enlarged space.

See [A fixed Hermitian exceptional slice forces the sign coefficient real and kills CP](../0300-0399/349_a_fixed_hermitian_exceptional_slice_forces_the_sign_coefficient_real_and_kills_cp.md).

### 20.262 Complexification supplies the missing quadrature through one cubic

Let \(\mathcal C(\mathbf X)=T(\mathbf X,\mathbf X,\mathbf X)\) be the real sign coefficient and write the complexified complement as

\[
\mathbf Z=\mathbf X+i\mathbf Y.
\]

Complex trilinearity gives

\[
\boxed{
\operatorname{Re}c
=T(\mathbf X,\mathbf X,\mathbf X)
-3T(\mathbf X,\mathbf Y,\mathbf Y),}
\]

\[
\boxed{
\operatorname{Im}c
=3T(\mathbf X,\mathbf X,\mathbf Y)
-T(\mathbf Y,\mathbf Y,\mathbf Y).}
\]

Under the real antiunitary \(\mathbf Y\mapsto-\mathbf Y\), the first expression is even and the second odd, so \(c\mapsto\bar c\). An odd sheet permutation reverses both. The two CP quadratures are therefore parts of one complexified exceptional cubic rather than unrelated coefficients.

For weak complexification, the imaginary quadrature begins linearly in \(\mathbf Y\), while the original real part shifts only quadratically. Predictivity now depends on deriving \(\mathbf Y=\mathfrak J(\mathbf X)\) from Furey’s retained complex structure, CAR polarization or a causal dispersion relation.

See [Complexifying the real exceptional cubic supplies CP quadratures with fixed parity](../0300-0399/350_complexifying_the_real_exceptional_cubic_supplies_cp_quadratures_with_fixed_parity.md).

### 20.263 Causality supplies a nonlocal complex structure for the exceptional response

For a retarded complement response, the dispersive and absorptive parts are Kramers–Kronig partners. The Hilbert transform satisfies

\[
\mathcal H^2=-I
\]

on the zero-mode-free real response space, so one may set

\[
\boxed{
\mathbf Y=\mathcal H\mathbf X,
\qquad
\mathbf Z=\mathbf X+i\mathcal H\mathbf X.}
\]

The analytic signal has one-sided Fourier support. Inserting this relation into the complexified exceptional cubic makes both \(\operatorname{Re}c\) and \(\operatorname{Im}c\) functionals of one real spectral response rather than independently fitted triples.

For a passive matrix Herglotz response, the absorptive spectral measure is additionally positive. However, \(\mathcal H^2=-I\) does not imply equal real and imaginary magnitudes at a fixed frequency; the norm-two or equal-quadrature phase still requires a special spectrum or additional dynamics.

See [Causal dispersion supplies the missing exceptional complex structure nonlocally](../0300-0399/351_causal_dispersion_supplies_the_missing_exceptional_complex_structure_nonlocally.md).

### 20.264 The neutral Majorana Pfaffian exists, but CP removes its real sign

For a symmetric three-flavor Majorana matrix \(M\), the correct Lorentz-antisymmetric bilinear is

\[
\Omega=M\otimes\varepsilon,
\qquad
\operatorname{Pf}\Omega=\det M.
\]

The explicit CP-violating checkpoint gives \(\det M=339+4i\). Although \(M\mapsto-M\) reverses the complex Pfaffian for three flavors, the allowed complex path \(e^{i\theta}M\), \(0\leq\theta\leq\pi\), remains nonsingular and connects the two endpoints. A sign cannot be assigned to the complex Pfaffian without additional reality data.

Nor does simple doubling solve the problem. If \(\Omega=A+iB\), the underlying-real alternating form for \(\operatorname{Re}(z^T\Omega w)\) is

\[
\mathcal R_{\rm alt}(\Omega)=
\begin{pmatrix}A&-B\\-B&-A\end{pmatrix}.
\]

Its Pfaffian has magnitude \(|\det M|^2\), and its twelve real dimensions make it invariant under overall sign reversal. The physically useful \(\mathbb Z_2\) therefore requires more than neutrality: either a selector/CAR-compatible real class, a determinant-line holonomy under deck gluing, or a closed phase-winding theorem.

See [The neutral Majorana Pfaffian is \(\det M\), but CP makes it complex and removes the sign](../0300-0399/352_the_neutral_majorana_pfaffian_is_det_m_but_cp_makes_it_complex_and_removes_the_sign.md).

### 20.265 Antipodal selector sewing recovers parity as determinant winding

The complex interpolation that destroys a bare Pfaffian sign becomes constrained once the selector deck action is retained. If

\[
M(\theta+\pi)=-M(\theta),
\]

then for \(N\) neutral flavors

\[
d(\theta+\pi)=(-1)^N d(\theta),
\qquad d=\det M.
\]

For a nonsingular family on the double cover, continuity of the determinant phase gives

\[
\boxed{w[d]=N+2k,\qquad w[d]\equiv N\pmod2.}
\]

Thus three flavors have odd determinant winding; the minimal family \(M(\theta)=e^{i\theta}M_0\) has \(w=3\). The complex line over a circle is still ordinarily trivial, so the invariant belongs to the antipodally equivariant problem, not to an asserted first Chern class. Its conversion into a protected zero mode remains conditional on constructing a physical selector-dependent operator and proving a mod-two index theorem.

See [Selector deck gluing turns the complex mass sign into determinant-winding parity](../0300-0399/353_selector_deck_gluing_turns_complex_mass_sign_into_determinant_winding_parity.md).

### 20.266 The determinant winding is an exact Toeplitz boundary index

Let \(P_+\) be the Hardy projection and let \(M:S^1\to GL(N,\mathbb C)\) be the selector mass symbol. The matrix Toeplitz operator

\[
T_M=P_+MP_+
\]

is Fredholm and satisfies

\[
\boxed{\operatorname{Ind}T_M=-w[\det M].}
\]

The chiral edge Hamiltonian \(H_\partial=\begin{psmallmatrix}0&T_M^\dagger\\T_M&0\end{psmallmatrix}\) therefore has total zero-space parity equal to selector winding parity. For \(M(z)=zM_0\) with three flavors, the minimal representative has index \(-3\) and three same-chirality boundary zero modes. This closes the analytic index gap in complex class AIII while leaving physical Majorana reality as a separate condition.

See [The selector determinant winding has an exact Toeplitz edge index](../0300-0399/354_the_selector_determinant_winding_has_an_exact_toeplitz_edge_index.md).

### 20.267 Reflection reality reduces the selector integer to class-D parity

For the canonical reflection-real symbol \(q_m(k)=e^{imk}\), the BdG representative

\[
H_m(k)=\cos(mk)\tau_z+\sin(mk)\tau_y
\]

has \(C=\tau_xK\), \(T=K\) and BDI winding \(m\). If \(T\) and chiral symmetry are relaxed while \(C\) is preserved, the invariant-momentum Pfaffians give

\[
\boxed{\nu_D=(-1)^m,\qquad \nu_D=(-1)^{w[\det q]}\text{ for multiple channels}.}
\]

Three selector-odd flavors are therefore class-D nontrivial. The BDI-parent reflection sewing \(q(-k)=U_Cq(k)^*U_C^T\) is distinct from both antipodal oddness and the exact CAR particle-hole operation. Takagi factorization supplies a convenient BDI representative for an isolated symmetric Majorana block; as the next section shows, physical flavor-CP breaking may remove that integer refinement while exact CAR self-duality preserves its class-D parity.

### 20.268 Furey CAR conjugation survives flavor-CP breaking

Furey's intrinsic complex conjugation exchanges left/right Weyl generalized ideals and particle/antiparticle minimal ideals. On the self-dual carrier it becomes

which is gauge equivariant and supplies exact BdG particle-hole self-duality. This must be distinguished from a second time-reversal-like or generalized-CP antiunitary \(J_W\), which generic Yukawas and the exceptional CP triangle may break.

H_m(k)\mapsto H_m(k)+\lambda\sin k\,\tau_x

breaks \(T=K\) and chiral symmetry while preserving \(J_0\), the gap and \(\nu_D=(-1)^m\). Thus flavor CP violation can destroy the BDI integer refinement without destroying odd class-D parity. The antiunitary-existence blocker is replaced by the selector-coordinate and dynamical-locality problem.

contains only Fourier harmonics \(e^{\pm imk}\). It therefore has a range-\(|m|\) real-space representative. The BDI-breaking class-D term is nearest neighbour, so the complete minimal three-flavor winding-three representative has finite range three.

### 20.271 Gauged \(B-L\) is a complete conventional vortex home, but an added one

With one \(\nu^c\) per generation, gauged \(B-L\) is anomaly free. A Standard-Model-singlet scalar \(S\) of charge \(-2\) permits

and breaks the gauge circle to a finite remnant. Its Abelian-Higgs strings have integer winding and finite tension. For three sterile flavors,

### 20.273 Pauli exclusion permits the Hermitian pairing channel; dynamics does not yet select it

The earlier local identity

\[
(\nu^c\nu^c)^2=0

for one Weyl flavor concerns a holomorphic fourth power. It does not kill the
Hermitian norm. Explicit exterior algebra gives

\[
B_{ab}=\epsilon_{\alpha\beta}\nu_a^{c\alpha}\nu_b^{c\beta}
=B_{ba},
\qquad
B_{aa}^2=0,
\qquad
B_{aa}^\dagger B_{aa}\ne0.

For three flavors the six \(B_{ab}\) are linearly independent, and

\[
G\operatorname{tr}(B^\dagger B)
\]

is a nonzero Lorentz-, gauge- and \(U(3)\)-invariant interaction. A symmetric
Hubbard--Stratonovich field of \(B-L=-2\) reproduces it exactly. This closes the
operator-existence question but exposes the real obstruction: no explicit
Furey, exceptional or Jordan interaction yet determines an attractive,
supercritical \(G\). Algebraic closure permits the channel; it does not choose

### 20.275 The missing fiveplet survives as a relationship tensor, not an internal product

The \(M_2(\mathbb C)\) neutral factor does contain a canonical Pauli triplet.
Its abstract symmetric square is \(\mathbf1\oplus\mathbf5\), but internal
Jordan multiplication obeys

\[
\sigma_i\circ\sigma_j=\delta_{ij}I
\]

and therefore kills the fiveplet. Retaining the two relationship indices gives
instead

\[
Q_{ij}(x)=x_ix_j-\frac{|x|^2}{3}\delta_{ij},
\qquad Q(Rx)=RQ(x)R^T.
\]

This tensor is an exact spin-two fiveplet and satisfies \(Q(-x)=Q(x)\). At
fixed radius its uniaxial orbit is \(\mathbb{RP}^2\), recovering the real-form
selector geometry directly from the neutral Pauli triplet.

The result makes the relational-carrier language precise: internal
multiplication discards the spin-two information, whereas the external
relationship square preserves it. The remaining physical gate is a derived
bosonic triplet and diagonal locking among the internal, sterile-flavor and
external relationship rotation groups.

### 20.276 Three fiveplets align uniquely only after their rotation groups are identified

Treating the neutral, sterile and external spin-two tensors as representations
of independent groups gives

\[
\dim\operatorname{Hom}_{SO(3)_A\times SO(3)_B}(\mathbf5_A,\mathbf5_B)=0.
\]

Repeated index notation between them is therefore already a locking spurion.
Under one diagonal group, by contrast,

\[
\dim\operatorname{End}_{SO(3)_D}(\mathbf5)=1,
\]

so the invariant contraction is unique up to scale. Positive square terms can
align both \(\Sigma_0\) and \(R_0\) with \(Q(x)\) exactly. The hard question is
not the aligned potential but the origin of the common group.

If three global \(SO(3)\) factors lock spontaneously to the diagonal, six
continuous generators break. Director selection breaks two more. A fully
global route therefore predicts eight Goldstones unless gauging, explicit
breaking, boundary conditions or a kinematic common origin removes them.

See [A common \(SO(3)\) uniquely aligns the three fiveplets, but spontaneous diagonal locking costs six modes](../0300-0399/364_a_common_so3_uniquely_aligns_the_three_fiveplets_but_spontaneous_diagonal_locking_costs_six_modes.md).

### 20.277 Triality is a discrete organizer, not the continuous lock

The ordinary three-sheet triality carrier is \(\mathbf1\oplus\mathbf2\) under
\(S_3\), with odd permutation matrices of determinant \(-1\). Multiplying odd
matrices by \(-1\) embeds \(S_3\) in \(SO(3)\), but changes the trivial singlet
into a sign line. Neither representation supplies a continuous rotation
triplet extending the existing sheet interpretation without extra choice.

More fundamentally,

\[
\operatorname{Lie}(SO(3)^3\rtimes S_3)
=\mathfrak{so}(3)^3,
\qquad \dim=9.
\]

Finite triality adds no tangent generators and does not produce the
three-dimensional diagonal algebra. It can permute sectors or equalize
coefficients of already-existing locks, but it cannot define contractions of
independently rotating indices. The continuous-lock search must therefore move
to a shared source, bifundamental field or gauged mechanism.

See [Triality can permute the three sectors but cannot supply their continuous diagonal \(SO(3)\)](../0300-0399/365_triality_can_permute_the_three_sectors_but_cannot_supply_their_continuous_diagonal_so3.md).

Writing the leading block as

=\operatorname{span}\{P_O,P_R,E_{OR},E_{RO}\},

its Hermitian basis is \(I,\sigma_x,\sigma_y,\sigma_z\). The response exchange
\(\Theta_{\rm face}=\sigma_xK\) fixes the first three and reverses population

Its determinant is the Lorentz norm \(p^2-|z|^2\). Pointwise exchange-fixed
positive spectral measures remain in this real form under Herglotz integration,
while an independent Hermitian flavor factor can retain nonzero CP-odd
commutator invariants.

This closes the algebraic response architecture but not its physical source.

### 20.281 Unbroken \(B-L\) blocks the full raw Nambu carrier

If the two neutral faces are the Nambu pair \((N,N^\dagger)\), their charges are
\((+1,-1)\). The response-entry charges are therefore

\[
\begin{pmatrix}0&+2\\-2&0\end{pmatrix}.
\]

In a continuous-\(B-L\)-invariant state, the anomalous off-diagonal entries
vanish. Intersecting this condition with the equal-population response real form
gives only

\[
\{pI:p\geq0\}.
\]

Thus one sterile Weyl field cannot realize the full neutral Lorentz cone through
its raw Nambu density while \(B-L\) remains unbroken. CAR also sews
\(+\omega\) to \(-\omega\); it does not require pointwise exchange equality at
one frequency.

The cone can reopen through charge-two symmetry breaking, an explicitly charged
source, or a separately justified frequency fold. Alternatively, two
independent same-charge neutral probes can have a full cross response, but that
requires a physical two-channel multiplicity. The Majorana-condensate and
response-carrier branches therefore meet at a precise superselection gate.

See [Unbroken \(B-L\) collapses a Nambu two-face response, while CAR sews opposite frequencies](../0300-0399/369_unbroken_bminusl_collapses_a_nambu_two_face_response_while_car_sews_opposite_frequencies.md).

### 20.282 Positive frequency folding restores the cone but forbids interior winding

For a positive-frequency density \(A(\omega)\), the normalized fold

\[
\rho_f(\omega)
=\frac12\left(A+\sigma_x\overline A\,\sigma_x\right)
\]

is positive, exchange fixed and ultraviolet-moment controlled. Its retarded
transform

\[
F(\zeta)=\int_0^\infty
\frac{\rho_f(\omega)}{\omega-\zeta}\,d\omega
\]

is a matrix Herglotz function. With full directional support,
\(\operatorname{Im}F(\zeta)\succ0\) in the upper half-plane, implying
\(\det F(\zeta)\neq0\).

Because the upper half-plane is simply connected, every closed contour wholly
inside it has

\[
\frac{1}{2\pi i}\oint d\log\det F=0.
\]

Thus folding solves the causal-cone problem but cannot reproduce the selector
winding as a pure passive interior-frequency invariant. Nonzero phase winding
must involve a boundary singularity, analytic continuation, compactification
data, or another periodic coordinate. The defect and momentum branches remain
viable; the pure interior-frequency branch is closed negatively.

See [A positive frequency fold restores the \(H_2(\mathbb R)\) cone but has zero interior determinant winding](../0300-0399/370_a_positive_frequency_fold_restores_the_h2r_cone_but_has_zero_interior_determinant_winding.md).

### 20.283 The selector topology survives as \(w_1\), not response determinant winding

On

\[
\mathbb C_+\times S^1_{\rm defect}\simeq S^1,
\]

the primitive selector lift satisfies \(n(2\pi)=-n(0)\), while its projector
closes. The corresponding real line has

\[
w_1=1.
\]

A strictly positive periodic response can be placed over the same circle, but
its determinant remains nonzero and has zero defect-angle winding. Contracting
the passive frequency factor leaves the selector line unchanged.

The surviving invariant is therefore the first Stiefel--Whitney class of the
real-form/eigenline bundle, not the complex determinant of the positive
response. A genuinely mixed invariant would require frequency compactification,
boundary singularities or another closed parameter dimension.

See [Frequency is a topological spectator while the selector \(\mathbb Z_2\) survives as a real-form bundle](../0300-0399/371_frequency_is_a_topological_spectator_while_the_selector_z2_survives_as_a_real_form_bundle.md).

### 20.284 Odd index three obstructs ordinary quotient descent

If the conventional index-three operator on the selector double cover were the
ordinary pullback of a quotient Fredholm operator, covering multiplicativity
would give

\[
3=2\,\operatorname{Ind}\mathcal D,
\]

which is impossible. Equivariantly, writing the cover index as
\(a\mathbf1+b\mathbf{sgn}\) gives \(a+b=3\), while a free ordinary action would
require vanishing nonidentity character \(a-b=0\).

Hence the primitive operator is necessarily twisted: the deck action must
reverse a grading, act projectively on spinors, twist the mass line, or place
the problem in a real mod-two index class. The ordinary index three proves odd
cover topology but cannot choose the physical deck sector or determine its
kernel count.

See [The odd double-cover index proves the primitive selector operator is twisted, not an ordinary quotient](../0300-0399/372_the_odd_double_cover_index_proves_the_primitive_selector_operator_is_twisted_not_an_ordinary_quotient.md).

### 20.285 The minimal deck algebra has four reality branches

Let \(S\) repair the selector mass sign, \(\Gamma\) be the chiral grading and
\(C\) the Furey/CAR conjugation. With

\[
S^2=\Gamma^2=C^2=1,\qquad S\Gamma=-\Gamma S,
\]

two signs remain:

\[
CS=\epsilon_SSC,\qquad
C\Gamma=\epsilon_\Gamma\Gamma C.
\]

They produce four branches with

\[
(S\Gamma)^2=-1,\qquad
(SC)^2=\epsilon_S,\qquad
(S\Gamma C)^2=-\epsilon_S\epsilon_\Gamma.
\]

Furey conjugation establishes \(C^2=1\) and gauge equivariance, but does not
define \(S\), \(\epsilon_S\) or \(\epsilon_\Gamma\). A common-basis
intertwiner is therefore logically required before assigning the primitive
defect a real symmetry class.

See [Minimal selector deck lifts form four Clifford branches, not one Furey-selected operator](../0300-0399/373_minimal_selector_deck_lifts_form_four_clifford_branches_not_one_furey_selected_operator.md).

### 20.286 A four-component model makes the Hamiltonian descend while the grading flips

The minimal complex module for \(\alpha,\beta_1,\beta_2,\Gamma\) has dimension
four. An explicit representative permits

\[
H(k,\varphi)
=k\alpha+\cos\frac\varphi2\,\beta_1
+\sin\frac\varphi2\,\beta_2,
\qquad S=\alpha.
\]

Then

\[
S H(k,\varphi+2\pi)S^{-1}=H(k,\varphi),
\]

but

\[
S\Gamma S^{-1}=-\Gamma.
\]

The primitive ungraded Hamiltonian is well defined, while the two chiral blocks
used by the integer index are exchanged by the deck transformation. Defining
\(C=SK\) gives \(C^2=+1\) and class-D particle--hole symmetry. Consequently the
double-cover \(\mathbb Z\) index loses its grading on the quotient and leaves a
possible \(\mathbb Z_2\) target; this statement identifies the symmetry class,
not the value of its invariant.

This supplies the missing mechanism behind the odd-cover obstruction without
fractionalizing the index or adding separate selector/Nambu doublings.

See [A minimal four-component Dirac model descends the Hamiltonian but reverses the chiral grading](../0300-0399/374_a_minimal_four_component_dirac_model_descends_the_hamiltonian_but_reverses_the_chiral_grading.md).

### 20.287 The local deck family does not by itself carry odd fermion parity

For the explicit model,

\[
H(k,\varphi)^2=(k^2+1)I_4,
\]

so its ordinary spectral flow is zero. At (k=0), a continuous real frame of
the two occupied states closes under the deck sewing with

\[
W=\begin{pmatrix}0&-1\\1&0\end{pmatrix},
\qquad W^2=-I,qquad\det W=+1.
\]

Thus the occupied rank-two bundle is orientable even though the selector
eigenline is Möbius. The Majorana endpoint matrix
(A(\varphi)=H(0,\varphi)S) is antisymmetric, but

\[
\operatorname{Pf}A(2\pi)=\operatorname{Pf}[-A(0)]
=\operatorname{Pf}A(0)
\]

in four dimensions. Selector-line (w_1=1), class-D eligibility and odd
fermion parity are therefore three distinct assertions. Computing the last
requires a spatially regulated Fredholm operator and its physical domain.

See [The minimal deck model loses the integer grading but does not yet prove odd fermion parity](../0300-0399/375_the_minimal_deck_model_loses_the_integer_grading_but_does_not_yet_prove_odd_fermion_parity.md).

### 20.288 The second kinetic direction turns grading loss into a Pin question

Extend the model to an oriented two-dimensional Dirac symbol with

\[
\alpha_x=\sigma_x\otimes I,quad
\alpha_y=\sigma_y\otimes I,quad
\beta_1=\sigma_z\otimes\sigma_x,quad
\beta_2=\sigma_z\otimes\sigma_z,quad
\Gamma=\sigma_z\otimes\sigma_y.
\]

The unique internal involution that preserves both kinetic generators and
flips both masses is

\[
D_{\rm or}=\pm I\otimes\sigma_y.
\]

It commutes with (Gamma), so the chiral integer grading descends. The former
grading-reversing repair (D_{\rm Pin}=\alpha_x) instead flips
(alpha_y), and sews the full symbol only together with
(k_y\mapsto-k_y). Hence the desired grading loss is not a purely internal
operation on a fixed oriented plane: it is a Pin/frame-reflection,
boundary-domain or equivalent projective sewing problem.

This is a useful convergence. The odd-cover obstruction, the trivial local
Pfaffian audit and the two-dimensional Clifford extension all demand extra
global geometry. The next decisive object is a self-adjoint Pin Dirac domain,
not another unconstrained mass matrix.

See [A second kinetic direction forces a choice between chiral descent and orientation reversal](../0300-0399/376_a_second_kinetic_direction_forces_a_choice_between_chiral_descent_and_orientation_reversal.md).

### 20.289 Stop-and-re-root: grading-reversing deck symmetry forces zero cover index

Let (K_\pm) be the two chiral parts of the kernel of a Fredholm operator
(\mathcal D). If an invertible deck lift obeys

\[
S\mathcal DS^{-1}=\pm\mathcal D,
\qquad S\Gamma S^{-1}=-\Gamma,
\]

then (S) bijects (K_+) and (K_-). Hence

\[
\operatorname{Ind}_\Gamma\mathcal D
=\dim K_+-\dim K_-=0.
\]

This produces an incompatible triangle: a conventional oriented cover index
three, an exact deck symmetry of the same operator and deck reversal of the
grading cannot all hold. The earlier local (4\times4) construction remains a
Clifford algebra certificate but is not a global quotient-index construction.

The programme now keeps four cases separate: a conventional oriented
index-three vortex without that exact deck; a grading-preserving oriented
quotient with even cover index; a Pin quotient whose real mod-two invariant is
computed independently and whose ordinary complex cover index is zero; and a
nonsymmetric half-winding interpolation that is not a quotient. No branch may
borrow an index from another.

See [A grading-reversing deck symmetry forces zero cover index, so the index-three parent cannot be the same operator](../0300-0399/377_a_grading_reversing_deck_symmetry_forces_zero_cover_index_so_the_index_three_parent_cannot_be_the_same_operator.md).

### 20.290 A correction ledger separates five valid theorems from one invalid synthesis

Five pieces of mathematics survive intact: sign-local-system homology,
Pfaffian wall parity, periodic BDI-to-D reduction, the conventional oriented
vortex index and the local Clifford sewing algebra. The withdrawn step is
their unsupported identification as invariants of one primitive physical
operator.

Future parity claims must name the operator, base/domain, exact symmetry,
invariant and bridge theorem. Without the fifth field, equal values in
(\mathbb Z_2) show compatibility only; they do not establish identity. This
discipline preserves useful comparison models while preventing a historical
cycle summary from overruling a later no-go theorem.

See [Correction ledger for selector index, parity and primitive deck claims](../0300-0399/378_correction_ledger_for_selector_index_parity_and_primitive_deck_claims.md).

### 20.291 Finite Majorana nullity is always even, so defect parity is relative

For every finite class-D Hamiltonian (H=iA) in a Majorana basis,
(A) is a real antisymmetric (2N\times2N) matrix. Its rank is even and
therefore

\[
\dim\ker H=2N-\operatorname{rank}A=0\pmod2.
\]

A finite Möbius or Pin lattice cannot certify a single defect Majorana by odd
total nullity. The required partner lies at another defect, a boundary, the
regulator or infinity. The correct finite diagnostics are a relative
Pfaffian switch in a common Majorana orientation, mod-two spectral flow and
finite-size localization of a defect/boundary near-zero pair. The clean
analytic target is an infinite-volume real Fredholm index.

See [A finite Majorana lattice has even total nullity, so Pin defect parity must be relative or local](../0300-0399/379_a_finite_majorana_lattice_has_even_total_nullity_so_pin_defect_parity_must_be_relative_or_local.md).

### 20.292 A glide-covariant double cylinder realizes the Pin domain exactly

On (x\in\mathbb Z_{2L}) and open (y\in\{-M,\ldots,M\}), define the free
glide

\[
g(x,y)=(x+L,-y),
\qquad U_g=P_g\otimes\alpha_x.
\]

The mass texture

\[
m_1=\sin(\pi x/L),\qquad m_2=\mu y
\]

is glide odd and has a deck-related vortex--antivortex pair. The centered
finite-difference Hamiltonian is exactly Hermitian and satisfies

\[
U_g^2=1,qquad [U_g,H]=0,qquad
U_g\Gamma U_g^{-1}=-\Gamma.
\]

Particle--hole reality (C=\alpha_xK) commutes with the glide, so it descends
to both equal-dimensional deck sectors even though the chiral grading does
not. This is the first complete operator/domain realization of the Pin branch.
Its ordinary complex index is zero as required. A regulator, common Majorana
orientation, relative Pfaffian and localization scaling are still required to
determine the independent real invariant.

See [An exact glide-covariant double cylinder realizes the Pin domain architecture](../0300-0399/380_an_exact_glide_covariant_double_cylinder_realizes_the_pin_domain_architecture.md).

### 20.293 Glide symmetry obstructs a four-component Wilson regulator

Every (4\times4) Hermitian matrix anticommuting with both
(\alpha_x=\sigma_x\otimes I) and (\alpha_y=\sigma_y\otimes I) lies in

\[
\sigma_z\otimes\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb R}
\{I,\sigma_x,\sigma_y,\sigma_z\}.
\]

Conjugation by the glide spin lift (S=\alpha_x) reverses every one of these
matrices. Hence no constant four-component Wilson mass is glide even. Class-D
reality retains three real candidates, but all remain glide odd.

One auxiliary regulator pair repairs the algebra on the oriented double:

\[
\widetilde S=\alpha_x\otimes\tau_x,
\qquad
M_W^{(8)}=(\sigma_z\otimes I)\otimes\tau_z.
\]

The two sign reversals make (M_W^{(8)}) glide even while it remains a valid
class-D Wilson mass. The deck exchanges the regulator partners, so quotienting
may return four independent components rather than adding mirror matter. That
species count and the regulated relative invariant now require an explicit
spectrum calculation.

See [The glide forbids a constant four-component Wilson mass but an exchanged regulator pair repairs it](../0300-0399/381_the_glide_forbids_a_constant_four_component_wilson_mass_but_an_exchanged_regulator_pair_repairs_it.md).

### 20.294 The exchanged Wilson pair removes doublers without a quotient mirror cone

The regulated bulk symbol

\[
H_W(\mathbf k)=\sin k_x\,\widetilde\alpha_x
+\sin k_y\,\widetilde\alpha_y
+r(2-\cos k_x-\cos k_y)M_W^{(8)}
\]

satisfies

\[
E^2=\sin^2k_x+\sin^2k_y
+r^2(2-\cos k_x-\cos k_y)^2.
\]

Only ((0,0)) remains gapless; the other naive cones have gaps
(2|r|,2|r|,4|r|). At the surviving glide-invariant cone, the traceless
involution (widetilde S=\alpha_x\otimes\tau_x) splits the eight-component
double fiber into two four-dimensional deck sectors. Each quotient sector
therefore contains one four-component cone, not two independent regulator
copies.

This clears the bulk species-count gate while preserving glide and class-D
reality. The decisive remaining calculation is the regulated textured
reference/defect relative Pfaffian and localization scaling.

See [The exchanged Wilson pair gaps all doublers while one deck sector retains one four-component cone](../0300-0399/382_the_exchanged_wilson_pair_gaps_all_doublers_while_one_deck_sector_retains_one_four_component_cone.md).

### 20.295 The regulated Pin defect has a nontrivial relative phase, but symmetry does not force it

Takagi-transforming (C=U_CK) to literal conjugation makes each projected deck
sector a real antisymmetric Majorana matrix. Reference and defect textures can
then be compared in one common oriented Majorana and glide basis.

The most symmetric exchanged regulator has an accidental sector-preserving
chiral symmetry

\[
Q=(\sigma_z\otimes\sigma_y)\otimes\tau_y
\]

and gives trivial relative Pfaffian sign. A complete Pauli audit finds eight
glide-even, class-D-allowed terms that break this extra symmetry. The simplest
is

\[
\delta I\otimes\sigma_y\otimes I_\tau.
\]

With it present, both deck sectors have

\[
\mathcal Q_{\rm rel}
=\operatorname{sgn}[\operatorname{Pf}A_{\rm ref}
                     \operatorname{Pf}A_{\rm def}]=-1
\]

at two separated parameter values across the tested (L=2,3) and transverse
widths (M=1,2). This is the first direct positive finite-lattice evidence for
an independent Pin relative phase. Multiple sign changes also show that glide
and CAR do not choose the phase: continuum stability, localization and a
Furey-derived source for the chiral-breaking term are now the controlling
gates.

See [The regulated Pin lattice has a nontrivial relative Pfaffian phase, but glide and CAR do not force it](../0300-0399/383_the_regulated_pin_lattice_has_a_nontrivial_relative_pfaffian_phase_but_glide_and_car_do_not_force_it.md).

### 20.296 The minimal phase-selecting term is the oriented neutral Furey relationship

Among the eight glide-even, class-D-allowed perturbations, exactly one is
identity on both kinetic and regulator factors:

\[
I\otimes\sigma_y\otimes I_\tau.
\]

In the neutral Furey block (operatorname{End}(O\oplus R)),

\[
\sigma_y=-i(E_{OR}-E_{RO}).
\]

It is gauge neutral, Hermitian, fixed by the response exchange
(sigma_xK), odd under CAR particle--hole symmetry as a BdG Hamiltonian term,
and glide even. This is an exact common-basis identification of the minimal
Pin-phase selector with the oriented neutral relationship quadrature.

It is not yet canonical. The residual relative rephasing of the gauge-identical
(O) and (R) lines rotates (sigma_x) and (sigma_y) continuously. Furey's
algebra supplies the operator, but an additional source, boundary phase,
exceptional orientation or second real structure must select its direction
and coefficient. The bridge has therefore advanced from representation
matching to a finite phase-selection problem.

See [The minimal Pin-phase selector is the oriented neutral Furey relationship, but its phase is not canonical](../0300-0399/384_the_minimal_pin_phase_selector_is_the_oriented_neutral_furey_relationship_but_its_phase_is_not_canonical.md).

### 20.297 Exceptional orientation can source the Pin phase only relationally

The exceptional coefficient (c) cannot be inserted as
(delta\propto\operatorname{Im}c) before fixing the neutral (O/R) phase.
Under relative rephasing, a relationship coefficient carries the opposite
weight to (E_{OR}), and one isolated nonzero coefficient can always be made
real.

With two relationship amplitudes—a selector reference (q) and an exceptional
amplitude (c_{OR})—the oriented area

\[
\Omega_{OR}=\operatorname{Im}(c_{OR}\bar q)
\]

is rephasing invariant and antiunitary odd. In the gauge (q>0), it reduces to
(|q|\operatorname{Im}c_{OR}) and can conditionally source the
(sigma_y) Pin term.

The established exceptional coefficient has sheet-sign and conjugation laws,
but no derived (O/R) relative charge. A charged intertwiner from the
exceptional sign line to (operatorname{Hom}(R,O)), together with the
selector-to-neutral map, is therefore required. This replaces a noninvariant
single-phase shortcut with a precise two-spurion bridge theorem.

See [The exceptional cubic can source the Pin orientation only through a second O/R relationship spurion](../0300-0399/385_the_exceptional_cubic_can_source_the_pin_orientation_only_through_a_second_or_relationship_spurion.md).

### 20.298 Schur elimination supplies the required second relationship path

For a positive three-port response with edges
(u=r_{12}), (v=r_{23}), (w=r_{31}), eliminating port three gives

\[
u_{\rm eff}=u-q_{\rm ind},
\qquad q_{\rm ind}=\frac{\bar w\bar v}{d_3}.
\]

The direct edge and indirect path have the same (O/R) rephasing weight, and

\[
\boxed{
\operatorname{Im}(u\bar q_{\rm ind})
=\frac1{d_3}\operatorname{Im}(uvw).}
\]

Thus the two-spurion orientation required by the Pin (sigma_y) term is
exactly the Schur shadow of the three-port Majorana/exceptional holonomy. This
avoids assigning an (O/R) charge to the exceptional coefficient by hand.

The reduced edge alone can still be rephased real; direct/indirect provenance
must be retained through frequency dependence, controlled detuning or a
microscopic path decomposition. The physical blocker is now selection of a
third neutral Furey port, a passive causal three-port response and the
normalization from loop area to the Hamiltonian coefficient.

See [Schur reduction turns three-port holonomy into exactly the two O/R spurions needed by the Pin phase](../0300-0399/386_schur_reduction_turns_three_port_holonomy_into_exactly_the_two_or_spurions_needed_by_the_pin_phase.md).

### 20.299 The third holonomy port cannot be another internal Furey matrix-unit line

Only (O) and (R) are equivalent trivial gauge modules. Schur's lemma gives

\[
\operatorname{End}_{G_{SM}}(V)
\cong M_2(\mathbb C)\oplus\mathbb C^3.
\]

Appending any trace direction from the color, weak or charged-singlet block
does not produce an internal (M_3): the four cross-block units required to
connect it to (O,R) transform nontrivially under the gauge group.

The three-port construction must instead live in source space. Three
gauge-invariant composite currents can have a full (3\times3) retarded
correlator even when the internal commutant has no (M_3) factor. Its
off-diagonal entries are dynamical cross-correlators, not internal matrix units.
Without interactions coupling the third current to both neutral ports, those
entries and the loop holonomy vanish. The weak trace is a provisional leading
candidate through neutrino/Higgs interactions, not an algebraically selected
answer.

See [No third Furey singlet extends the neutral M2 to M3, so the holonomy port must be a composite response](../0300-0399/387_no_third_furey_singlet_extends_the_neutral_m2_to_m3_so_the_holonomy_port_must_be_a_composite_response.md).

### 20.300 Passive three-port holonomy requires spectral rank at least two

For a rank-one spectral residue (ho=aa^\dagger),

\[
\rho_{12}\rho_{23}\rho_{31}=|a_1a_2a_3|^2\geq0,
\]

so its loop has no oriented imaginary part. Two transition vectors are
minimal. Taking

\[
a=(1,1,1)^T,qquad b=(1,i,0)^T
\]

and adding (I_3) gives the strictly positive density

\[
\rho=
\begin{pmatrix}
3&1-i&1\\1+i&3&1\\1&1&2
\end{pmatrix}>0,
\]

with loop (uvw=1-i) and Schur orientation
(Omega_{OR}=-1/2). The one-pole response
(G(z)=\rho/(\omega_0-z)) is strictly Herglotz, proving that passivity,
causality and nonzero holonomy are mutually compatible.

The physical third-port gate is now sharper: named composite currents must
share at least two independent spectral transitions, or acquire equivalent
multi-pole interference. One isolated mediator cannot generate the Pin-source
orientation.

See [A rank-two spectral multiplicity is the minimum for passive three-port holonomy](../0300-0399/388_a_rank_two_spectral_multiplicity_is_the_minimum_for_passive_three_port_holonomy.md).

### 20.301 Multi-pole interference removes the need for degenerate spectral rank

A strict causal model can use only rank-one atoms at distinct frequencies:

\[
G(z)=\frac{aa^\dagger}{-2-z}
+\frac{bb^\dagger}{1-z}
+0.4\sum_{j=1}^3\frac{e_je_j^\dagger}{\omega_j-z},
\]

with (a=(1,1,1)^T), (b=(1,i,0)^T) and
((\omega_1,\omega_2,\omega_3)=(3,4,5)). Each atom separately has zero
oriented loop, while their interference produces

\[
u(z)=s_{-2}(z)-is_1(z),
\qquad
q_{\rm ind}(z)=
\frac{s_{-2}(z)^2}{s_{-2}(z)+0.4s_5(z)}.
\]

The direct and indirect paths have different pole sets, and
(operatorname{Im}[u\bar q_{\rm ind}]) varies with frequency and reverses
sign along an imaginary-frequency scan. Separate diagonal atoms make
(operatorname{Im}G(z)) strictly positive throughout the upper half-plane.

Thus exact degeneracy is unnecessary: multi-pole interference supplies both
causal holonomy and an operational way to retain path provenance. The remaining
bridge is a low-energy Schur self-energy mapping this response area to the
static Pin coefficient.

See [Multi-pole interference generates a causal holonomy even when every spectral atom is rank one](../0300-0399/389_multi_pole_interference_generates_a_causal_holonomy_even_when_every_spectral_atom_is_rank_one.md).

### 20.302 Schur holonomy becomes a Hamiltonian term only at kernel level

For a quadratic kernel

\[
K=\begin{pmatrix}A&B\\B^\dagger&d\end{pmatrix},
\]

eliminating the third variable gives

\[
K_{\rm eff}=A-Bd^{-1}B^\dagger,
\]

and the direct-minus-indirect off-diagonal term has the correct energy
dimension to become (delta\sigma_y). If instead (G=K^{-1}) is a measured
correlator, block inversion gives

\[
G_{xx}=K_{\rm eff}^{-1},
\]

while Schur-complementing (G) over its third block returns (A^{-1}), not
(K_{\rm eff}). A susceptibility therefore cannot be treated directly as an
effective Hamiltonian.

Dirichlet-to-Neumann maps, admittances and inverse propagators do compose by
Schur reduction and remain viable direct sources. Inverting a Herglotz
correlator produces the expected anti-Herglotz imaginary-part sign. The final
response-to-Pin arrow is now pinned at an explicit object-category choice,
dimensions and wavefunction normalization rather than an informal matrix
analogy.

See [Schur holonomy maps to the Pin Hamiltonian only for a kernel or admittance, not an arbitrary correlator](../0300-0399/390_schur_holonomy_maps_to_the_pin_hamiltonian_only_for_a_kernel_or_admittance_not_an_arbitrary_correlator.md).

### 20.303 A causal normalized kernel reaches a verified nontrivial Pin point

Let

\[
\gamma=\frac{5\sqrt{11}}{12},
\qquad
K_0=
\begin{pmatrix}
4&1-i\gamma&1\\1+i\gamma&4&1\\1&1&3
\end{pmatrix}>0,
\]

and (K(z)=K_0-zI). Then (K) is strictly anti-Herglotz and
(G=K^{-1}) is strictly Herglotz. Kernel-level elimination of port three gives
an oriented two-port term with raw coefficient (gamma).

The low-frequency residue matrix is

\[
Z=I+\frac19
\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&1\end{pmatrix},
\qquad \det Z=\frac{11}{9}.
\]

After canonical (Z^{-1/2}) normalization, the (sigma_y) coefficient is

\[
\delta_c=\frac{\gamma}{\sqrt{\det Z}}=\frac54.
\]

This is exactly a finite-lattice checkpoint previously verified to have
negative relative Pfaffian in both deck sectors. The construction closes the
causality, positivity, dimensions and residue-normalization existence gate. Its
entries were chosen to reach the checkpoint, so it is a compatibility witness,
not a prediction or a full continuum match.

See [A causal inverse propagator can land exactly on a verified nontrivial Pin checkpoint after canonical normalization](../0300-0399/391_a_causal_inverse_propagator_can_land_exactly_on_a_verified_nontrivial_pin_checkpoint_after_canonical_normalization.md).

### 20.304 The finite Pin phase is banded and the causal checkpoint is near a boundary

A (0.025)-spaced scan with Pfaffian sign bisection resolves eight crossings
below (delta=2) for the (L=2,M=1) benchmark. The resulting nontrivial
relative-Pfaffian bands are approximately

\[
(0.164642,0.431858),quad
(0.876560,1.321239),quad
(1.421520,1.739993),quad
(1.892503,1.962478).
\]

Six crossings belong to the defect sector and two to the reference. The
normalized causal checkpoint (delta=1.25) lies in the second band and remains
nontrivial in both deck sectors at the existing enlarged sizes, but it is only
about (0.071) below that benchmark band's upper boundary.

The extra defect roots may be boundary hybridization, transverse levels,
regulator bands or genuine multiple phases. Pfaffian signs alone cannot decide.
Coefficient prediction is therefore pinned until root drift and eigenvector
localization are tracked with size.

See [The finite Pin benchmark has four Pfaffian bands below delta two, and the causal checkpoint is not deep inside one](../0300-0399/392_the_finite_pin_benchmark_has_four_pfaffian_bands_below_delta_two_and_the_causal_checkpoint_is_not_deep_inside_one.md).

### 20.305 The upper finite Pin boundary is a localized defect crossing

The Pfaffian roots can now be separated by their paired-nullspace spatial
density. At fixed (L=2), the upper defect root above the causal checkpoint is

\[
1.321239\quad(M=1),\qquad
1.263992\quad(M=2),\qquad
1.266541\quad(M=3).
\]

Across these widths, roughly one third of the crossing pair remains on the two
defect-core sites, its effective support saturates near eleven sites, and its
outer-edge weight falls

\[
0.4316\longrightarrow0.1010\longrightarrow0.0189.
\]

This is strong finite-system evidence for a defect-localized crossing rather
than a boundary resonance. A low-delta (M=2) control root instead occupies
19.70 of 20 effective sites with uniform-baseline core weight, demonstrating
that the localization diagnostic does not automatically bless every Pfaffian
root.

The causal value (delta=1.25) remains on the nontrivial side at (M=3), but only
by approximately (0.01654). The source construction therefore remains a close
compatibility witness, not a robust prediction. Continuum language is still
pinned until circumference and regulator scaling preserve the localized root
and the neighboring gaps.

See [The upper Pin boundary is defect-localized and nearly converged in transverse width](../0300-0399/393_the_upper_pin_boundary_is_defect_localized_and_nearly_converged_in_transverse_width.md).

### 20.306 Circumference scaling separates a stable defect root from a contaminating reference edge root

At fixed (M=2), the localized defect root is

\[
1.263992\quad(L=2),\qquad
1.261130\quad(L=3),\qquad
1.257363\quad(L=4).
\]

Its central-row weight remains above one half and its enhancement over uniform
core weight increases with circumference. The defect crossing therefore

by about (4.88 times 10^{-4}). The exact causal normalization remains close to

is withdrawn.

The correction is structural: an open-boundary reference Pfaffian is not an
inert comparator once its own edge state crosses. The next invariant must
separate local defect spectral flow from remote edge spectral flow, through a

Writing the transverse slice as (V_y=mu y beta_2+K), with (beta_2^2=I), gives

whenever the denominator is positive. A conservative benchmark bound is

\|\psi_y\|\le\frac{18}{7|y|}
(\|\psi_{y+1}\|+\|\psi_{y-1}\|).

The crucial inverse-radius factor is now proved. The factorial theorem remains

and has unit determinant modulus. At the \(L=2\) benchmark its 64 singular

### 20.322 Standard-Model anomaly cancellation is a triorthogonal code condition

Prakash and Ramya identify the sixteen fields of an \(SO(10)\) generation with
the even-parity sign vectors in \(\{\pm1\}^5\). Their cubic anomaly form

\[
\tau_c(x,y,z)=\sum_\ell c_\ell x_\ell y_\ell z_\ell
\]

is exactly the triorthogonality form after reduction modulo a prime. Removing
\(\nu^c\) produces a \([[15,1,3]]_p\) code for every prime: the fifteen
remaining fields are its coordinates and the removed sterile state is its
logical coordinate.

This independently sharpens three programme results. The same neutral state is
the unique small ternary completion of the fifteen-dimensional Furey matter
TRO, the missing partner of the \(8+7\) Yukawa grading, and the coordinate whose
restoration cancels the code's logical cubic anomaly.

The bridge has strict limits. The anomaly cubic has not been identified with
the exceptional Jordan determinant, and the code does not derive
\(Spin(2,3)\). Moreover, ordinary all-positive ternary Golay coefficients
cannot lift to the required integral anomaly-free \(P\)-lattice. The arithmetic
branch is now a precise search for a mixed-sign distance-five integral
\(P\)-lattice with \(|N|=1\).

See [The Standard-Model triorthogonal code: a new cubic bridge and a Golay integrality gate](../0400-0499/410_standard_model_triorthogonal_code_bridge_and_golay_integrality_gate.md).

Thus the one-step stable planes do not show the resonance that could have
