### 20.324 The completed Furey TRO realizes the five-bit anomaly code as a ternary grading

Every matrix unit in the sixteen-dimensional completed matter TRO can be
labelled by one distinct even-parity sign vector in \(\{\pm1\}^5\). Each of the
five charge coordinates factors through the two-sided linking action as

\[
q_a(E_{ts})=\lambda_a(t)-\rho_a(s).
\]

Consequently every nonzero ternary composition obeys

\[
q(xy^\dagger z)=q(x)-q(y)+q(z).
\]

All 80 nonzero matrix-unit triples pass this identity. The full cubic anomaly
tensor vanishes, while puncturing the unique all-plus \(\nu^c\) arrow leaves
exactly \(-\mathbf1^{\otimes3}\). Restoring the same arrow therefore both closes
the TRO minimally and cancels the code's rank-one cubic defect.

See [The completed Furey TRO carries the SO(10) five-bit code as a Cartan–ternary intertwiner](../0400-0499/412_the_completed_furey_tro_carries_the_so10_five_bit_code_as_a_cartan_ternary_intertwiner.md).

### 20.325 The nonabelian Standard Model roots also descend to the Furey blocks

The fermionic bilinears \(a_i^\dagger a_j\) for the colour coordinates
\(1,2,3\) and weak coordinates \(4,5\) preserve the same sixteen matrix units.
Colour acts on the left \(O_2\) index of \(Q\) and the right \(O_2\) index of
\(u^c,d^c\). Weak isospin acts on the right \(H\) index of \(Q\) and the left
\(H\) index of \(L\). The simple-root commutators close exactly.

Thus the explicit bijection is now an isomorphism of Standard Model gauge
modules with compatible ternary charge grading. The remaining Furey interface
is no longer the gauge representation: it is Lorentz/CAR character,
antiunitary conjugation and production of the external \(H_2(\mathbb R)\)
response.

See [The SO(10) Fock root operators close exactly on the completed Furey matter TRO](../0400-0499/413_the_so10_fock_root_operators_close_exactly_on_the_completed_furey_matter_tro.md).

### 20.326 Dirac doubling is an internal face exchange, not charge conjugation

The doubled-code pairing is the \(SO(10)\) Weyl involution

\[
\sigma(q_1,\ldots,q_5)=(-q_1,-q_2,-q_3,q_4,-q_5),
\]

which preserves the even chiral spinor and pairs all eight \(f^c/f\) states.
On the completed TRO it is a carrier permutation composed with transpose,
\(\Theta(X)=PX^TP\), and reverses the outer order of the TRO triple. The
symmetrized Jordan triple is invariant.

Full charge reversal \(q\mapsto-q\) changes even to odd parity because there
are five signs. It therefore requires the opposite spinor or conjugate ideal.
Dirac doubling, bare dagger, CAR conjugation and mirror doubling are now
mathematically separated.

See [Dirac doubling is an internal Weyl face exchange, while charge conjugation requires the opposite spinor](../0400-0499/414_dirac_doubling_is_an_internal_weyl_face_exchange_while_charge_conjugation_requires_the_opposite_spinor.md).

### 20.327 The neutrino response reaches \(H_2(\mathbb R)\) only after CAR and Higgs dressing

The all-left pair \((\nu,\nu^c)\) has opposite \(B-L\) charges. Its Hermitian
cross response is forbidden, and exchange reciprocity reduces the surviving
diagonal response to a scalar. The internal Weyl pair alone therefore does not
produce the three-dimensional carrier.

After CAR conjugation, the physical pair \((\nu_L,N_R)\) has equal \(B-L\) and
electric charges; before electroweak breaking its mixing is supplied by the
gauge-invariant Higgs dressing \(LH\nu^c\). Exchange-real Hermitian responses
then have the form

\[
\begin{pmatrix}a&x+iy\\x-iy&a\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
\det=a^2-x^2-y^2,
\]

which is unitarily equivalent to \(H_2(\mathbb R)\). This gives a precise
conditional matter-to-\(Spin(2,3)\) route, but the Furey CAR action and positive
spectral kernel still have to force the real form physically.

See [The neutrino face pair yields H2R only after CAR conjugation and Higgs dressing](../0400-0499/415_the_neutrino_face_pair_yields_h2r_only_after_car_conjugation_and_higgs_dressing.md).

### 20.328 The ternary product breaks the \(SO(10)\) representation envelope

The sixteen matter states form one \(SO(10)\) spinor, but a generator is a
symmetry of the Furey structure only if it is a derivation of
\(xy^\dagger z\). Colour and weak roots pass this identity exactly.
Colour–weak leptoquark roots fail it on explicit basis triples. Thus the
five-bit \(SO(10)\) structure organizes the representation without forcing a
physical grand-unified gauge symmetry.

See [The Furey ternary product preserves Standard-Model roots but breaks colour–weak SO(10) roots](../0400-0499/416_the_furey_ternary_product_preserves_sm_roots_but_breaks_color_weak_so10_roots.md).

### 20.329 Puncture-neutral ternary symmetry selects the exact Standard Model Lie algebra

All 45 compact \(so(10)\) oscillator generators were subjected to the complete
ternary derivation constraint. The real constraint rank is 30, leaving

\[
\operatorname{Der}(M_{\rm TRO})\cap so(10)
\cong \mathfrak u(3)\oplus\mathfrak{so}(4)
\]

of dimension 15. Two extra weak pair generators move
\(\nu^c\leftrightarrow e^c\), while the five Cartans act on \(\nu^c\) through
their coefficient sum. Fixing the puncture removes those two roots and one
Cartan direction, leaving

\[
\boxed{
\mathfrak{su}(3)\oplus\mathfrak{su}(2)\oplus\mathfrak u(1).
}
\]

The Standard Model algebra is therefore the intersection of the \(SO(10)\)
spinor envelope, Furey ternary multiplication and anomaly-code puncture.

See [The puncture-neutral ternary stabilizer inside so(10) is exactly the Standard Model Lie algebra](../0400-0499/417_the_puncture_neutral_ternary_stabilizer_inside_so10_is_exactly_the_standard_model_lie_algebra.md).

### 20.330 The global kernel is the standard \(\mathbb Z_6\)

Using \(Y_6=6Y\), the central elements acting trivially on the completed
generation are exactly

\[
(\omega_3^k,(-1)^k,e^{ik\pi/3}),
\qquad k=0,\ldots,5.
\]

Hence the faithful group is

\[
\frac{SU(3)\times SU(2)\times U(1)}{\mathbb Z_6}
\cong S(U(3)\times U(2)).
\]

This exactly matches the global stabilizer selected independently by the
exceptional-Jordan nested flag. The remaining cross-branch problem is no
longer group identification but construction of a canonical equivariant map
between the two \(3+2\) carrier flags.

See [The faithful global group of the puncture-neutral ternary stabilizer has the standard Z6 quotient](../0400-0499/418_the_faithful_global_group_of_the_puncture_neutral_ternary_stabilizer_has_the_standard_z6_quotient.md).

### 20.331 The two \(3+2\) carriers are equivariantly isomorphic but not yet canonically identified

The exceptional construction supplies a colour \(\mathbb C^3\) from
\(\mathbb O=\mathbb C\oplus\mathbb C^3\) and a weak \(\mathbb C^2\) from the
embedded \(H_2(\mathbb C)\subset H_3(\mathbb C)\). This matches the oscillator
split \(\mathbb C^5=\mathbb C^3\oplus\mathbb C^2\).

Solving the complete intertwiner commutant gives

\[
T=\alpha I_3\oplus\beta I_2.
\]

Thus the common faithful group guarantees existence but leaves two complex
scalars. Unitarity leaves two phases; matching only the combined five-volume
leaves one phase; matching separate normalized three- and two-volumes leaves
\(\mathbb Z_3\times\mathbb Z_2\). The order-six remainder resembles, but is not
yet identified with, the faithful gauge kernel.

The next selection test must use the octonionic/Jordan and Furey/TRO products.
Group equality alone cannot make the synthesis canonical.

See [The common exceptional and oscillator 3+2 flag has a two-scalar intertwiner ambiguity](../0400-0499/419_the_common_exceptional_and_oscillator_3plus2_flag_has_a_two_scalar_intertwiner_ambiguity.md).

### 20.332 Exceptional multiplication fixes the colour phase but not the weak phase

The actual octonion product sharpens the equivariant-map ambiguity. In the
decomposition \(\mathbb O\cong\mathbb C\oplus\mathbb C^3\), its vector part
contains \(\overline{a\times b}\). Under \(a,b\mapsto\alpha a,\alpha b\),
product compatibility requires

\[
\overline{\alpha}^{,2}=\alpha,
\qquad\text{hence}\qquad
|\alpha|=1,\quad \alpha^3=1.
\]

The colour ambiguity is therefore reduced to \(\mathbb Z_3\). By contrast,
the weak Jordan data are built from rank-one observables \(vv^\dagger\), which
are blind to \(v\mapsto\beta v\) for every \(\beta\in U(1)\). The product-level
remainder is consequently \(\mathbb Z_3\times U(1)\), not yet the finite
Standard Model kernel.

If a common normalized top line identifies
\(\Lambda^5\mathbb C^5\) with
\(\Lambda^3\mathbb C^3\otimes\Lambda^2\mathbb C^2\), then
\(\alpha^3\beta^2=1\) reduces the ambiguity to
\(\mathbb Z_3\times\mathbb Z_2\cong\mathbb Z_6\). This is a conditional match,
not a canonical identification: the nested Jordan flag itself has not yet
been shown to supply the required weak determinant phase.

See [The octonion cross product fixes the colour phase, but the weak Jordan algebra is phase-blind](../0400-0499/420_the_octonion_cross_product_fixes_the_colour_phase_but_the_weak_jordan_algebra_is_phase_blind.md).

### 20.333 The bare weak Jordan flag cannot canonically trivialize its spinor determinant line

The remaining weak phase is subject to an exact no-go theorem. If
\(W=\mathbb C^2\), the central phase acts on observables by

\[
(e^{i\theta}I)A(e^{i\theta}I)^\dagger=A,
\]

but acts on the weak top line by

\[
v_1\wedge v_2\longmapsto e^{2i\theta}v_1\wedge v_2.
\]

Consequently no nonzero vector of \(\Lambda^2W\) can be naturally selected by
data intrinsic to \(H_2(\mathbb C)\). The Jordan determinant
\(ab-|z|^2\) is a real quadratic form on observables and does not evade this
central-phase blindness.

The exceptional stabilizer can make the combined top line
\(\Lambda^3\mathbb C^3\otimes\Lambda^2\mathbb C^2\) a trivial
representation, but an invariant line is not a canonically phased vector.
Therefore the unconditional ambiguity remains \(\mathbb Z_3\times U(1)\).
Reaching the faithful \(\mathbb Z_6\) requires additional phase-sensitive
sewing data, with the Furey CAR vacuum/top state and Higgs-dressed pairing now
the leading candidates.

See [The weak Jordan flag determines only a projective spinor and cannot canonically supply its volume phase](../0400-0499/421_the_weak_jordan_flag_determines_only_a_projective_spinor_and_cannot_canonically_supply_its_volume_phase.md).

### 20.334 A matched CAR real structure supplies the missing weak \(\mathbb Z_2\), conditionally

There is a concrete phase-sensitive replacement for the absent Jordan datum.
If the exceptional and Furey weak carriers have specified antiunitaries
\(C_E,C_F\), then a unitary scalar comparison \(T=\beta I_2\) satisfying

\[
TC_E=C_FT
\]

obeys \(\beta=\bar\beta\) in matched real bases. Hence \(\beta=\pm1\), and
together with the octonionic \(\alpha^3=1\) this gives
\(\mathbb Z_3\times\mathbb Z_2\cong\mathbb Z_6\).

The qualification is essential. An antiunitary may be rephased as
\(C\mapsto e^{i\phi}C\) without changing \(C^2\) or its induced conjugation of
the CAR algebra. The allowed pair then becomes
\(\beta=\pm e^{i\phi/2}\). A CAR particle-hole automorphism or vacuum projector
therefore does not canonically fix the comparison phase. The live sewing
problem is to derive phase-matched antiunitaries, perhaps from a normalized
vacuum-to-top amplitude, Pfaffian orientation or Higgs-dressed response.

See [A specified CAR real structure reduces the weak phase to a sign but does not canonically choose that real structure](../0400-0499/422_a_specified_car_real_structure_reduces_the_weak_phase_to_a_sign_but_does_not_canonically_choose_that_real_structure.md).

### 20.335 Response positivity validates the carrier but is blind to the antiunitary phase

For \(J=\sigma_x\mathcal K\), the fixed Hermitian responses are exactly

\[
R(a,c)=\begin{pmatrix}a&c\\ \bar c&a\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
R\ge0\iff a\ge|c|.
\]

This is the three-dimensional Lorentz cone and is unitarily Jordan-isomorphic
to \(H_2(\mathbb R)_+\). The response branch to
\(Sp(4,\mathbb R)\cong Spin_0(2,3)\) therefore remains intact.

However, \(J_\phi=e^{i\phi}J\) has the same square and exactly the same adjoint
action on every response. Its fixed cone, determinant and spectral positivity
cannot determine \(\phi\). Indeed, positive rank-one fixed residues exist with
every complex off-diagonal phase. A whole spectral family is realifiable in
one face convention only when
\(\operatorname{Im}(c_n\bar c_m)=0\) for every pair, a condition not implied by
positivity.

Thus the Higgs-dressed response can establish the physical Jordan carrier
without phase-matching the exceptional and Furey antiunitaries. That latter
datum must be a phased amplitude, Pfaffian orientation or explicit
state-level sewing map rather than an adjoint-invariant response condition.

See [Exchange-real spectral positivity supports the Spin(2,3) carrier but cannot phase-match the antiunitaries](../0400-0499/423_exchange_real_spectral_positivity_supports_the_spin23_carrier_but_cannot_phase_match_the_antiunitaries.md).

### 20.336 One Higgs–Dirac mass aligns the complete free spectral family

For a complex mass \(m=|m|e^{i\varphi}\), the fixed-helicity positive-energy
projector is

\[
P_+(k)=\frac12
\begin{pmatrix}
1+k/\omega_k&m/\omega_k\\
\bar m/\omega_k&1-k/\omega_k
\end{pmatrix}.
\]

Every off-diagonal residue has phase \(\varphi\), independent of momentum.
Consequently one fixed chiral rotation \(D_\varphi\) maps the entire free
spectral family into \(H_2(\mathbb R)_+\). The Higgs-generated mass therefore
does supply a genuine relative phase alignment and selects a rotated real
Jordan slice inside \(H_2(\mathbb C)\).

For one isolated generation, however, \(\varphi\) changes under the relative
chiral field redefinition that removes the mass phase. It is not an absolute
observable and cannot alone compare independently defined exceptional and
Furey carriers. Multiple effective mass phases admit one real slice exactly
when their pairwise products have vanishing imaginary parts. This gives a
sharp interacting and multi-Higgs falsification gate.

See [A single Higgs–Dirac mass aligns all free spectral residues into one rotated H2(R) slice](../0400-0499/424_a_single_higgs_dirac_mass_aligns_all_free_spectral_residues_into_one_rotated_h2r_slice.md).

### 20.337 A fixed flavor mass matrix realifies every free pole without erasing CKM-type CP

For \(M=U_LDU_R^\dagger\), the multiflavor fixed-helicity Hamiltonian

\[
H(k)=\begin{pmatrix}kI&M\\M^\dagger&-kI\end{pmatrix}
\]

is transformed by the one momentum-independent frame
\(\operatorname{diag}(U_L,U_R)\) into a direct sum of real two-face Dirac
blocks. Its positive-energy projector therefore decomposes into rank-one
boundary rays of \(H_2(\mathbb R)_+\) for every mass eigenmode and momentum.

This does not force flavor CP to vanish. Two fermion sectors can be separately
realified while their relative left frame
\(V=U_{Lu}^\dagger U_{Ld}\) has a nonzero Jarlskog invariant. The real
operation acts on the face blocks, not entrywise on the relative flavor frame.

The theorem yields a direct sum of carriers, not automatically a universal
\(H_2(\mathbb R)\otimes A_{\rm flavor}\) factorization. For interacting poles
and cuts, a fixed biunitary frame is a new dynamical gate; noncommuting left or
right spectral positive products falsify it.

See [A fixed mass matrix aligns the full free multiflavor spectrum while relative singular frames retain CP](../0400-0499/425_a_fixed_mass_matrix_aligns_the_full_free_multiflavor_spectrum_while_relative_singular_frames_retain_cp.md).

### 20.338 Mixed Yukawa spurions rotate the free real frame without destroying local positivity

For a single mass matrix \(M=U_LDU_R^\dagger\), every real functional-calculus
correction

\[
C(s)=M f_s(M^\dagger M)
\]

retains the same left and right singular frames. This protects the real
two-face decomposition against flavor-blind factors and single-spurion
polynomials.

The protection fails generically for a weak-partner insertion

\[
C_\varepsilon=(I+\varepsilon NN^\dagger)M.
\]

When \([MM^\dagger,NN^\dagger]\ne0\), the corrected and uncorrected positive
products do not share a left eigenframe. Standard-Model one-loop Yukawa flow
contains precisely such mixed partner-sector matrix data. Positivity survives;
what fails is one globally fixed embedding of the real carrier.

The natural surviving object is therefore potentially a bundle of local
\(H_2(\mathbb R)\) slices with connections
\(U_L^\dagger dU_L\) and \(U_R^\dagger dU_R\). Whether their holonomy is tied
to CKM/PMNS CP or to the exceptional/Furey sewing phase is now a concrete open
branch rather than an asserted identification.

See [Single-spurion self-energies preserve the real face frame, but mixed Yukawa spurions generically rotate it](../0400-0499/426_single_spurion_self_energies_preserve_the_real_face_frame_but_mixed_yukawa_spurions_generically_rotate_it.md).

### 20.339 The running frame has an exact connection, but one RG coordinate has no curvature

For a nondegenerate left spectral product
\(L(t)=\Lambda+tK+O(t^2)\), the parallel-transport eigenframe connection is

\[
A_{ij}=\frac{K_{ij}}{\lambda_j-\lambda_i},
\qquad i\ne j.
\]

For the mixed-spurion deformation \(C(t)=(I+tH_N)D\), this becomes

\[
A_{ij}=\frac{d_i^2+d_j^2}{d_j^2-d_i^2}(H_N)_{ij}.
\]

Thus frame running is explicit and is amplified near spectral degeneracy. But
on a one-dimensional RG line, \(\mathcal A=A(t)dt\) has identically zero
curvature because \(dt\wedge dt=0\). Its open-path rotation is not by itself a
gauge-invariant CP observable.

A curvature/holonomy bridge therefore needs at least two physical parameter
directions, a closed loop, a singularity or an independently fixed comparison
frame. This prevents premature identification of Yukawa running with a Berry
phase while leaving a precise two-parameter continuation available.

See [The mixed-spurion flow has an exact frame connection, but one-parameter running has no intrinsic curvature](../0400-0499/427_the_mixed_spurion_flow_has_an_exact_frame_connection_but_one_parameter_running_has_no_intrinsic_curvature.md).

### 20.340 Two-parameter curvature is not automatically flavor CP

For \(L(x,y)=\Lambda+xX+yY+\cdots\), the isolated-eigenline curvature is

\[
F^{(i)}_{xy}=2\operatorname{Im}\sum_{j\ne i}
\frac{X_{ij}Y_{ji}}{(\lambda_i-\lambda_j)^2}.
\]

This is genuine rephasing-invariant geometry, but it is not automatically a
CP-odd observable. Choosing real symmetric \(\Lambda,X\) and the Hermitian
tangent \(Y=i[\Lambda,X]\) produces nonzero curvature even though
\(\operatorname{ImTr}[\Lambda,X]^3=0\) and the original pair is CP-real.

By contrast, the commutator cubic
\(\operatorname{ImTr}[H_u,H_d]^3\) is basis invariant, CP odd and nonzero for
the certified complex CKM-type frame. Any proposed holonomy explanation of
flavor CP must reproduce those transformation properties and vanish on the
CP-real counterexample. Generic Berry language is insufficient.

See [Two-parameter frame curvature is real geometry but is not automatically a Jarlskog CP invariant](../0400-0499/428_two_parameter_frame_curvature_is_real_geometry_but_is_not_automatically_a_jarlskog_cp_invariant.md).

### 20.341 A non-Abelian character carries the Jarlskog cubic, while its determinant is blind

Let \(C=[H_u,H_d]\). Since \(C\) is traceless and anti-Hermitian,

\[
\operatorname{ImTr}e^{\epsilon C}
=\frac{\epsilon^3}{6}\operatorname{ImTr}C^3+O(\epsilon^5).
\]

This character is basis invariant, reverses sign under coefficient
conjugation, and vanishes in CP-real and two-generation cases. It therefore
passes the transformation-law gates that generic frame curvature failed.

At the same time,

\[
\det e^{\epsilon C}=e^{\epsilon\operatorname{Tr}C}=1.
\]

The continuous flavor CP data live in the traceless non-Abelian eigenphase
distribution and cannot be carried by the ordinary determinant line. The
discrete \(\mathbb Z_6\) determinant sewing and Jarlskog holonomy are therefore
distinct layers. Unifying them requires a richer flag representation with a
central quotient and a non-Abelian character, not one top-line phase.

See [The commutator exponential has the Jarlskog cubic as its leading CP-odd character but trivial determinant](../0400-0499/429_the_commutator_exponential_has_the_jarlskog_cubic_as_its_leading_cp_odd_character_but_trivial_determinant.md).

### 20.342 The actual flavor plaquette has the same Jarlskog leading character

The rectangular group commutator

\[
W(t)=e^{itH_u}e^{itH_d}e^{-itH_u}e^{-itH_d}
\]

is a genuine non-Abelian plaquette for constant formal connection components.
Its small-loop character satisfies

\[
\operatorname{ImTr}W(t)
=-\frac{t^6}{6}\operatorname{ImTr}[H_u,H_d]^3+O(t^7)
\]

for the stated orientation. The certificate finds normalized ratios converging
to \(-1/6\), verifies CP sign reversal, and gives zero for a CP-real frame.

As for every group commutator, \(\det W=1\). The result strengthens the
non-Abelian flag branch but does not yet make the loop physical: the programme
must derive two independent connection directions from Higgs, response,
Furey or exceptional data. Until then it is a correctly transforming
algebraic plaquette rather than an observable Wilson loop.

See [A rectangular flavor group-commutator loop has the Jarlskog cubic as its leading CP-odd character](../0400-0499/430_a_rectangular_flavor_group_commutator_loop_has_the_jarlskog_cubic_as_its_leading_cp_odd_character.md).

### 20.343 The flavor plaquette is an inner ternary automorphism after generation amplification

For an amplified rectangular Furey component

\[
M_{p,q}(\mathbb C)\otimes M_3(\mathbb C)
\cong M_{3p,3q}(\mathbb C),
\]

every two-sided unitary action \(\Phi(X)=LXR^\dagger\) satisfies

\[
\Phi(XY^\dagger Z)=\Phi(X)\Phi(Y)^\dagger\Phi(Z).
\]

Taking \(L=I_p\otimes W(t)\) and \(R=I_q\otimes W(t)\) therefore lifts the
Jarlskog flavor plaquette to an exact inner automorphism of the
generation-amplified completed TRO. A universal flavor action commutes with
the independent one-generation gauge action and preserves the five-bit
grading.

This establishes compatibility, not origin. The original Furey TRO contains
one generation and does not derive the \(M_3\) factor, the Yukawa matrices or
the two loop directions. Moreover, physical sector-dependent frames must glue
at shared linking vertices; independent choices on each rectangle would
overcount flavor symmetry and erase CKM/PMNS constraints.

See [The flavor plaquette lifts to an inner ternary automorphism only after generation amplification of the Furey TRO](../0400-0499/431_the_flavor_plaquette_lifts_to_an_inner_ternary_automorphism_only_after_generation_amplification_of_the_furey_tro.md).

### 20.344 The completed Furey graph itself supplies exactly two flavor cycles

The completed matter graph has five linking vertices and six arrows, so its
connected cycle rank is

\[
b_1=6-5+1=2.
\]

The two cycles are naturally distinguished by the \(C\) and \(D\) branches:

\[
H\to O_2\to C\to E\to H,
\qquad
H\to O_2\to D\to E\to H.
\]

After generation amplification, edge transports transform by independent
vertex frames, while both based cycle holonomies transform by simultaneous
conjugation at \(H\). Their group commutator therefore has a gauge-invariant
trace character and unit determinant. This supplies a source-defined
topological home for the Jarlskog plaquette.

Removing the \(\nu^c:E\leftarrow D\) edge lowers the cycle rank to one and
eliminates the internal group-commutator construction. The sterile completion
now has four exact roles: ternary closure, cancellation of the puncture cubic,
creation of the second relational cycle and availability of a non-Abelian
flavor plaquette. The graph does not yet determine the edge transports, so it
does not predict CP by topology alone.

See [The completed Furey linking graph has exactly two independent flavor cycles and a gauge-covariant plaquette](../0400-0499/432_the_completed_furey_linking_graph_has_exactly_two_independent_flavor_cycles_and_a_gauge_covariant_plaquette.md).

### 20.345 The two graph cycles separate Abelian line phases from traceless flavor CP

Modulo vertex gauge, the flavor-transport data are a pair
\((U_C,U_D)\in U(3)^2\) up to simultaneous conjugation. Writing

\[
U_C=z_C\widetilde U_C,
\qquad
U_D=z_D\widetilde U_D,
\qquad
\widetilde U_C,\widetilde U_D\in SU(3),
\]

exhibits two Abelian determinant holonomies and two traceless parts. Their
group commutator cancels \(z_C,z_D\) exactly:

\[
[U_C,U_D]=[\widetilde U_C,\widetilde U_D]\in SU(3).
\]

Thus the completed graph carries both central line data and a determinant-one
CP-sensitive plaquette, but neither determines the other. The latter vanishes
as an imaginary trace on an embedded two-flavor \(SU(2)\) pair and can be
nonzero for three flavors.

This provides the correct layered architecture for a synthesis but not yet a
relation between layers. Identifying the two flavor determinant holonomies
with the weak/color/hypercharge data behind the faithful \(\mathbb Z_6\)
requires an additional exceptional/Furey sewing law.

See [The two-cycle representation variety separates central-line holonomies from the traceless CP plaquette](../0400-0499/433_the_two_cycle_representation_variety_separates_central_line_holonomies_from_the_traceless_cp_plaquette.md).

### 20.346 Polar decomposition derives graph transport from flavor amplitudes

For an invertible complex edge amplitude \(A_e:F_s\to F_t\), the polar factor

\[
T_e=A_e(A_e^\dagger A_e)^{-1/2}
\]

is a unique unitary satisfying the exact endpoint covariance

\[
A_e\mapsto g_tA_eg_s^\dagger
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
T_e\mapsto g_tT_eg_s^\dagger.
\]

The two completed-graph holonomies and their plaquette can therefore be
derived from complex amplitudes rather than assigned freely. The positive
polar factors retain singular values, while the unitary factors carry
relational transport. Their determinant phases obey
\(\det T_e=\det A_e/|\det A_e|\), giving a concrete source for the central
cycle holonomies.

Rank deficiency is the exact obstruction: the polar factor becomes only a
partial isometry and its extension over the null space is noncanonical.
Repeated nonzero singular values are harmless. The remaining physical issue
is whether the Standard-Model/Furey Yukawa amplitudes belong to individual
edges or only to gauge-invariant Higgs-dressed paths.

See [Polar decomposition canonically extracts cycle transports from invertible flavor edge amplitudes](../0400-0499/434_polar_decomposition_canonically_extracts_cycle_transports_from_invertible_flavor_edge_amplitudes.md).

### 20.347 Higgs completion reveals four Yukawa cycles and corrects the matter-loop interpretation

The physical cyclic-Yukawa topology contains two additional arrows
\(h_C:C\to H\) and \(h_D:D\to H\). The connected graph therefore has eight
edges, five vertices and cycle rank

\[
b_1=8-5+1=4.
\]

The four natural cycles are the up, down, charged-lepton and neutrino Yukawa
paths. For their unitary polar transports,

\[
U_C^{\rm matter}=U_eU_u,
\qquad
U_D^{\rm matter}=U_\nu U_d.
\]

Thus the earlier two matter loops are paired quark–lepton composites, not the
individual up/down generators. The quark plaquette is \([U_u,U_d]\), while the
lepton plaquette is \([U_\nu,U_e]\); the commutator of the two matter composites
is a different cross-sector invariant.

Removing \(\nu^c\) lowers the augmented rank from four to three and removes
the neutrino cycle, but it does not eliminate the quark plaquette. This
corrects the strongest causal reading of the sterile-edge result while
preserving its exact ternary, anomaly and neutral-lepton topology roles.

See [The Higgs-augmented linking graph has four Yukawa cycles, and the two matter cycles are paired composites](../0400-0499/435_the_higgs_augmented_linking_graph_has_four_yukawa_cycles_and_the_two_matter_cycles_are_paired_composites.md).

### 20.348 A flavor-blind locked Higgs cannot generate the non-Abelian plaquettes

If \(h_C,h_D\) are block components of one flavor-singlet Higgs, their unitary
polar transports are central:

\[
T_{h_C}=z_CI_3,
\qquad
T_{h_D}=z_DI_3.
\]

They cancel exactly from the sector commutators,

\[
[U_u,U_d]=[M_u,M_d],
\qquad
[U_\nu,U_e]=[M_\nu,M_e],
\]

where the \(M\)'s are the matter-path transports. They shift individual cycle
determinants by \(z_C^3,z_D^3\), but conjugate phases cancel in the paired
matter cycles.

Therefore the Higgs block topology selects and weights the paths but cannot by
itself generate CKM/PMNS noncommutativity in the flavor-blind one-doublet
case. Non-Abelian CP lies in the matter/Yukawa transport. Higgs magnitudes and
two-doublet dynamics remain physical and are not removed by this unitary
phase cancellation.

See [Flavor-blind one-Higgs locking cancels from sector plaquettes and only shifts central cycle phases](../0400-0499/436_flavor_blind_one_higgs_locking_cancels_from_sector_plaquettes_and_only_shifts_central_cycle_phases.md).

### 20.349 A massless neutrino breaks full polar holonomy but not canonical leptonic CP

For a rank-two Dirac-neutrino amplitude, the polar factor is a partial isometry.
Its full-unitary extensions differ by an arbitrary phase on the null line. A
generic lepton plaquette trace depends on that phase and is therefore not an
intrinsic observable of the rank-deficient amplitude.

The shared-left Hermitian spurion

\[
H_\nu=M_\nu M_\nu^\dagger
\]

is extension independent, as is

\[
\operatorname{ImTr}[H_e,H_\nu]^3.
\]

The certificate gives a nonzero value with one exactly zero neutrino mass and
also verifies a nonzero PMNS quartet invariant under rephasing the massless
eigenstate. Thus one massless neutrino does not eliminate Dirac-type flavor CP,
but it requires the graph formulation to use support projectors, partial
isometries or Hermitian mass-squared composites rather than an arbitrarily
completed \(U(3)\) polar connection.

See [With one massless neutrino the polar-unitary plaquette is ambiguous, but the mass-squared commutator CP invariant remains canonical](../0400-0499/437_with_one_massless_neutrino_the_polar_unitary_plaquette_is_ambiguous_but_the_mass_squared_commutator_cp_invariant_remains_canonical.md).

### 20.350 Projector quadrilaterals give the canonical rank-deficient flavor holonomy

Let \(P_i^e\) and \(P_j^\nu\) be charged-lepton and neutrino spectral
eigenprojectors on the shared left flavor space. The alternating word

\[
\mathcal B_{ik;j\ell}
=\operatorname{Tr}(P_i^eP_j^\nu P_k^eP_\ell^\nu)
\]

is a closed projective/groupoid path and equals the corresponding PMNS
quartet. It is invariant under all eigenvector phases, including rephasing of
an isolated massless neutrino eigenline, while its imaginary part reverses
under CP.

For three nondegenerate eigenvalues, allowing one to be zero,

\[
|\operatorname{ImTr}[H_e,H_\nu]^3|
=6|\operatorname{Im}\mathcal B|
\left|\prod_{i<k}(a_i-a_k)\right|
\left|\prod_{j<\ell}(b_j-b_\ell)\right|.
\]

This supplies the correct canonical holonomy when the polar transport is only
a partial isometry. Exact degeneracies require higher-rank non-Abelian
projectors, but an isolated zero mass is not an obstruction.

See [Projector-quadrilateral holonomy recovers the Jarlskog quartet without extending rank-deficient polar transport](../0400-0499/438_projector_quadrilateral_holonomy_recovers_the_jarlskog_quartet_without_extending_rank_deficient_polar_transport.md).

### 20.351 The canonical CP quadrilateral lives in the commutant of the real face carrier

For factor-local combined operators

\[
X_r=S_r\otimes P_r,
\qquad
S_r\in H_2(\mathbb R),
\]

the alternating four-step trace factorizes:

\[
\operatorname{Tr}(X_1X_2X_3X_4)
=\operatorname{Tr}_{\rm face}(S_1S_2S_3S_4)
\operatorname{Tr}_{\rm flavor}(P_1P_2P_3P_4).
\]

The face factor is real, so the CP-odd imaginary part remains entirely in the
flavor projector quadrilateral. For one common normalized rank-one real face
ray, the combined six-dimensional trace equals the PMNS/CKM quartet exactly.

The face Jordan action and flavor holonomy commute, tensor-product residues
remain positive, and flavor partial trace preserves the
\(H_2(\mathbb R)_+\) marginal. This establishes exact compatibility of the
local \(Spin_0(2,3)\) response carrier with nonzero complex flavor CP in its
commutant. It does not prove radiative factor locality; entangled
face–flavor corrections remain the decisive interacting gate.

See [The projector CP quadrilateral factors through the commutant of the exchange-real H2(R) face carrier](../0400-0499/439_the_projector_cp_quadrilateral_factors_through_the_commutant_of_the_exchange_real_h2r_face_carrier.md).

### 20.352 Marginal-safe entanglement splits between real and complex parents

The lowest face-odd entangler is \(\sigma_y\otimes F\) with Hermitian flavor
coefficient \(F\). It preserves the unweighted real face marginal exactly when
\(\operatorname{Tr}F=0\). Relative to a chosen flavor real structure,

\[
F=S+iK,
\qquad
S\in\operatorname{Sym}_3^0(\mathbb R),
\quad
K\in\operatorname{Alt}_3(\mathbb R).
\]

The three \(iK\) directions satisfy

\[
\sigma_y\otimes iK=-J\otimes K\in H_6(\mathbb R),
\]

while the five \(S\) directions are purely imaginary combined Hermitian
operators and require \(H_6(\mathbb C)\) in that real structure. Both sectors
have open positive neighborhoods, with the isotropic bound
\(|\epsilon|\|F\|_{\rm op}\le c\), and both pass gauge and partial-trace tests.

The real versus complex parent is therefore not selected by positivity or the
external \(H_2(\mathbb R)\) marginal. It is selected only if a source-defined
flavor antiunitary makes the 3+5 split covariant or an explicit interacting
calculation populates the five-dimensional complex leakage sector.

### 20.353 A universal flavor reality selects an orthogonal subgroup and kills Jarlskog CP

The 5+3 decomposition of the traceless flavor octet is preserved not by all
of \(U(3)\), but by the normalizer of the standard real algebra:

\[
N_{U(3)}(M_3(\mathbb R))=U(1)\cdot O(3).
\]

Generic complex flavor rotations mix the symmetric and
imaginary-antisymmetric sectors. More decisively, if one involutive
antiunitary fixes both Hermitian flavor spurions, a basis exists in which both
are real symmetric and

\[
\operatorname{ImTr}[H_u,H_d]^3=0.
\]

Each sector separately admits an eigenbasis conjugation, so flavor complexity
can be viewed as mismatch between sector real forms. But that mismatch is not
yet a derived observable: the individual sector antiunitaries require phase
choices. A viable graded-real theory must use a sector-dependent or genuinely
combined action, break the universal antiunitary, or accept the complex
parent. One unbroken universal flavor conjugation is incompatible with
observed Jarlskog CP.

### 20.354 Sector conjugations form a phase torus; the relative spectral flag is canonical

For a nondegenerate Hermitian spurion \(H=VDV^\dagger\), all involutive
antiunitaries fixing it are

J_{\boldsymbol\eta}
=V\operatorname{diag}(\eta_1,\eta_2,\eta_3)KV^\dagger,
\qquad |\eta_i|=1.
\]

They form a \(U(1)^3\) family. Consequently, the linear product of two
independently chosen sector antiunitaries varies with eigenline phases while

canonical CKM/PMNS observable.

The canonical mismatch is instead the relative position of the two spectral
flags, measured by phase-independent projector quadrilaterals and
\(\operatorname{ImTr}[H_u,H_d]^3\). The existence of one common antiunitary is
also canonical: a nonzero Jarlskog invariant obstructs it. A Furey or
exceptional conjugation could make a relative antiunitary product meaningful
only by fixing the entire eigenline phase torus through additional source
data.

### 20.355 Generation-blind Furey conjugation cannot select flavor reality

Under simple three-generation replication, every one-generation internal

\[
U(3)/O(3),
\]

and the full \(U(3)\) action fixes no distinguished point of this space. Thus
the dagger, particle-hole and CAR conjugations of the one-generation Furey
system cannot, by themselves, choose the flavor real structure or resolve its

This is a sharp boundary on the synthesis: the one-generation algebra can
control gauge representations and ternary composition, while flavor reality
requires a generation-sensitive operator, nontrivial inter-generation
sewing, a boundary condition, an anomaly datum or dynamics. The canonical

### 20.365 Physical logical-weight strata obstruct transversal full (Sp(4))

generates the complete order-51840 group.

### 20.369 A positive integral scalar response supplies the finite mutual shear

is positive with eigenvalues 1 and 3 and is exactly the Dirichlet-to-Neumann
response of a scalar interval with \(m=\sqrt3\) and
\(mL=\operatorname{arcosh}2\). Its quadratic boundary action induces the
integral canonical shear

\mathcal S_X=
\begin{pmatrix}I&0\\X&I\end{pmatrix}
\in Sp(4,\mathbb Z).
\]

The off-diagonal coefficient survives reduction modulo every prime. At
\(p=3\), composing with an already-certified diagonal charge shear and
squaring produces exactly the mutual cross shear that completes
\(Sp(4,\mathbb F_3)\).

This is the first explicit generator-level vertical bridge from a positive

logical symplectic group. The unresolved step is physical rather than

### 20.370 Positive response plus boundary duality generates the integral carrier

Unit self-shears remove the diagonal part of the positive integral response

mutual-root shear. Conjugating it by a local boundary Legendre transform
produces the elementary port-mixing matrix

A=
\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\0&1\end{pmatrix}
\]

with its inverse-transpose momentum action. Together with the two long-root
self-shears and their Fourier conjugates, these are the standard elementary

polarization dualities, they generate all of \(Sp(4,\mathbb Z)\).

The same fixed integral matrices reduce to the full \(Sp(4,\mathbb F_2)\) and
\(Sp(4,\mathbb F_3)\) groups. The algebraic/arithmetic carrier is therefore
complete. The remaining gates are physical: canonical normalization,
implementation of boundary Legendre duality, and identification of these
ports with the code and Furey/Standard-Model observables.

### 20.371 Free-scalar positivity does not canonically quantize the boundary lattice

For a noncompact scalar, the canonical field redefinition

\[
q\mapsto\lambda q,
\qquad
p\mapsto p/\lambda
\]

preserves the symplectic form but sends \(X\mapsto X/\lambda^2\). The positive
integral response can therefore be made fractional or irrational without
altering its canonical or positivity structure. Independent positive port
rescalings act by \(X\mapsto D^{-T}XD^{-1}\).

The unit-independent response datum is instead

\[
\frac{X_{12}}{\sqrt{X_{11}X_{22}}}=-\frac12.
\]

Accordingly, the integral \(Sp(4,\mathbb Z)\) completion is conditional on an
additional quantized boundary lattice. Credible sources are compact phases
and gauge fluxes, topological action levels, a compatible code inverse limit
or genus-two homology. The free noncompact scalar supplies positivity and the

### 20.372 Compact phase/flux data repair the lattice normalization, but change the global theory

The normalization no-go has an exact conditional resolution. If the two-port carrier is a principally polarized symplectic torus

\[
\mathbb R^4/\mathbb Z^4,
\]

then its primitive intersection lattice is part of the object and its arithmetic automorphism group is \(Sp(4,\mathbb Z)\). An integral symmetric response \(K\) defines the well-defined shear \((q,p)\mapsto(q,p+Kq)\), whereas a nonintegral rescaling generally fails to descend because different representatives of \(q\) produce inequivalent representatives of \(p\).

This makes the previously conditional integral bridge exact *after* the compact phase-space structure is supplied. It also provides compatible finite reductions and the metaplectic interpretation of the code's Fourier and quadratic-phase operations. For odd levels, \(Q_K(q)=q^TKq/2\) is the required quadratic refinement; even levels need additional phase/refinement data.

Two caveats are decisive. First, compact angles alone give \(T^*\mathbb T^2\), not automatically a compact four-torus. Second, an ordinary quadratic potential is not globally periodic on \(\mathbb T^2\); a Villain, theta, periodic-potential or topological completion must replace it. The programme has therefore isolated a credible arithmetic carrier, not yet derived it from Furey matter or Standard-Model dynamics.

See [Compact phase/flux variables supply a canonical \(Sp(4,\mathbb Z)\) lattice, but require periodic completion](../0400-0499/460_compact_phase_flux_variables_supply_a_canonical_sp4z_lattice_but_require_periodic_completion.md).

### 20.373 The scalar mutual ratio has arithmetic shadows but is not a shared invariant

The unit-independent scalar datum may be written without square roots as

\[
\rho=\frac{X_{12}^2}{X_{11}X_{22}}=\frac14.
\]

It has a coherent reduction \(\rho_p=4^{-1}\) at every odd prime. Characteristic three is deceptive: \(4^{-1}=1\), and the reduced response matrix has determinant zero. The qutrit code therefore sees a rank-one shadow of a full-rank positive real response.

This does not furnish an independent prediction. The code's available diagonal logical shears alter \(\rho\), so the ratio is not invariant under the logical operation set. Likewise the positive \(H_2(\mathbb R)\) cone contains every \(\rho\in[0,1]\), and the Furey real-face carrier alone cannot select \(1/4\). What survives across the three descriptions is the existence of one nonzero mutual direction beyond two self-relations. A shared numerical value would require a separate theta-kernel, linking-amplitude, inverse-limit or stress-sum-rule derivation.

See [The one-quarter mutual ratio has coherent prime shadows, but is not a code or Furey invariant](../0400-0499/461_the_one_quarter_mutual_ratio_has_coherent_prime_shadows_but_is_not_a_code_or_furey_invariant.md).

### 20.374 Periodic completion produces Poisson duality, not yet a unitary duality defect

The local quadratic response has a canonical positive periodic completion,

\[
\Theta_{X,t}(q)=\sum_{n\in\mathbb Z^2}e^{-\pi t(q+n)^TX(q+n)}.
\]

Poisson summation rewrites it on the reciprocal lattice with quadratic form \(X^{-1}/t\), while its local logarithmic Hessian tends to \(2\pi tX\). This supplies a genuine compact value/flux duality and repairs the global angular-variable defect.

It does not yet supply the code gate. The positive theta kernel has nonconstant magnitude and describes Euclidean heat weighting, whereas the finite metaplectic shear is an oscillatory unitary quadratic phase. Passing between them requires analytic continuation, a quantized level and a chosen quadratic refinement. Moreover, \(X\) is the \(A_2\) Cartan form with discriminant group \(\mathbb Z_3\); this explains the exceptional role of three but supplies only one order-three discriminant coordinate, not the full \((\mathbb F_3)^4\) logical phase space.

See [Villain–theta completion restores periodicity and Poisson duality, but not a unitary code gate](../0400-0499/462_villain_theta_completion_restores_periodicity_and_poisson_duality_but_not_a_unitary_code_gate.md).

### 20.375 The \(A_2\) discriminant form supplies one qutrit per face, not the mutual gate

The determinant-three response has an exact finite quantization. Its discriminant form is \(D\cong\mathbb Z_3\) with \(q(a)=a^2/3\), and the Weil action on \(\mathbb C[D]\) is the standard one-qutrit Fourier/quadratic Clifford representation. Two same-sign copies therefore give a nine-dimensional two-qutrit Hilbert space and the required four-dimensional finite Weyl phase space.

This sharpens rather than removes the relational gap. The direct-sum quadratic phase factorizes, and the intrinsic automorphism group of \(a^2+b^2\) over \(\mathbb F_3\) consists only of signed permutations. The required \(\omega^{ab}\) phase has Schmidt rank three and cannot arise from product Weil operations. Opposite-orientation doubling admits isotropic diagonal gluing, but maximal gluing kills the discriminant sector instead of coupling and preserving it.

Hence the arithmetic construction now supplies exactly two faces. The third, mutual relationship must be an interface operator or mediator coupling. This is the strongest exact realization so far of “one carrier, two faces, three relationships,” while leaving the physical code/discriminant observable map open.

This completes an exact finite-to-integral-to-Jordan-to-boundary-action diagram for both branches, while leaving the Standard-Model origin of the interval mode and its parameters open.
